components.name: Calendar
components.summary: Date picker grid wrapping react-day-picker v9, themed entirely with semantic tokens (no external stylesheet). Supports single, multiple, and range selection; nav chevrons render through the injected icon set.

usage.description: Use Calendar to browse or choose dates in a month grid, especially when relative date position matters.

bestPractices.description: Use it when users need to compare weekdays, ranges, or nearby dates.
Provide selected, disabled, and today states when date choice is interactive.
Do not use Calendar when a compact DatePicker (with granularity="minute" for a time) would be faster.
Do not use it as the only way to enter a date. A grid is slow for a date far from today and unusable for someone who knows the value — always pair it with a text input.

props.name: mode
props.description: Selection behavior. Pair with the matching selected/onSelect shape (Date, Date[], or DateRange).

props.name: selected
props.description: The controlled selection. Shape follows mode.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fires when a day is chosen. The first argument's type follows mode.

props.name: defaultMonth
props.description: The month shown on first render (uncontrolled navigation).

props.name: month
props.description: Controlled displayed month; pair with onMonthChange.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: How many month grids to render side by side.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Days matching this are dimmed and non-selectable (e.g. { before: new Date() }).

props.name: showOutsideDays
props.description: Render leading/trailing days from adjacent months, dimmed.

props.name: bare
props.description: Drop the card frame (border, fill, padding) so the grid sits flush inside a surface that already has one, such as a Popover. DatePicker renders its Calendar this way.

props.name: motion
props.description: How much motion this component uses: `full` inherits the app's policy, `subtle` keeps feedback and drops the month slide, `off` stills it. It can only turn motion down — it never overrides a reader's reduce-motion setting.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the bordered card container that wraps the grid.

props.name: classNames
props.description: Per-part class overrides merged over the themed defaults. Themed slots: months, month, nav, button_previous, button_next, month_caption, caption_label, month_grid, weekdays, weekday, week, day, day_button, range_start, range_middle, range_end, selected, today, outside, disabled, hidden. Selection/state slots (selected/today/range_*/outside/disabled) style the day CELL; the inner day button is targeted via the [&>button] descendant.

props.name: components
props.description: Render overrides for RDP parts. Chevron is supplied by default and merged with yours.

motion.why: Inline, it arrives with its form; in a DatePicker the Popover carries the entrance. A grid that animated in by itself would put a second motion on the same opening.

Days ease their hover wash, and the month arrows are ghost Buttons on Button's own recipe. Across a seven-column grid the pointer crosses many cells at once, and an eased wash reads as a cursor travelling rather than a grid flashing.

Picking a day eases the primary fill onto it and off the previous one, so a click reads as the selection moving rather than two cells flipping. A range's band is painted on the cells, which carry the same recipe, so the band eases along with its endpoints as the range grows.
Days are resident data; nothing in the grid loads. Availability fetched per month belongs to the surface around the calendar.

Paging months slides the outgoing grid toward the edge it is leaving by and brings the new one in from the other, over a short travel with a fade (react-day-picker's `animate` mode on Sable keyframes in styles.css), so forward and back read as direction rather than a grid swapping in one frame. RDP adds a single class per part, which a recipe utility cannot be; mirrored in RTL. Expressive: Calendar turns `animate` on only at full motion, and an explicit `animate` prop still wins.

a11y: react-day-picker manages the roving-tabindex grid, arrow-key navigation, and ARIA roles/labels for the calendar.
Selected days use bg-primary/text-primary-foreground for AA contrast; today is marked with a dot under the number (not a ring, which is reserved for keyboard focus) rather than color alone.
Disabled and outside days are dimmed and removed from the tab order.
Nav chevrons resolve through the injected IconProvider; ensure chevron-left and chevron-right are registered in the icon set.

<Calendar mode="single" selected={date} onSelect={setDate} />

<Calendar mode="range" selected={range} onSelect={setRange} numberOfMonths={2} />

components.name: Card
components.summary: Raised surface container (rounded-lg) with optional Header/Title/Description/Action/Content/Footer parts. A density knob trades the part padding (comfortable vs compact) for denser section panels. `render` makes the whole card one link or button, with a hover, a full-card focus ring and motion.

usage.description: Use Card for a discrete thing with its own boundary, such as one product, one notification, one metric, or one setting cluster. Do not use Card as the default way to group every page section; whitespace, headings, Stack, Section, and dividers often create cleaner hierarchy.

bestPractices.description: Use Card when the item could be reordered, removed, selected, or compared independently.
Keep sibling cards on the same density and padding rhythm so lists and grids scan cleanly.
Use CardHeader, CardContent, and CardFooter when the card has a stable title/body/action structure.

Make the whole card one link (`render={<a href="…" />}`) when the card IS a single destination — a nav tile, a gallery item, a news teaser — and nothing inside it is interactive. All of the card text becomes the accessible name of the link, so keep it short: a title and a line.

Make a card a link when it holds its own buttons, menus, switches or links. Interactive content nested in a link is invalid HTML and announces twice; keep the card a plain surface and put the link on its title or in CardFooter instead.
Wrap every settings section or form group in a card; use headings, Stack, or the SettingsPage pattern instead.
Nest cards inside cards. Flatten the hierarchy or use dividers and spacing inside one card.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The raised or flat surface that creates the item boundary.

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: Optional title, description, and aligned action area for the card's identity.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: The body region. It should contain the information or controls that belong to this one item.

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Optional action or metadata row, usually lower-emphasis than the header.

props.name: variant
props.description: "default" raises with bg-card + border + soft shadow; "flat" is transparent, for a card inside a section that already frames it. A flat card made a link or button shows its shape only on hover (the muted fill), so over a photo with square bottom corners it reads as a cropped image at rest: give a linked media card the default variant.

props.name: density
props.description: Padding of the Header/Content/Footer parts: comfortable = p-6 (default), compact = p-4 for denser section panels (pair compact with the flat variant for a settings / form section panel). Threaded to the parts via the inherited --card-p custom property. Card sets --card-p via inline style, which beats a plain (non-!important) stylesheet override of the same property on the same element — use this prop rather than a className override; if an external override is unavoidable, it needs !important.

props.name: render
props.description: Replace the rendered element through the Base UI render prop — most often `render={<a href="/x" />}` (or a router Link) to make the whole card one link. When the rendered element is a link (a[href]) or a button, the card gains a hover state (stronger border and shadow; a muted fill when flat), a full-card focus-visible ring and motion-interactive easing. Any other element (article, li) stays a static surface. Children can answer the hover with `group-hover/card:`.

subcomponents.name: CardHeader
subcomponents.description: Top section holding CardTitle/CardDescription (and optionally CardAction). Padding follows the density knob.

subcomponents.name: CardTitle
subcomponents.description: The card's name (text-title-lg). A div by default; pass `render={<h2 />}` (or h3…) to make it a heading in the page outline, at the level the card's position calls for.

subcomponents.name: CardDescription
subcomponents.description: Muted supporting line under the title.

subcomponents.name: CardAction
subcomponents.description: Header-aligned top-right action slot (e.g. an overflow menu, switch, or close button). Place inside CardHeader, which becomes a 2-column grid when present and collapses to a single column otherwise. A ghost or link Button that ends the slot bleeds by its own padding at the end, so a "View all" label or a "⋯" glyph sits on the card's content edge; filled buttons keep their edge there.

subcomponents.name: CardContent
subcomponents.description: The body region. Padding follows the density knob on all sides — does not assume a preceding CardHeader, so it is safe to use standalone (e.g. no CardHeader in the card). When paired with CardHeader, the seam stays tight because CardHeader zeroes its own bottom padding. `flush` runs it edge to edge for a table: the Table insets its first and last columns by exactly the card padding, so it lines up with the header — never hand-set pl-6/pr-6 on columns.

subcomponents.name: CardList
subcomponents.description: Rows that run edge to edge in the card (Entity rows, most often), divided by hairlines. Insets each row to the card's own padding, so a list card lines up with every other card at any density — no hand-tuned px-* on the rows. Under a CardHeader it opens with a hairline and a gap; alone it fills the card.

subcomponents.name: CardFooter
subcomponents.description: Bottom row for actions/meta. Padding follows the density knob. `actions` marks it as the card's action row (buttons only): in a sheet (IosSheet, a bottom SheetContent) it becomes a full-width stack pinned to the bottom, primary on top; on a page nothing changes.

motion.why: A card is part of the layout it ships in; whatever stages that region owns the entrance. A card that fades in on its own delays reading the thing it holds.

Only when the card is rendered as a link or button. The border, shadow and ring ease in so the pointer reads as landing on one target, not as the grid flickering. No motion-press: a 0.97 settle on a surface this large reads as the layout lurching. A static card has no response, so it gets no transition.
A card has no states of its own to move between. Selection is CheckboxCard or RadioCard; disclosure is Collapsible or Accordion.
A card does not work on anything. Loading content inside it is a Skeleton's job.

a11y: Purely presentational by default; add headings/landmarks in content as needed.

Rendered as a link or button, the whole card is one target: its full text is the accessible name, and the focus ring wraps the whole card. Nothing interactive may sit inside it — nested links or buttons inside a link are invalid and unreachable for keyboard users in some browsers.

A Card is a container, not a landmark and not a heading. If its title is the only heading in the region, render it as a real heading element with a title tier — a visually-styled div gives screen-reader heading navigation nothing to find.

components.name: CaretMenu
components.summary: Suggestions at the caret of a text field, for @mentions and /slash commands. `useCaretTrigger` watches a Textarea, Input or ChatComposer (through `fieldRef`) for a trigger character and reports the query; CaretMenu draws the list beside the trigger and drives it from the field's keys, so focus never leaves the field. The value stays plain text: a mention is inserted as `@Sam Rivera`, a command runs and clears its `/query`.

usage.description: Use CaretMenu with `useCaretTrigger` when typing a character in running text should offer choices: `@` for people, `/` for commands, `#` for channels, `:` for emoji. The app owns the items (filter or fetch them from `trigger.match.query`) and what choosing one does; Sable owns detecting the trigger, placing the list at the caret, the keys and the accessibility. Use Combobox when the whole field is a search for one value, and CommandMenu for a global palette.

bestPractices.description: Attach the hook's `fieldRef` to the field: `ref` on Textarea or Input, `fieldRef` on ChatComposer. On ChatComposer, Enter picks the highlighted suggestion instead of sending, because CaretMenu takes the Enter first.
Insert a mention with a trailing space, `trigger.replace(`@${person.name} `)`, so the reader keeps typing; run a slash command and then `trigger.replace("")` to clear `/query` from the field.
For `@` names with spaces set `allowSpaces: true` on that trigger; for `/` commands set `atStart: true` so `and/or` mid-sentence stays text.

Fetch remote suggestions from `trigger.match?.query` yourself, debounced, and pass `status` while loading or when nothing matches ("Searching…", "No one matches"). The status row is also what the list announces.

Do not expect chips inside the field. A textarea holds text, so a mention is text. Rendering tokens in the field needs a rich-text editor, which Sable does not own (`sable docs extending-a-component`).
Do not move focus into the list or wrap the field in a Popover. Focus stays in the field; the list is pointed at with aria-activedescendant.

anatomy.name: useCaretTrigger
anatomy.description: The hook on the field: trigger detection, the query, the caret anchor, replace() and dismiss().

anatomy.name: CaretMenu
anatomy.description: The list at the caret, its keys, and its announcements.

anatomy.name: CaretMenuItem
anatomy.description: One suggestion row, with optional icon and description.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The result of `useCaretTrigger({ triggers })`, whose `fieldRef` is attached to the field. Each trigger is `{ char, atStart?, allowSpaces?, maxQueryLength? }`; the result carries `match` (`{ trigger, query, start, end }` or null), `replace(text)`, `dismiss()` and `getAnchorRect()`.

props.name: label
props.description: The list's accessible name, e.g. "People" or "Commands".

props.name: status
props.description: A row under the items for what the list is doing: loading, nothing found, an error. Announced politely in place of the suggestion count. With no items and no status the list stays shut.

props.name: children
props.description: CaretMenuItems, already filtered for the query.

props.name: className
props.description: Layout classes for the popup, such as a width.

subcomponents.name: CaretMenuItem
subcomponents.type: div props + onSelect: () => void + disabled?: boolean + icon?: ReactNode + description?: ReactNode
subcomponents.description: One suggestion, styled as a Menu row. `onSelect` runs on Enter, Tab or click; `icon` and `description` work as on MenuItem. A disabled row shows but the arrow keys skip it.

motion.why: Scales in from the caret's side, so the list reads as coming from the character just typed. It leaves instantly: it answers a keystroke and should be gone by the next one.

a11y: Focus stays in the field. The field carries aria-autocomplete="list", aria-controls (the listbox) and aria-activedescendant (the highlighted option), so a screen reader follows the arrow keys without focus moving.

An <input> becomes role="combobox" with aria-expanded. A <textarea> keeps its textbox role (combobox would drop multiline), and since a textbox cannot carry aria-expanded, opening is announced through a polite status, mounted from the start: "3 suggestions", or the `status` text.
↑/↓ move the highlight and wrap; Enter or Tab choose it; Escape closes the list without reaching an enclosing Dialog or Sheet. Shift+Enter is left alone, so a line break still breaks the line.
Rows keep focus in the field on pointer down, so a click does not blur it and close the list first.
Triggers follow a word boundary (`ana@example.com` and `and/or` stay text), wait for IME composition to end, and stay closed after Escape until the caret leaves that trigger.

components.name: Carousel
components.summary: Generic, accessible, zero-dependency slide carousel. Transform track with measured slide pitch — multiple slides per view, infinite loop (cloned ends), pointer drag-to-swipe with snap, autoplay (with a pause control + hover/focus/reduced-motion pausing), arrows, dots, counter, and keyboard. Motion is token-driven.

usage.description: Use Carousel for a curated, finite sequence of media or cards that benefits from horizontal browsing.

bestPractices.description: Use obvious previous and next controls and make the current position understandable.
Keep slide content independent so users do not need every slide to complete a task.
Do not hide critical information or primary conversion actions only inside later slides.
Do not autoplay without a visible pause control. Motion that cannot be stopped fails WCAG 2.2.2 and makes the surrounding text hard to read.

props.name: children
props.description: Each top-level child becomes one slide.

props.name: slidesToShow
props.type: number | { base?: number; sm?: number; md?: number; lg?: number; xl?: number }
props.description: Slides visible per view. A number, or a mobile-first breakpoint set keyed to Tailwind's default min-widths (sm 640, md 768, lg 1024, xl 1280px); a missing key inherits from the next smaller defined one, and base (default 1) is also the server-render value. Resolved with matchMedia, so no hand-rolled resize hook is needed.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between slides (any CSS length). Use the spacing scale — e.g. "calc(var(--spacing) * 4)" — so density moves it.

props.name: loop
props.description: Infinite loop via cloned ends (needs count > slidesToShow).

props.name: autoplay
props.description: Auto-advance interval in ms (0 = off). Pauses on hover/focus/reduced-motion and exposes a play/pause control.

props.name: arrows
props.description: Prev/next arrow buttons.

props.name: dots
props.description: Pagination dots.

props.name: counter
props.description: An N / M slide counter.

props.name: draggable
props.description: Pointer drag-to-swipe.

props.name: index
props.description: Controlled active index.

props.name: defaultIndex
props.description: Initial index (uncontrolled).

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Notified when the active index changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the carousel region.

props.name: slideClassName
props.description: Class for each slide wrapper (e.g. an aspect ratio).

props.name: arrowClassName
props.description: Class for both prev/next arrow buttons. Merged through cn(), so a radius or shadow utility replaces the default rounded-full shadow-md rather than stacking with it.

props.name: motion
props.description: How much motion this component uses: `full` (default) inherits the app's policy, `subtle` keeps feedback and drops the glide, `off` stills it. It can only turn motion down — it never overrides a reader's reduce-motion setting. Under subtle the slides still travel and the active dot snaps; off also cuts between slides and pauses autoplay.

motion.why: A carousel arrives with its section. Its content already moves on every advance; an entrance on top would make the first view feel like an advance nobody asked for.
The dot's 24px hit area eases its focus ring and the dot brightens under the pointer, which is how a 6px mark tells you it is a button.

The slide track's translate is set inline from the measured slide pitch, on --motion-duration-slow and the emphasized easing, and switched off during a drag so the track follows the finger. A recipe cannot carry a measured, drag-interrupted offset. Essential: it is the answer to "next", so it plays under subtle.

The active dot stretches to a bar while the one it left shrinks, on one timeline, so the row keeps its length and the mark reads as travelling with the slide. It used to change width unanimated and jumped while the slides beside it glided. Expressive: motion="subtle" snaps it.
Autoplay's progress is the slides themselves advancing and the play/pause control; a separate timer animation would put a second clock beside the first.

a11y: Region carries aria-roledescription='carousel'; each slide is a group with aria-roledescription='slide' and an 'N of M' label; clones are aria-hidden.
Arrows and dots are real buttons (dots set aria-current); Left/Right arrow keys navigate when the viewport is focused.
A polite live region announces the active slide; it goes silent while auto-rotating (APG).
Autoplay exposes a pause/play control and pauses on hover, focus, and under prefers-reduced-motion (which also makes transitions instant).

examples.label: Looping media
examples.code: {images.map((s) => )}

examples.label: Multiple per view
examples.code: <Carousel slidesToShow={3} gap="calc(var(--spacing) * 4)">{cards}</Carousel>

examples.label: Responsive per view
examples.code: <Carousel slidesToShow={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }} gap="calc(var(--spacing) * 6)" label="Templates">{cards}</Carousel>

examples.label: Autoplay
examples.code: <Carousel loop autoplay={4000} counter>{slides}</Carousel>

examples.label: Subtle motion
examples.code: <Carousel loop motion="subtle" label="Gallery">{slides}</Carousel>

components.name: ChatComposer
components.summary: The input half of a conversation: one surface holding attachments, an auto-growing field, and its controls. Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line (sendOn="mod-enter" swaps them for long-form replies; on touch, Return always breaks the line), and send becomes stop while a reply streams. allowEmpty sends attachments without text.

usage.description: Pairs with MessageScroller to make a working chat. A single surface rather than an input with buttons parked beside it: attachments above, text in the middle, affordances along the bottom. Works controlled or uncontrolled — uncontrolled is the default because it is what the common case wants, and what lets a hook-free page shell ship a composer that actually types.

bestPractices.description: Wiring it to a streaming source? `sable docs building-a-chat` maps a turn lifecycle (submitted, streaming, done, stopped, error) onto `busy`, `onStop` and `disabled`, and says where each failure goes.
Pass `busy` while a reply streams, and `onStop` alongside it. Interrupting a long generation is the most common thing a reader wants during one, and the control belongs where their cursor already is.
Leave it uncontrolled unless you need the text elsewhere — a slash-command menu, a draft you persist. Uncontrolled clears itself on send; controlled does not.
Render pending uploads as `<Attachment>` chips in `attachments`, so the file and the message it belongs to stay in one box.

Pass `allowEmpty={files.length > 0}` when a file can go without a caption. Send enables on the attachment alone and `onSend` receives `""`. Tie it to the pending files: a constant `allowEmpty` leaves send enabled with nothing to send.
Put model pickers and tool toggles in `leading`, beside the attach button — they are composer state, not message content, and belong on the chrome row rather than in the field.
Do not clear a controlled composer for the user on send. Only the caller knows whether the send succeeded, and clearing on their behalf loses the message when it did not.

Do not add your own Enter-to-send handler on top. The built-in one already guards against firing mid-IME-composition, and on a touch device lets Return break the line (a soft keyboard has no Shift+Return), which are the lines hand-rolled chat inputs miss.

Building a docked agent panel inside a tool? Wrap the whole conversation — scroller, messages and composer — in `<Density value="compact">`. The entire set follows the workspace register from there: prose drops a tier, the rhythm tightens, and the controls come off the compact ladder. Do not hand-size it at the call site.

Do not use it as a general multi-line input inside a larger form. That is `Textarea`. A standalone reply box that sends multi-paragraph messages (email, support replies) is this one with sendOn="mod-enter".

Do not override the field's type utility to make it match your transcript. The field and `Bubble` both read the same tier already, which is what stops a message changing size the moment it is sent — overriding one breaks that pairing.
Do not remove the height cap to let the field grow without limit. A pasted essay would push the conversation off the screen; past the cap it scrolls.

anatomy.name: Attachments
anatomy.description: Pending files as chips, above the field, inside the same surface.

anatomy.name: Field
anatomy.description: An auto-growing Textarea, stripped of its own border and ring — the surface carries both — capped before it eats the transcript.

anatomy.name: Controls
anatomy.description: Attach and any `leading` controls on the left; `actions` and the send/stop button on the right.

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Helper text or a character counter below the controls.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value. Omit for an uncontrolled composer that owns its own text.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Notified on every keystroke. Required when `value` is supplied.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Called with the trimmed message. An uncontrolled composer clears itself afterwards; a controlled one is the caller's to clear. With `allowEmpty` the message can be `""`.

props.name: allowEmpty
props.description: Let the reader send with no text, because the app has something else to send (pending attachments). Pass it only while that is true, `allowEmpty={files.length > 0}`; `onSend` then receives `""`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for the field.

props.name: sendOn
props.description: Which key sends. enter for chat (Shift+Enter breaks the line). mod-enter for long-form replies such as an email or a support answer: Enter breaks the line and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends, so a paragraph break never mails a draft. Say so in footer ("Cmd+Enter to send"). On a touch device (pointer: coarse) enter behaves as mod-enter: a soft keyboard has no Shift+Return, so Return breaks the line and the send button sends.

props.name: busy
props.description: A reply is streaming. Disables send, and swaps it for a stop control when `onStop` is supplied.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Interrupt the in-flight reply. Supplying it turns send into stop while busy.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Block sending entirely — over a limit, disconnected, read-only thread. Distinct from `busy`, which is temporary and offers a way out (stop).

props.name: invalid
props.description: Mark the current text invalid. Colours the surface border and sets `aria-invalid` on the field.

props.name: attachments
props.description: Attachment chips, shown above the field.

props.name: leading
props.description: Controls on the left of the footer row — model picker, tool toggles.

props.name: actions
props.description: Extra controls left of the send button.

props.name: onAttach
props.description: Attach handler. Supplying it renders the built-in attach button.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the field.

props.name: sendLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the send button.

props.name: stopLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the stop button.

props.name: footer
props.description: Helper text or counter below the controls. For a keyboard hint pass a function: it receives the send key in effect (touch turns `enter` into `mod-enter`), and returning null removes the row, e.g. `footer={({ sendOn }) => sendOn === "enter" ? "Enter to send" : null}`.

props.name: fieldRef
props.description: Ref to the underlying textarea — for focusing after a send, or on mount, and the extension point for anything that listens to the field. Pass `useCaretTrigger`'s `fieldRef` here for mentions and slash commands (CaretMenu). An Enter another listener already handled (`preventDefault()`) does not send.

props.name: motion
props.description: How much motion this component uses: `full` (default) inherits the app's policy, `subtle` keeps feedback and drops the flourish, `off` stills it. It can only turn motion down — it never overrides a reader's reduce-motion setting. Under `subtle` the field snaps to its new height and the send/stop glyphs swap without the morph.

props.name: ...form props
props.description: Spread onto the form element. Use `onSend` rather than `onSubmit`.

motion.why: The composer is the fixed foot of a thread, there before anything else is. An entrance would only delay the first keystroke.
The surface's focus ring and invalid border ease in, so focusing the field reads as the whole box waking up rather than a frame flicker.

As a line breaks or a paste lands, the field eases to its new height (up to its cap) instead of jumping, so the transcript above is visibly pushed rather than teleported. `field-sizing` alone cannot ease — its height stays `auto` — so a small hook measures and pins a pixel height. Expressive and short (`fast`): the text itself lands at once, and `subtle` snaps the box.

Send turning into stop is the moment a reply starts, and stop turning back is the moment it is over. One button changes role in place — the fill eases, the arrow collapses into the square — so it reads as the same control changing what it does, not a different button appearing under the cursor.
Busy with no stop handler, Button's own loading Spinner replaces the arrow, so a send in flight is not mistaken for a disabled one.

a11y: A real `<form>`, so the send button is a submit button and the whole thing behaves as one control to assistive tech and to password managers alike.
Enter never submits while an IME composition is open (`isComposing`), so a CJK reader confirming a candidate word does not mail a fragment of their first sentence.
The focus ring is drawn on the surface via `focus-within`, not on the textarea, so the visible focus indicator matches the box a sighted user perceives as the input.
Send is disabled — not merely styled down — until there is non-whitespace to send (or `allowEmpty` says an attachment is enough), so the affordance and the behaviour agree for keyboard users.
On a touch device Return breaks the line and the send button sends; `aria-keyshortcuts` reports the shortcut actually in effect (⌘/Ctrl+Enter there, Enter on desktop).
Icon-only attach, send and stop buttons all carry accessible labels, each overridable for localisation.

examples.label: Uncontrolled — the common case
examples.code: <ChatComposer onSend={(text) => send(text)} onAttach={pickFile} />

examples.label: Streaming, with a stop control
examples.code: <ChatComposer onSend={send} busy={isStreaming} onStop={stop} placeholder="Ask a follow-up…" />

examples.label: Controlled, with pending attachments
examples.code:
<ChatComposer
	value={draft}
	onValueChange={setDraft}
	onSend={(text) => { post(text, files); setDraft("") }}
	onAttach={pickFile}
	attachments={files.map((f) => (<Attachment key={f.id} variant="media" name={f.name} thumbnail={f.url} actions={<Button variant="floating" size="icon-xs" aria-label="Remove" onClick={() => drop(f.id)}><Icon name="xmark" /></Button>} />))}
	footer={`${draft.length} / 4000`}
	invalid={draft.length > 4000}
/>
examples.imports: import { Attachment, Button, ChatComposer, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: Attachments sent without text
examples.code:
<ChatComposer
	onSend={(text) => post(text, files)}
	allowEmpty={files.length > 0}
	onAttach={pickFile}
	attachments={files.map((f) => <Attachment key={f.id} name={f.name} meta={f.size} />)}
/>

examples.label: A working chat, end to end
examples.code: {messages.map((m) => ({m.body}))} {streaming ? Thinking… : null}
examples.imports: import { Bubble, ChatComposer, Marker, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: Square toggle (18px at rest, on the spacing scale) over Base UI's Checkbox. Checked/indeterminate/disabled states; controlled or uncontrolled; form-ready via the hidden native input.

usage.description: Use Checkbox for independent boolean choices or for selecting multiple options in a set.

bestPractices.description: Use Checkbox when each option can be toggled independently.
Attach a visible label that explains the consequence of checking the control.
Do not use Checkbox for mutually exclusive choices; use Radio or Select instead.
Do not use it without a label or an aria-label. An 18px square with no accessible name is announced as just "checkbox", which tells a screen-reader user nothing about what they are agreeing to.

Do not phrase the label as a negative, such as "Don't send read receipts". Paired with an unchecked box it becomes a double negative the reader has to solve before they can answer. Label the state being turned on.

props.name: checked
props.description: Controlled checked state. Pair with onCheckedChange. Omit for uncontrolled.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Initial checked state for an uncontrolled checkbox.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Fires when the checkbox is ticked or unticked. Note: Base UI passes a second eventDetails arg — not the common (checked) => void, so a single-arg handler must widen its signature.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Mixed state (neither checked nor unchecked). Renders a dash instead of the check. For a "select all" box inside a CheckboxGroup, use `parent` instead and the group sets this for you.

props.name: parent
props.description: Makes this the "select all" box of a CheckboxGroup that has `allValues`. It checks or clears every child, and shows the dash when only some are checked. Only works inside a CheckboxGroup.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Ignores user interaction and dims the control.

props.name: name
props.description: Field name for the hidden input on form submit.

props.name: value
props.description: Value submitted with the form when checked. Inside a group-owned CheckboxGroup, it is the name the group's value array uses for this checkbox.

props.name: render
props.description: Compose the root with another element through the Base UI render prop.

props.name: motion
props.description: How much motion this component uses: `full` (default) inherits the app's policy, `subtle` keeps feedback and drops the flourish, `off` stills it. It can only turn motion down — it never overrides a reader's reduce-motion setting. Under `subtle` the tick fades in instead of drawing itself.

motion.why: It arrives with the form it belongs to. Animating each box in turns a settings list into a title sequence.
The box fills with the primary colour as it is checked; easing the fill keeps the mark and the box changing as one event rather than two frames apart.

The check draws itself in from its leading stroke, so checking reads as the box being ticked rather than a glyph appearing. The dash wipes the same way. Unchecking only fades, so clearing a list is quick; under `subtle` checking fades too.
A checkbox commits instantly. A slow write belongs to the surrounding form's pending state, not the control.

a11y: Base UI renders a hidden native <input type=checkbox> for keyboard, focus, and form semantics.
Space toggles; focus-visible draws a 2px ring in the --ring token.
indeterminate sets aria-checked=mixed automatically; a `parent` checkbox in a CheckboxGroup gets aria-checked=mixed and aria-controls for its children from the group.
Label it with Field orientation="horizontal": it wires the label's htmlFor to the checkbox, so the label text joins the click target, and adds the description and error plumbing.

examples.label: Default
examples.code: <Checkbox defaultChecked />

examples.label: Controlled
examples.code: <Checkbox checked={value} onCheckedChange={setValue} />

examples.label: Indeterminate
examples.code: <Checkbox indeterminate />

examples.label: Select all in a group
examples.code: <CheckboxGroup allValues={["email", "sms"]} defaultValue={["email"]} className="gap-3"><Field label="All channels" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox parent /></Field><Field label="Email" orientation="horizontal" className="ps-7"><Checkbox value="email" /></Field><Field label="SMS" orientation="horizontal" className="ps-7"><Checkbox value="sms" /></Field></CheckboxGroup>

examples.label: With label
examples.code: <Field label="Remember me" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox /></Field>

components.name: CheckboxCard
components.summary: A multi-select selection card — a card-sized Base UI Checkbox with a checkbox box, title, and optional description. The checkbox twin of RadioCard (same tone table). CheckboxGroup lays a column out and can own the selection: give each card a `value` and the group holds the checked values as an array, with an optional parent "select all" Checkbox.

usage.description: Use CheckboxCard when an option needs more visual weight, supporting text, or iconography than a plain checkbox row.

bestPractices.description: Use it for a small number of options where details help users compare choices.
Keep the checked state visible across the full card, not only inside the indicator.
Let CheckboxGroup own the selection when the cards answer one question: give each card a `value` and read one array from `onValueChange` instead of wiring a toggle per card.
Use a plain Checkbox with `parent` for "select all", and list every child value in the group's `allValues`. The group works out its checked and mixed states.
Do not use CheckboxCard for long lists; use Checkbox rows or a Combobox with `multiple` instead.
Do not put a link or a button inside the card. The whole card is the checkbox's label, so a nested interactive element is either unreachable or steals the click that should toggle it.

anatomy.name: CheckboxCard
anatomy.description: One card-shaped checkbox option.

anatomy.name: CheckboxGroup
anatomy.description: A grouped set of related checkbox cards. Optionally owns the selected values and a parent "select all" checkbox.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Fires with the next checked state (Base UI passes eventDetails second). Pair with `checked` for a controlled card; omit both to let it manage its own state.

props.name: title
props.description: The card's primary label (text-title-sm).

props.name: description
props.description: Optional supporting copy beneath the title (text-body-sm, muted).

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional glyph (a solid <Icon>) in the tone colour. Its presence switches to the two-dimensional card RadioCard uses — icon top-left, checkbox top-right, copy below — so the two cards match in one form.

props.name: tone
props.description: Semantic colour the checked state carries across the border, checkbox box, and icon.

props.name: value
props.description: Names the card inside a group-owned CheckboxGroup: the card is checked when the group's value array includes it. Also the value submitted with a form. Inside a CheckboxGroup, `name` stands in for `value` when `value` is omitted.

props.name: checked / onCheckedChange / defaultChecked / disabled
props.description: Standard checkbox state. Without a group-owned value, each card is independent — drive checked/onCheckedChange per item for multi-select.

props.name: motion
props.description: How much motion this component uses: `full` (default) inherits the app's policy, `subtle` keeps feedback and drops the flourish, `off` stills it. It can only turn motion down — it never overrides a reader's reduce-motion setting. Under `subtle` the tick fades in instead of drawing itself.

subcomponents.name: CheckboxGroup
subcomponents.type: { className?: string; children: ReactNode; value?: string[]; defaultValue?: string[]; onValueChange?: (value: string[]) => void; allValues?: string[]; disabled?: boolean }
subcomponents.description: Column wrapper (role=group) over Base UI's CheckboxGroup. With no group props it is layout only and each card stays independent. Pass value/defaultValue/onValueChange (string[]) and give each child a `value` to let the group own the selection — works for CheckboxCard and plain Checkbox children alike. Add allValues plus a `<Checkbox parent />` for a select-all box that turns mixed when only some are checked. `disabled` disables every child. onValueChange gets (value, eventDetails). Override the grid via className for multi-column layouts.

motion.why: It arrives with the form it belongs to. Animating each box in turns a settings list into a title sequence.
The box fills with the primary colour as it is checked; easing the fill keeps the mark and the box changing as one event rather than two frames apart.

The check draws itself in from its leading stroke, so checking reads as the box being ticked rather than a glyph appearing. The dash wipes the same way. Unchecking only fades, so clearing a list is quick; under `subtle` checking fades too.
A checkbox commits instantly. A slow write belongs to the surrounding form's pending state, not the control.

a11y: Base UI provides the checkbox role, aria-checked, hidden native input, keyboard toggle, and data-[checked]/data-disabled state.
The whole card is the hit target; focus draws a 2px outline outside the card (not a ring, so the checked tone ring survives focus); Space toggles the focused card.
Selection never relies on colour alone — the filled checkbox box + check mark and the card border all shift.
A parent select-all Checkbox gets aria-checked=mixed and aria-controls pointing at its children from Base UI; give it a visible label.

examples.label: Group-owned selection
examples.code: <CheckboxGroup value={selected} onValueChange={setSelected}>{REASONS.map((r) => (<CheckboxCard key={r} value={r} title={r} />))}</CheckboxGroup>

examples.label: Select all
examples.code: <CheckboxGroup allValues={REASONS} value={selected} onValueChange={setSelected}><Field label="All reasons" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox parent /></Field>{REASONS.map((r) => (<CheckboxCard key={r} value={r} title={r} />))}</CheckboxGroup>
examples.imports: import { Checkbox, CheckboxCard, CheckboxGroup, Field } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: A single independent card
examples.code: <CheckboxCard title="Email me a receipt" description="Sent when the payment settles" checked={receipt} onCheckedChange={setReceipt} />

examples.label: Toned with description
examples.code: <CheckboxCard tone="1" title="Reports" description="Weekly usage reports by email" defaultChecked />

components.name: Code
components.summary: Inline code. A styled `<code>` for code spans, keys, and identifiers inside running text — soft muted fill, monospace.

usage.description: Use Code for short inline identifiers, commands, tokens, props, and file names inside prose.

bestPractices.description: Use it for brief technical literals that need to stand apart from body copy.
Keep inline code short enough that it does not dominate the paragraph.
Do not use Code for multiline snippets; use CodeBlock instead.
Do not put a value the reader needs to copy inside it. Code has no copy affordance, so they will select it by hand and catch the surrounding punctuation; use CodeBlock with a prompt.

props.name: ...props
props.description: All native `<code>` attributes (children, className, ref, …) pass through.

a11y: Renders a semantic `<code>` element so assistive tech announces it as code.

A `<code>` element is not announced distinctly by most screen readers — a code span in running prose is read as ordinary text. Where the exactness matters (a command to type verbatim, a case-sensitive identifier), say so in the sentence rather than relying on the styling to carry it.

examples.label: Inline
examples.code: Run pnpm dev to start the server.

examples.label: Code vs CodeBlock

components.name: CodeBlock
components.summary: Multi-line code surface. Optional header bar carries a filename and a copy affordance; the body is a horizontally scrollable monospace pre. Syntax highlighting is opt-in: pass a highlighter per block or once via CodeHighlightProvider (the package ships none).

usage.description: Use CodeBlock for multiline code samples that users may read, inspect, or copy.

anatomy.name: CodeBlock
anatomy.description: The surface: optional filename header, copy affordance, scrollable pre.

anatomy.name: CodeHighlightProvider
anatomy.description: Optional app-level wrapper that supplies one highlighter to every CodeBlock inside it.

bestPractices.description: Give the snippet a filename, or a sentence of surrounding copy, when it helps readers and agents place it.
Keep examples complete enough to teach the intended pattern.

Wire highlighting once with CodeHighlightProvider and map token colors to semantic tone tokens (keywords → tone-1, strings → success, comments → muted-foreground), so code follows the theme instead of a fixed palette.
Do not put short inline identifiers in a CodeBlock; use Code for those.
Do not paste code with the indentation the surrounding file had. A block indented to sit inside your JSX shows the reader leading whitespace that is not part of the example.

props.name: code
props.description: The code to display. Always what the copy button copies, whatever the highlighter renders.

props.name: filename
props.description: Optional filename shown in the header bar.

props.name: showCopy
props.description: Show the copy affordance — in the header bar with a filename, floating in the corner without one.

props.name: highlight
props.description: Highlighter for this block; overrides CodeHighlightProvider. false renders plain text inside a provider.

props.name: prompt
props.description: A shell prompt ("$", ">"). Makes it a one-line command: the prompt is dimmed and unselectable, the line truncates, and copy takes only code.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Wrap long lines instead of scrolling them. For prose in a code face (a prompt to paste into an agent, a log line); code keeps scrolling, since wrapping breaks its indentation.

subcomponents.name: CodeHighlightProvider
subcomponents.description: Supplies one highlighter to every CodeBlock beneath it, so an app wires highlighting once. Map the highlighter's token colors to Sable tone tokens so code follows the theme.

motion.why: Code is reading content and arrives with the page or message it belongs to. An entrance of its own would delay the text someone came to copy.
The copy button is a quiet ghost icon in the corner of a block. Its hover fill is what tells the pointer it is a control and not decoration.
The copy mark turning into a check is the only proof the clipboard took the text. Snapped between frames it was easy to miss at the edge of a block; the swap reads as one mark being replaced.
Copying is instant. There is no in-between worth showing, and a spinner for a clipboard write would read as a slow one.

a11y: Code renders inside a <pre><code> for correct semantics and screen-reader handling.
Copy is the ghost icon Button with `useCopy`, which guards clipboard access for SSR safety.
A successful copy is announced as "Copied" through a polite role=status region that is always mounted; the button keeps its label, which names what it does. Both glyphs are aria-hidden.

examples.label: With filename + copy
examples.code: <CodeBlock filename="cn.ts" code={"import { clsx } from \"clsx\"\nexport const cn = clsx"} />

examples.label: With a highlighter for the whole app
examples.code: <CodeHighlightProvider highlight={(code) => <span dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: highlightToHtml(code) }} />}><CodeBlock code={"const a = 1"} /></CodeHighlightProvider>

examples.label: No header
examples.code: <CodeBlock showCopy={false} code={"type Size = \"sm\" | \"md\"\nconst size: Size = \"md\""} />

components.name: Collapsible
components.summary: Show/hide a panel of content over Base UI Collapsible — open/close state, ARIA expanded wiring, and the animated height transition. The minimal primitive behind Accordion: a trigger that toggles an overflow-clipped panel.

usage.description: Use Collapsible for a single piece of optional content that can expand in place.

bestPractices.description: Use it for local detail, advanced settings, or secondary context.
Make the trigger label describe the hidden content, not the mechanism.
Do not use Collapsible for multi-section navigation; use Accordion or Tabs instead.
Do not animate it by transitioning height from auto. Use the motion-disclosure recipe, which transitions to the measured panel height — `auto` does not animate and the panel will snap.

anatomy.name: CollapsibleTrigger
anatomy.description: The control that toggles the panel.

anatomy.name: CollapsiblePanel
anatomy.description: The content that expands or collapses.

anatomy.name: CollapsibleIndicator
anatomy.description: A visual affordance for open or closed state.

props.name: Collapsible (Root)
props.type: Base UI Collapsible.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, disabled)
props.description: Groups the trigger and panel and owns open state. Uncontrolled by default; pass `open` + `onOpenChange` to control it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the panel starts open in the uncontrolled case.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the trigger and prevents toggling.

subcomponents.name: CollapsibleTrigger
subcomponents.description: The button that toggles the panel. Compose with render={<Button variant="ghost" … />}.

subcomponents.name: CollapsiblePanel
subcomponents.type: Base UI Collapsible.Panel props + className (keepMounted, hiddenUntilFound)
subcomponents.description: The collapsible contents. Overflow-hidden; animates height via the --collapsible-panel-height var Base UI sets.

subcomponents.name: CollapsibleIndicator
subcomponents.description: Auto-rotating disclosure chevron. Place it anywhere inside the trigger content; it reads the trigger's open state itself, no class to add. direction="down" (default) flips 180° on open; direction="end" points to the inline end while closed and turns down on open — the caret for a grouped list's section header or a tree row. Use it instead of rotating your own chevron with CSS, which snaps with no transition.

motion.why: A collapsible is part of the page it sits in, present from first paint. Its trigger is what the reader notices, not an entrance.
The trigger is whatever the consumer renders (usually a Button), and that control brings its own response. Adding one here would double it.
The height change ties the content that appears to the trigger that was pressed; snapped open, everything below jumps with nothing linking cause to effect.
The chevron turns with the panel rather than flipping in one frame: motion-interactive lists `rotate`, the property rotate-180 and rotate-0 write.
Nothing here is indeterminate; content that loads on open should put its own loader inside the panel.

a11y: Base UI wires aria-expanded on the trigger and aria-controls/id between trigger and panel.
Trigger is a real <button>; toggles on click and Enter/Space.
Animate open/close via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style]; data-[panel-open] marks the open state.
Set hiddenUntilFound on the panel to let in-page browser search expand it.

components.name: ColorField
components.summary: A colour swatch that opens a themed picker — saturation/value area, hue and alpha sliders, hex entry, presets, and transparent as a value rather than a separate toggle.

usage.description: Use ColorField wherever a colour is a property: a canvas background, an effect parameter, a stroke or fill. It is sized to the control ladder so it lines up inside a PropertyRow or PropertyPair. Deliberately not <input type="color">, which opens the OS dialog — that ignores the theme entirely, cannot show a transparency checkerboard, has no alpha channel, hosts no eyedropper or presets, and renders at whatever size the platform picks, so it never aligns in a property grid.

bestPractices.description: Use allowTransparent when "no colour" is a real value. It appears inside the picker as a value; a transparent switch sitting beside a colour control reads as two properties when it is one.
Pass swatches when a surface has a house palette. Presets are how most colour choices actually get made, and they cost one row.
Decide whether your persistence layer accepts 8-digit hex before enabling allowAlpha. The value format is the contract — see the tokens note.
Put a separate opacity slider next to a ColorField that already has allowAlpha. Two controls writing one channel is how they drift out of sync.

Re-derive hue from the committed value on every render. Grey has no hue, so dragging saturation to zero would snap the hue slider to red with no way back — ColorField keeps hue in its own state for exactly this reason.

Hand-roll a transparency checkerboard. Use the `checkerboard` utility with `--checkerboard-size` (~16px for an artboard, ~8px for a 24px swatch); two hand-rolled copies had already drifted before it existed. Its colours come from --panel / --panel-raised, so it is correct in both modes. It is deliberately not named bg-checkerboard: a custom bg-* utility lands in tailwind-merge's background group and silently evicts, or is evicted by, a real bg-* colour class.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: A swatch at --control-xs with a hairline ring, on a checkerboard so a translucent or transparent value reads as such.

anatomy.name: Picker
anatomy.description: Saturation/value area over the current hue, a hue slider, an alpha slider when allowAlpha, and a hex field.

anatomy.name: Presets
anatomy.description: An optional swatch row, and the Transparent entry when allowTransparent.

props.name: value
props.description: The current value: "transparent", "#rrggbb", or "#rrggbbaa".

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the new value on every commit, including mid-drag.

props.name: allowTransparent
props.description: Offers "transparent" as a value inside the picker. Colour → transparent → colour restores the colour you had.

props.name: allowAlpha
props.description: Enables the alpha slider, and therefore 8-digit hex output. Off by default because it widens the value format.

props.name: swatches
props.description: Optional preset row.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the trigger; the current value is appended to it.

motion.why: The picker grows out of the swatch it edits (PopoverContent's recipe, its origin on the anchor). In a property panel with a column of swatches, that origin is what tells you which colour you are now editing.
Preset swatches lift slightly under the pointer. They are 20px chips of colour with no label, and the eased lift is what tells you which one a click will take.

The saturation, hue and alpha handles follow the pointer exactly. A handle that trailed the drag would misreport the colour under the cursor, and a swatch or a typed hex moving them is the value changing, which the field should show at once.
Picking is synchronous. The EyeDropper is the browser's own modal, with its own feedback.

a11y: The trigger's accessible name includes the current value, so a screen reader announces the colour rather than just "button" — the swatch itself conveys nothing without sight.
The Transparent entry is a toggle with aria-pressed, because it is a state of the value and not a navigation action.

The hex field is the keyboard path to any colour. The saturation/value area and the sliders are pointer-driven and are NOT keyboard operable — a known gap, and the reason the hex field is never hidden.
The eyedropper is only rendered where the EyeDropper API exists (Chromium), rather than shown and broken elsewhere.

examples.label: Canvas background
examples.code:
<PropertyRow label="Background">
  <ColorField value={background} onValueChange={setBackground} allowTransparent />
</PropertyRow>

examples.label: With alpha and a palette
examples.code:
<ColorField
  value={tint}
  onValueChange={setTint}
  allowAlpha
  swatches={["#f43f5e", "#facc15", "#22c55e", "#3b82f6", "#a855f7"]}
  label="Tint"
/>

components.name: Combobox
components.summary: Autocomplete over Base UI Combobox — type-to-filter, roving focus, ARIA combobox/listbox wiring, collision-aware positioning, Esc/outside dismissal. A search input (with chevron trigger) plus a portal-rendered popup of filterable items.

usage.description: Use Combobox when users choose from a list that benefits from typing, filtering, or autocomplete — one value, or several with `multiple` and ComboboxChips (tags, collaborators, categories). Use Select for short finite sets, a Checkbox group when every choice should stay visible, and CommandMenu for global actions.

bestPractices.description: Pass items so internal filtering, empty state, and accessibility wiring have the full option set.
Use ComboboxEmpty with helpful copy for zero matches.

For results from a server, pass `filter={null}` so Base UI shows the items as the server returned them, fetch from `onInputValueChange`, and make ComboboxEmpty say which state it is in (searching, no results, type to search). Object items take `itemToStringLabel`.
Wrap in Field when the combobox is part of a form.
Use Combobox for tiny option sets where Select or Radio would be easier to scan.

Reach for ComboboxVirtualList past roughly a thousand rows, and leave filtering to the root. It reads the filtered list through useFilteredItems(), so the rendered rows and the rows Base UI navigates cannot drift apart.
Use `multiple` with ComboboxChips for several values from a filterable set, and keep chip labels short so the field does not turn into a paragraph.
Use Combobox as a command launcher. Use CommandMenu for actions and navigation.

Take filtering over with filteredItems in order to virtualize. Base UI ignores filteredItems while the untouched field still holds the selected item's label, so the list you render and the list it indexes diverge — and the symptom is clicking one row and getting another.

anatomy.name: Root
anatomy.description: Owns selected value, input value, filtering, and open state.

anatomy.name: Input
anatomy.description: The searchable text field and trigger.

anatomy.name: Chips
anatomy.description: The field for `multiple`, used in place of Input: one removable chip per selected item plus the text input, in one wrapping shell.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: The positioned popup surface.

anatomy.name: List
anatomy.description: The listbox inside the popup. Takes a render function that receives each filtered item.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: A selectable suggestion row.

anatomy.name: Empty
anatomy.description: Fallback shown when filtering returns no items.

props.name: Combobox (Root)
props.type: Base UI Combobox.Root props (items, value, defaultValue, onValueChange, inputValue, onInputValueChange, open, onOpenChange, multiple, autoHighlight, filter, disabled)
props.description: Groups all parts and owns selection + filter state. Pass `items` (flat array or groups) to enable internal filtering and ComboboxEmpty.

props.name: items
props.description: The pool of options, flat or grouped ({ value, items }). Drives type-to-filter and is required for ComboboxEmpty to render its fallback.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Select several items instead of one. `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` become arrays, choosing an item toggles its membership, and the popup stays open between picks. Pair it with ComboboxChips in place of ComboboxInput; every other part is unchanged.

props.name: filter
props.description: How items match the query. `null` turns matching off, for items a server already filtered: pair it with `onInputValueChange` to fetch.

props.name: highlightMatches
props.description: Paints the typed text wherever it appears in a row's label, on the `highlight` / `highlight-foreground` pair, through the CSS Custom Highlight API — no `<mark>` in the row, and the accessible name is unchanged. Only typed text counts: a field still holding the selected item's label lists everything and lights nothing. A literal, case-insensitive match within the label; a `filter` that matches differently leaves rows it kept unpainted. `false` turns it off.

props.name: onInputValueChange
props.description: Fires as the reader types. The place to fetch results for a server-backed combobox.

props.name: itemToStringLabel
props.description: The text an object item shows in the input once chosen, and is matched by. Needed for object items without a `label` field.

props.name: virtualized
props.description: Tells Base UI the DOM holds only part of the list. Required when using ComboboxVirtualList.

subcomponents.name: ComboboxInput
subcomponents.type: Base UI Combobox.Input props (minus the native `size` attribute) + size?: "md" | "xs" + className
subcomponents.description: The search field, styled like Input, wrapped with an InputGroup + chevron Trigger that toggles the popup. The chevron flips while the popup is open (data-[popup-open] on the toggle). `size="xs"` is the property-grid rung and mirrors SelectTrigger's `xs` exactly — same height, radius and inset surface — so a combobox and a select in one panel are the same shape holding different content (a font-family picker directly above a font-weight select is the case it exists for). Note the type: the native numeric `size` attribute is omitted rather than shadowed, because intersecting a string union onto it resolves to `never` and breaks every call site.

subcomponents.name: ComboboxChips
subcomponents.type: Base UI Combobox.Input props (minus the native `size` attribute) + size?: "md" | "xs" + chipLabel?: (item) => string + className
subcomponents.description: The field for a `multiple` combobox, used in place of ComboboxInput. Each selected item renders as a soft `sm` Badge with a ghost `icon-xs` Button that removes it (labelled "Remove {label}"), followed by the text input; the shell wraps and grows as chips are added. `chipLabel` turns an item into its chip text — defaults to the item for strings/numbers and its `label` field for objects. Keyboard is Base UI's: Backspace in an empty field removes the last chip, ←/→ move between chips, Backspace/Delete removes the highlighted one. `size="xs"` mirrors ComboboxInput's property-grid rung.

subcomponents.name: ComboboxContent
subcomponents.type: Base UI Popup props + { side?: Side; align?: Align; sideOffset?: number; scroll?: boolean; className?: string }
subcomponents.description: Portal + Positioner + Popup — it does not render a list, so put a ComboboxList (or ComboboxVirtualList) inside it. Width matches the input via --anchor-width. side is which side of the input the popup renders against (auto-flips on collision), align its alignment along that side, sideOffset the gap in px. Defaults to side='bottom', align='start', sideOffset=6, scroll=true. Pass scroll={false} when a ComboboxVirtualList inside owns the scrolling.

subcomponents.name: ComboboxList
subcomponents.type: Base UI Combobox.List props (children: ReactNode | (item, index) => ReactNode)
subcomponents.description: The listbox. Required inside ComboboxContent: pass a render function and it is called once per filtered item (or per group when `items` is grouped), so the rendered rows always match Base UI's filtering.

subcomponents.name: ComboboxVirtualList
subcomponents.type: { itemHeight: number; groupLabelHeight?: number; overscan?: number; children: (item, { index }) => ReactNode; renderGroupLabel?; className?; itemClassName? }
subcomponents.description: A windowed list: only the rows on screen exist. Fixed row heights (nothing is measured, so late-arriving content changes how a row looks and never where the rows are). Filtering stays Base UI's — the component reads the filtered list through useFilteredItems() — and groups keep their role=group wrapper and label association. Needs virtualized on the root and scroll={false} on ComboboxContent.

subcomponents.name: ComboboxItem
subcomponents.type: Base UI Combobox.Item props + className (value, disabled, index, onClick)
subcomponents.description: A suggestion row. Highlights via data-[highlighted]; shows a trailing check (ItemIndicator) when it matches the selected value.

subcomponents.name: ComboboxEmpty
subcomponents.description: Fallback shown when the filtered list is empty. Requires the `items` prop on the root.

subcomponents.name: ComboboxGroup
subcomponents.description: Groups related items under an accessible label auto-associated with the group.

subcomponents.name: ComboboxGroupLabel
subcomponents.description: The label for a ComboboxGroup. Auto-associated with the group it sits in.

motion.why: The list grows from the field it filters, its origin on Base UI's anchor. With several comboboxes in a form, that is what attaches the open list to the one being typed in.
A row's ink eases as the pointer or the arrow keys reach it, so moving through a long filtered list reads as continuous movement rather than rows blinking.

One highlight travels to the active row (lib/highlight-glide: a measured translate on the motion tokens) instead of each row painting its own fill. When the list re-filters under the caret, the highlight sliding to the new match is what shows the keyboard target moved.
The chevron toggle at the field's edge eases its ink on hover; the change is what tells you it is a separate target from the text box.
The chevron turns 180° as the list opens and closes (motion-interactive lists `rotate`), in step with the popup, so it reads as one control changing direction.
Closing shrinks back toward the field, returning the eye to the input that now holds the value.

Combobox ships no loading part. A list fetched as you type shows a Spinner (motion-spin) in ComboboxEmpty or the content — where the results will land — and only the caller knows a fetch is in flight.

a11y: Base UI provides role=combobox/listbox/option, roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and type-to-filter.
Esc and outside-press dismiss; focus returns to the input on close.
The chevron Trigger carries an aria-label and toggles the suggestions popup.
ComboboxEmpty announces filter results politely; keep it mounted (do not conditionally render it).
Animate open/close via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] attributes.

With `multiple`, the listbox is multi-selectable and each chip's remove button is labelled `Remove {label}`; Backspace in an empty field removes the last chip and ←/→ move between chips, so every chip is reachable without a pointer.
ComboboxVirtualList gives every rendered row aria-setsize (the full filtered count) and aria-posinset, so a screen reader is told the size of the list rather than the size of the window.
A highlight that lands on a row the window has not rendered is scrolled into view by the root, which forwards it to the list; Base UI's own scrollIntoView only reaches rows that exist.

examples.label: Basic
examples.code: <Combobox items={fruits}><ComboboxInput placeholder="Search fruit…" /><ComboboxContent><ComboboxEmpty>No matches.</ComboboxEmpty><ComboboxList>{(item) => (<ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>)}</ComboboxList></ComboboxContent></Combobox>

examples.label: Multiple selection
examples.code: <Combobox multiple items={tags} value={value} onValueChange={setValue}><ComboboxChips placeholder="Add tags…" /><ComboboxContent><ComboboxEmpty>No matching tags.</ComboboxEmpty><ComboboxList>{(item) => (<ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>)}</ComboboxList></ComboboxContent></Combobox>

examples.label: Async search (server results)
examples.code: <Combobox items={results} filter={null} itemToStringLabel={(person) => person.name} value={person} onValueChange={setPerson} onInputValueChange={setQuery}><ComboboxInput placeholder="Search people…" /><ComboboxContent><ComboboxEmpty>{searching ? "Searching…" : query ? "No one matches." : "Type a name to search."}</ComboboxEmpty><ComboboxList>{(item) => (<ComboboxItem key={item.id} value={item}>{item.name}</ComboboxItem>)}</ComboboxList></ComboboxContent></Combobox>

examples.code: <Combobox virtualized items={districts} value={district} onValueChange={setDistrict}><ComboboxInput placeholder="Search districts…" /><ComboboxContent scroll={false}><ComboboxEmpty>No district matches.</ComboboxEmpty><ComboboxVirtualList itemHeight={32}>{(item) => item.label}</ComboboxVirtualList></ComboboxContent></Combobox>

examples.label: Inside Field
examples.code: <Field label="Creator" description="Search by display name."><Combobox items={creators} value={creator} onValueChange={setCreator}><ComboboxInput placeholder="Search creators" /><ComboboxContent><ComboboxEmpty>No creators found.</ComboboxEmpty><ComboboxList>{(item) => (<ComboboxItem key={item.id} value={item}>{item.name}</ComboboxItem>)}</ComboboxList></ComboboxContent></Combobox></Field>
