components.name: CommandMenu
components.summary: A command palette (Cmd+K) built on our Dialog: a top-aligned wide surface with a search input and a scrollable, JS-filtered list of grouped commands. CommandMenuPanel renders the same palette in place, on a card in the page.

usage.description: Use CommandMenu for global or contextual keyboard-driven actions: navigation, creation, quick settings, or searchable commands. It should feel curated and fast; use Select, Menu, or Combobox for ordinary inline choices.

bestPractices.description: Open the palette from a header search with CommandMenuTrigger: a button wearing SearchInput's field shell, with the ⌘K / Ctrl K hint and the page-wide shortcut built in. A palette with no visible trigger still takes useCommandMenuShortcut rather than a hand-written keydown listener.

Hand-style a <button> to look like a search field, or put a SearchInput in the header that opens a dialog when focused. The first drifts from the field it imitates; the second is a text box you cannot type in. A header search that opens the palette is CommandMenuTrigger.
Group items by task area, such as Navigation, Create, or Settings, so users can scan before typing.
Keep command labels action-oriented and unique enough to search.
Provide useful bootstrap items so the menu is valuable before the user types.
Use CommandMenu as a replacement for every dropdown. Simple choices belong in Select, Menu, or Tabs.

Pass a filter when the palette searches more than one source. Ranking (exact prefix over substring over subsequence) is the caller's to own, and the returned order is kept verbatim — including group order, which follows each group's first surviving row.
List a command the user cannot currently run as disabled with the reason in hint, rather than filtering it away. A palette that hides what you cannot do teaches you nothing about why.
Resize the list with listClassName rather than reaching past className into the palette's DOM. className is the dialog surface; listClassName is the Scroller that actually scrolls.

Use CommandMenuPanel when the palette lives in the page: a sidebar launcher, a settings search, a demo. It takes the same items, filter, query and children, and keeps the same keyboard model; it is a static card, so it does not trap focus or take it on mount, and Esc clears the query instead of closing anything.
Hand-build a palette mock from a search glyph, a row of buttons and a highlight. That is CommandMenuPanel, and the hand-built one has no combobox, no filtering and no keyboard model.
Dump every app route and action into one uncurated list. Keep the palette opinionated.
Rebuild the combobox over Dialog to get consumer-owned ranking. query/onQueryChange and filter are that seam; the keyboard model, activedescendant wiring, and result-count live region come with them.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: CommandMenuTrigger — the search-field-shaped button in a header that opens the palette on click or on ⌘K / Ctrl+K. It sits outside CommandMenu; wire its onOpen to the palette's open state.

anatomy.name: Dialog surface
anatomy.description: The modal shell that traps focus and positions the launcher. CommandMenuPanel replaces it with a static card in the page (border, card fill, no shadow).

anatomy.name: Search input
anatomy.description: The combobox input that filters commands while focus remains in the field.

anatomy.name: Groups
anatomy.description: Labelled command sections that keep results scannable.

anatomy.name: Items
anatomy.description: Keyboard-selectable command rows that run onSelect and close the palette.

props.name: scope
props.description: A scope chip in the header, between the search glyph and the input — "In: Backdrop". A scope belongs beside the field rather than in its value: put it in the value and the user deletes prose to widen their search, and your filter parses it back out. Pair with inputProps.onKeyDown handling Backspace on an empty query, or the only way out of a scope is the mouse.

props.name: inputProps
props.description: Extra props for the search input. `onKeyDown` runs BEFORE the palette's own handling and opts out of a key by calling preventDefault() — which is what makes a scope chip Backspace-dismissable. Running first is deliberate: Backspace happens not to be a key the palette claims today, so a plain passthrough would work until the palette grows a 'Backspace clears the query' affordance, at which point the consumer's behaviour breaks silently. The combobox wiring (role, aria relationships, controlled value) is not overridable; aria-label and className compose.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state of the palette.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called on open/close (select, Esc, outside click).

props.name: items
props.description: Data-driven commands ({ group, label, onSelect, id?, icon?, detail?, stacked?, hint?, disabled? }). stacked puts detail on its own line under the label, for results only their detail tells apart (two tickets with one subject); beside a long label an inline detail truncates first. Ignored when children are provided. id is optional identity: filter is handed these same objects, so it is how a caller that ranks over its own richer model maps the array back onto it — and it becomes the row's DOM id (namespaced to the palette) and React key, so two rows may share a label.

props.name: query
props.description: Controlled query. Leave undefined to let the palette own it; either way it resets on close (a controlled caller gets onQueryChange('')).

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Called on every query change. Required to control query, optional otherwise.

props.name: filter
props.description: Replaces or disables the built-in match. A function ranks and filters items itself and its order is kept verbatim; null renders items exactly as given. Either also stops declarative CommandMenuItem children self-filtering. The query arrives raw — trimming and case are policy, and this is the prop that hands policy over.

props.name: highlightMatches
props.description: Paints the query wherever it appears in a row's label (not its detail or hint), on the `highlight` / `highlight-foreground` pair, through the CSS Custom Highlight API — no `<mark>` in the row, and the accessible name is unchanged. A literal, case-insensitive match, so under a fuzzy `filter` a row that matched as a subsequence keeps an unpainted label. `false` turns it off. Applies to CommandMenuPanel too.

props.name: listClassName
props.description: Classes for the scrolling list. className lands on the dialog surface, so this is the seam for the list's own height cap — listClassName="max-h-[60vh]". The list is a Scroller, so the cap lands on the element that scrolls and the edge fades come free.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for the search input.

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: Copy shown when the query matches nothing.

props.name: title
props.description: Accessible name for the palette dialog (visually hidden).

props.name: description
props.default: "Search for a command and press Enter to run it."
props.description: Accessible description for the palette dialog (visually hidden).

props.name: finalFocus
props.description: Where focus goes when the palette closes. The Dialog default returns it to the trigger — the CommandMenuTrigger, when there is one. A palette opened by the keystroke alone has none, so pass a resolver to restore whatever had focus, or false to restore nothing.

props.name: children
props.description: Declarative commands via CommandMenuGroup / CommandMenuItem. Takes precedence over items.

subcomponents.name: CommandMenuTrigger
subcomponents.type: { onOpen?: () => void; placeholder?: string; shortcut?: string | false; size?: "sm" | "md"; disabled?: boolean }
subcomponents.description: The search field in a header that is really a button. Wears SearchInput's shell (the field fill and outline, leading magnifier, muted placeholder) on the control ladder, with a trailing Kbd: ⌘K on macOS, Ctrl K elsewhere. onOpen runs on click and on the shortcut, which it listens for page-wide (useCommandMenuShortcut). shortcut is the key (default "k"); false drops both the hint and the listener. size is sm in a header beside small buttons, md (default) beside Input and SearchInput. It sits outside CommandMenu, so the Dialog returns focus to it on close.

subcomponents.name: useCommandMenuShortcut
subcomponents.type: (onShortcut: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void, key?: string | false) => void
subcomponents.description: The page-wide ⌘K / Ctrl+K listener CommandMenuTrigger installs, for a palette with no visible trigger. Ignored while focus is in a text field, textarea, select or contenteditable (Ctrl+K belongs to the field there) except the palette's own input, so the callback may toggle. It calls preventDefault() on a match and skips an event already prevented, so two listeners on one page fire once. key defaults to "k"; false turns it off. Removed on unmount.

subcomponents.name: CommandMenuPanel
subcomponents.type: { items?: CommandItem[]; query?: string; onQueryChange?: (query: string) => void; filter?: CommandFilter; listClassName?: string; placeholder?: string; emptyMessage?: string; title?: string; scope?: ReactNode; inputProps?: ComponentProps<'input'>; className?: string; children?: ReactNode }
subcomponents.description: The palette rendered in place: the same search header, filtered and grouped listbox, keyboard model and result-count live region, on a static card (border-border, bg-card, no shadow) instead of in a Dialog. Takes every CommandMenu prop except open, onOpenChange, finalFocus and description; className lands on the card, title names the listbox. Focus is not trapped and the input does not take focus on mount (inputProps.autoFocus opts in). Esc clears the query, and passes through once it is empty, so a Popover around the panel still closes. A chosen row runs its onSelect and the panel stays as it was. The page-wide shortcut does not fire from its input.

subcomponents.name: CommandMenuGroup
subcomponents.description: A labelled group of command rows.

subcomponents.name: CommandMenuItem
subcomponents.type: { onSelect?: () => void; icon?: string; detail?: ReactNode; stacked?: boolean; hint?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean; id?: string; children }
subcomponents.description: A selectable row. Self-filters by its text (unless the root was given a filter), runs onSelect, then closes the palette. detail is secondary text after the label, or under it with stacked; hint is the end-aligned trailing slot — a shortcut, a count, or a disabled row's reason. A disabled row stays listed, stays announced, and stays reachable by arrow key so its reason can be read, but is inert to Enter and to a click.

motion.why: The palette opens on DialogContent's recipe over a fading backdrop. It is summoned by a keystroke from nowhere on screen, and the short scale-in is what says a layer arrived rather than the page changing. The inline CommandMenuPanel has no entrance: it is part of the page.

The clear button mounts on the first keystroke, beside the caret the eye is already on. Fading in, it reads as the field offering a way back instead of a control blinking into the header. Removal is instant, so an emptied query does not wait on its X.
The active row follows both the arrow keys and the pointer, and its fill eases between rows, so scanning results while typing reads as one highlight moving rather than rows flashing in turn.
The search-shaped trigger eases its ink on hover like the field shell it imitates, so it reads as the field it opens.
Closing on Enter or Esc shrinks the palette away fast and returns focus where it came from; the exit is the confirmation that the command ran or was dismissed.
Results are filtered synchronously from the items passed in. Async results are the caller's to mark with a Spinner (motion-spin) in the list, where the person is already looking.

a11y: CommandMenuTrigger is a real <button> named by its visible placeholder, with aria-haspopup=dialog and aria-keyshortcuts (Meta+K on macOS, Control+K elsewhere). Its Kbd hint is aria-hidden, so the shortcut is announced once rather than read as part of the name.
The shortcut never fires from inside a text field, textarea, select or contenteditable (Ctrl+K is delete-to-end-of-line in macOS text views), except the palette's own input.

CommandMenuPanel is the same combobox and listbox in the page, with no dialog: it does not trap or steal focus, and Esc clears a non-empty query (stopping there) instead of dismissing. With an empty query Esc is left alone for whatever contains the panel.
Built on Base UI Dialog, so focus trap, scroll lock, and Esc/outside dismissal come for free; the dialog carries a visually-hidden title + description so it is announced.
Follows the ARIA combobox pattern: the search input is role=combobox (aria-autocomplete=list) that owns the role=listbox popup via aria-controls.
ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End and PageUp/PageDown move a virtual aria-activedescendant highlight while focus stays in the input; Enter runs the highlighted command. Arrow keys wrap; page jumps clamp.
Groups expose role=group labelled by their heading; items are role=option and never enter the tab order.
A polite role=status live region announces the result count as the query narrows, so the size of the list is available without reading it.
A disabled row carries aria-disabled and is skipped when seeding the highlight, but stays in the arrow-key walk so its reason can be reached and read.

The component keeps ownership of aria-activedescendant even when a caller claims a key through inputProps.onKeyDown. Skipping a move is coherent (they took responsibility for that key), but nothing may leave the active id naming a row that is not painted as active — so the opt-out returns before any highlight change rather than after it.

Exactly one row is ever painted as active: the pointer takes the highlight over (moving onto a row makes it the aria-activedescendant) rather than adding a hover fill of its own, so what looks highlighted is always what Enter will run.

components.name: ConfirmButton
components.summary: An inline two-step confirm for a low-stakes destructive or irreversible action: the first press arms it ("Delete" → "Confirm delete?", destructive), a second press within a few seconds runs it, and leaving it disarms it.

usage.description: Use ConfirmButton when an action deserves one beat of second thought but not a modal: deleting a draft, removing a row, revoking one token, clearing a list that can be rebuilt. The question appears on the button the user is already pressing, so confirming costs one more press in the same place and backing out costs nothing.

bestPractices.description: Keep the idle label a plain verb ("Delete", "Remove", "Revoke") and let the confirm label ask about it ("Confirm delete?" by default, or `confirmLabel`). The user should read the consequence on the very control they are about to press again.
Leave room for it to grow. The button eases wider to fit the question, so give it space at the end of a row or in a table's action column rather than wedging it between fixed-width neighbours.
Return the promise from `onConfirm` when the action is async. The button stays armed with a spinner until it settles and refuses further presses, so a slow network cannot run it twice.

Do not use it for high-stakes or wide-reaching actions — deleting a project, an account, anything other people depend on. Those need the consequence spelled out and a typed or deliberate confirmation; use DestructiveActionModal.
Do not use it where an undo is possible. If the action can be reversed, run it on the first press and offer Undo in a Toast — no question at all is faster than a good question.

Do not use it for a non-destructive primary action ("Save", "Send"). Asking twice for something harmless teaches people to press twice without reading, which is what defeats the confirm when it matters; use Button.

props.name: children
props.description: The idle label — the action, e.g. "Delete".

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: The label while armed. Defaults to "Confirm delete?" for a text label "Delete" (first letter lowered) and "Confirm?" otherwise. Pass it to localise.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Runs on the second press while armed. Return a promise to hold the button armed with a spinner until it settles.

props.name: timeout
props.description: How long it waits for the second press, in ms. A decision time, so it is not scaled by motion settings.

props.name: variant
props.description: The idle look — any Button variant.

props.name: confirmVariant
props.description: The armed look — any Button variant.

props.name: size
props.description: A labelled Button size. Icon-only sizes are excluded: the label is the interaction.

props.name: icon
props.description: A leading icon kept through both states, e.g. `<Icon name="trash" />`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables it; disabling while armed also disarms.

props.name: confirmHint
props.description: Read to assistive tech after the armed label when it arms. Override to localise.

props.name: motion
props.description: How much motion this component uses: `full` (default) inherits the app's policy, `subtle` keeps feedback and drops the flourish, `off` stills it. It can only turn motion down — it never overrides a reader's reduce-motion setting. The width easing and the draining countdown are the flourish; the label cross-fade and colour change stay.

motion.why: It is a button in a row of actions, and arrives with that row. Its moment is the arming, not the mount.
Inherited from Button with motion-interactive. The press settle confirms the first press landed even before the label has finished changing — which is what stops a second, accidental press.

Arming changes the label, so the button's width changes. Easing it makes the button visibly grow into the question and its neighbours travel, instead of the row jumping under the pointer that is about to press again. useAutoSize measures the content and writes a px width for motion-size to ease between (a content-sized box is width:auto before and after, which cannot transition). The labels cross-fade in one cell so there is never a frame with both or neither.

While armed, a thin line drains along the foot of the button over the timeout — the only way to see that the question expires. A transition on scale, timed by the `timeout` prop and multiplied by the motion scale and expressive factor, so under reduced motion or `subtle` it is absent rather than frozen full.

a11y: A native <button> through Button. Focus stays on it through both presses; Enter and Space confirm exactly as a click does.
Only the current label is in the accessible name — the other is aria-hidden — so the name changes to the question while armed.
Arming is also announced through a polite role=status region outside the button ("Confirm delete? Press again to confirm."), because a focused button's name change is not read by every screen reader.
Escape disarms and is consumed, so it does not also close the dialog or popover around it. Focus leaving, a press elsewhere, or the timeout disarm it too.
A second press within 300ms of arming is ignored: a double-click is a habit, not a decision.
Under reduced motion the label still changes and the colour still turns; only the width easing and countdown are dropped.

examples.code: <ConfirmButton icon={<Icon name="trash" />} onConfirm={() => removeRow(id)}>Delete</ConfirmButton>

examples.label: Custom question, longer wait
examples.code: <ConfirmButton variant="ghost" size="sm" confirmLabel="Revoke this key?" timeout={5000} onConfirm={revokeKey}>Revoke</ConfirmButton>

examples.label: Async confirm
examples.code: <ConfirmButton onConfirm={() => api.deleteDraft(draft.id)}>Discard draft</ConfirmButton>

components.name: ContextCard
components.summary: Hover/focus-triggered rich preview card over Base UI PreviewCard. Reveals contextual content (a profile, a project summary) from an inline anchor; 20rem-wide surface with delayed open and collision-aware positioning.

usage.description: Use ContextCard to show richer contextual content near a trigger without taking users out of flow.

bestPractices.description: Use it for previews, summaries, or supporting context tied to a specific element.

Keep the card read-only and make the trigger the action: it is a real link to the full profile or item. Keyboard users cannot reach a button inside the card, because moving focus off the trigger closes it. If the preview needs an action (Follow, Add), use a Popover instead.
Do not put critical decisions, long forms, or required workflow steps inside ContextCard.
Do not open it on click. It is a hover/focus preview; making it click-triggered gives you a Popover with no dismiss affordance and no way to reach the content it previews.

anatomy.description: The element that anchors the card.

anatomy.name: ContextCardContent
anatomy.description: The contextual surface shown near the trigger.

anatomy.name: ContextCardArrow
anatomy.description: An optional arrow connecting card and trigger.

a11y: Opens on hover and on keyboard focus of the trigger, after a short delay; dismisses on Esc, outside press, and blur.
The trigger renders an <a> by default — compose render={<a href='…'/>} so it stays a real, navigable link.
Base UI wires the popup's ARIA association with the trigger; the card holds non-interactive context, not focusable controls.
Animate via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] opacity attributes on the popup.

components.name: ContextMenu
components.summary: Right-click menu over Base UI ContextMenu — opens on the native contextmenu event or long press and positions at the pointer. Shares Menu's roving focus, typeahead, ARIA menu/menuitem wiring, collision-aware positioning, and Esc/outside dismissal.

usage.description: Use ContextMenu for actions that are specific to the object or area the user invoked.

bestPractices.description: Use it for secondary object actions such as rename, duplicate, move, or delete.
Group destructive or uncommon actions away from frequent safe actions.
Do not make ContextMenu the only way to access a primary or required action.
Do not rely on it for touch. There is no right-click on a touchscreen — the long-press fallback is discoverable by nobody, so anything in here needs a visible route too.

anatomy.name: ContextMenuTrigger
anatomy.description: The target area or element that opens the menu.

anatomy.name: ContextMenuContent
anatomy.description: The menu surface.

anatomy.name: ContextMenuItem
anatomy.description: One actionable command.

anatomy.name: ContextMenuSeparator
anatomy.description: A divider between command groups.

anatomy.name: ContextMenuGroup

anatomy.name: ContextMenuGroupLabel
anatomy.description: An optional label for a command group.

props.name: ContextMenu (Root)

subcomponents.name: ContextMenuTrigger

subcomponents.description: The right-clickable area that opens the menu on contextmenu (right click) or long press. Renders a <div>.

subcomponents.name: ContextMenuContent

subcomponents.description: Portal + Positioner + Popup. Positions at the pointer. side is which side of the anchor the popup renders against (auto-flips on collision), align its alignment along that side, sideOffset the gap in px. Defaults to side='bottom', align='start', sideOffset=6.

subcomponents.name: ContextMenuItem
subcomponents.type: Base UI ContextMenu.Item props + variant?: "default" | "destructive" + shortcut?: ReactNode + className (disabled, closeOnClick, onClick)
subcomponents.description: An interactive row. Lays out as a flex row, so a leading Icon sits inline before the label. Highlights via data-[highlighted]; dims via data-[disabled], and disabled items are skipped by keyboard focus. variant="destructive" marks a destructive command (Delete, Remove) and keeps its destructive ink while highlighted; never fake it with a text-destructive class, which the highlight repaints. `shortcut` ends the row with the command's key, muted and end-aligned, as on MenuItem.

subcomponents.name: ContextMenuSeparator
subcomponents.description: Hairline rule between item runs.

subcomponents.name: ContextMenuGroup

subcomponents.name: ContextMenuGroupLabel

a11y: Base UI provides role=menu/menuitem, roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and typeahead.
Opens on right click (contextmenu) or long press; Esc and outside-press dismiss and restore focus.
Animate open/close via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] attributes.
ContextMenuGroupLabel is auto-associated with its ContextMenuGroup for screen readers.

components.name: DataTable
components.summary: A data-driven table over the Table primitives — a columns def + data array with built-in client-side sorting (click a sortable header to cycle asc → desc → none), optional row click / selection, rows grouped under collapsible header rows (groupBy), and an empty state. For server data or paging, sort/page the data and pair with Pagination.

usage.description: Use DataTable when a data array and column definition should render a sortable, semantic table with optional row actions and an empty state. Use the lower-level Table parts for hand-authored markup or highly custom row layouts.

bestPractices.description: Put a table that fills a card in <CardContent flush>. The table runs edge to edge and its first and last columns inset to the card padding on their own; do not hand-set pl-6 / pr-6 on columns.
Provide stable rowKey values for dynamic data so selection and sorting do not jump.
Use sortable only on columns where ordering is obvious and useful.
Pair server-side datasets with Pagination and pass already-sorted/paged rows.

Group rows by status for an issue tracker (or by owner, by day) with groupBy + groups on ONE DataTable: every group shares the header and the column widths, each header row carries the group's count and an add action, and sorting applies within each group. Do not stack one DataTable per group inside Collapsibles; the header repeats and the columns stop lining up.

Move to TanStack Table, rendered with Sable's Table parts, once the table needs server-side sorting or filtering, column visibility or resizing, nested or aggregated grouping, or virtualised rows. DataTable stays dependency-free and does not grow into a data grid; `sable docs tables-with-tanstack` maps one onto the other.
Make every row clickable and also fill it with competing buttons. Choose a clear row interaction model.
Use DataTable for heterogeneous cards or timeline content. A list or card layout will scan better.

anatomy.name: Columns
anatomy.description: Definitions for headers, cell renderers, sorting, alignment, and classes.

anatomy.name: Rows
anatomy.description: The data array rendered through the column definitions.

anatomy.name: Empty state
anatomy.description: Content spanning all columns when the row array is empty.

anatomy.name: Group header row
anatomy.description: With groupBy: one row per group heading its own tbody (a th with scope=rowgroup across every column) holding the disclosure toggle, the group's icon, label and count, and an optional trailing action.

anatomy.name: Caption
anatomy.description: Accessible table caption rendered by the underlying Table.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column defs: { key, header, cell?, sortValue?, sortable?, align?, className? }. cell defaults to row[key]; sortValue defaults to row[key]. When cell renders a formatted string (e.g. a date), pass sortValue returning the underlying value (e.g. date.getTime()) so the column sorts by the real value, not the rendered text.

props.name: data
props.description: The rows to render.

props.name: rowKey
props.description: Stable React key per row.

props.name: onRowClick
props.description: Row click handler — makes rows pointer-interactive.

props.name: isRowSelected
props.description: Mark a row visually selected (data-selected), e.g. the one open in a detail pane. Derive it from a stable id (row.id === selectedId), not the row index, so selection survives re-sorts. For checking several rows, use selectedKeys.

props.name: selectedKeys
props.description: The checked rows, by rowKey, for bulk actions. With onSelectedKeysChange it adds a checkbox column (each box named by rowSelectionLabel) and a select-all box in the header that acts on the rows shown and goes mixed when some are checked. Checked rows get the selected fill. Controlled: when the rows shown change (a filter, another view), set the keys to keep, usually none. Needs rowKey.

props.name: onSelectedKeysChange
props.description: Called with the new set of checked keys. Its presence turns selection on. A click on a box never fires onRowClick.

props.name: rowSelectionLabel
props.description: A row checkbox's accessible name. Name the row, e.g. (t) => `Select ${t.subject}`, so a screen reader can tell the boxes apart.

props.name: selectAllLabel
props.description: The select-all checkbox's accessible name; say what it acts on ("Select all 7 tickets shown").

props.name: defaultSort
props.description: Initial sort column + direction.

props.name: empty
props.description: Rendered spanning all columns when data is empty. Pass an EmptyState for the full treatment (icon, title, next step).

props.name: caption
props.description: Bottom table caption.

props.name: groupBy
props.description: Group the rows under header rows by the key this returns (a status, an owner, a day). One header serves every group, so the columns line up across them; sorting applies within each group.

props.name: groups
props.type: { key: string; label?: ReactNode; icon?: ReactNode; action?: ReactNode; defaultExpanded?: boolean }[]
props.description: Order and presentation of the groups, by key: the header row's label (defaults to the key), a leading icon such as a status mark, a trailing action such as an icon Button that adds a row to the group, and whether it starts open (default true). Groups groupBy returns that are not listed follow, in the order their first row appears in data. A listed group with no rows is not shown.

props.name: collapsible
props.description: Whether each group's header row is a toggle that opens and closes the group. A closed group keeps its header row and count; its rows are hidden and select-all skips them.

props.name: expandedGroups
props.description: The open groups, by key (controlled). Without it each group starts at its defaultExpanded and the table holds the state.

props.name: onExpandedGroupsChange
props.description: Called with the new set of open group keys when a group header is toggled.

motion.why: Rows render with the page or the query that produced them. Staggering rows in delays reading a table someone opened to scan.

Body rows ease to a muted wash under the pointer (TableRow's recipe), which keeps the eye on the right line across a wide row of numbers. Sortable headers are ghost Buttons and answer on Button's recipe.

One chevron turns to show direction instead of two glyphs swapping, so ascending to descending reads as the same column reversing. Its opacity rises from the resting 60% as the column becomes the sort.
A checked row's fill eases in across its cells, so selecting by checkbox reads as the row being picked rather than a band stamped over it.
A group's chevron turns from pointing along the reading direction (closed) to down (open), so the group reads as folding rather than a glyph being swapped.
Opening a group shows its rows at once: table rows cannot animate their height without leaving the table layout, and the rows are the content the reader asked for.
DataTable has no loading state. While data is fetched, render Skeleton rows (motion-shimmer) in its place — only the caller knows a fetch is in flight.

a11y: Sorted columns set aria-sort=ascending/descending on the header cell.
Sortable headers are real <button>s with a focus-visible ring, keyboard-operable.
Inherits the Table's scrollable frame and semantic <table>/<th>/<td> structure.

Grouped, each group is its own <tbody> (a rowgroup) headed by a <th scope="rowgroup"> spanning the columns, so group headers are never read as data rows; the toggle is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls naming that tbody.

components.name: DatePicker
components.summary: Date (and optionally time) picker: a field-shaped trigger (the Input / SelectTrigger shell) opens a Popover holding Sable's Calendar. With granularity="day" selecting a day fires onValueChange and closes; granularity="minute" adds an hour + minute row of Selects and keeps the time-of-day when the day changes.

usage.description: Use DatePicker when users need to choose one date — or, with granularity="minute", one date and time — from a compact control.

bestPractices.description: Use it in forms where a typed date alone would be error-prone.
Show clear selected and disabled states when date rules apply.
Set granularity="minute" when a time matters, with a minuteStep that matches the real precision (15 for meetings, 5 for scheduled posts).
Do not show a time without saying which zone it is in. A meeting time with no zone is wrong for everyone not in yours — wrap the picker in a Field whose description names the zone.
Do not leave the format ambiguous. `03/04` is two different dates depending on the reader's locale — the trigger shows a formatted date precisely so the interpretation is not guessed.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected date (controlled). When absent, the trigger shows a muted placeholder.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value when uncontrolled (no `value` prop).

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fired when the day is chosen or cleared, and under granularity="minute" when the hour or minute changes. With granularity="day" it also closes the popover.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Deprecated alias for onValueChange, kept for backwards compatibility. Both fire when set; prefer onValueChange.

props.name: granularity
props.description: What the picker chooses. "minute" adds an hour + minute row and keeps the popover open so day and time can be set in any order.

props.name: minuteStep
props.description: Minute increment for the time row (granularity="minute" only).

props.name: defaultTime
props.description: Time-of-day shown and applied while nothing is selected yet, as 24h "HH:mm" — the first day pick lands on this time instead of midnight (granularity="minute" only).

props.name: placeholder
props.default: "Pick a date" ("Pick date & time" with granularity="minute")
props.description: Trigger label shown when no date is selected.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable the trigger and block selection.

props.name: minDate
props.description: Earliest selectable day (inclusive). Earlier days are disabled and navigation is bounded.

props.name: maxDate
props.description: Latest selectable day (inclusive). Later days are disabled and navigation is bounded.

props.name: size
props.description: The trigger's rung. md is the form field beside Input and Select. xs is the property-grid rung (24px in a workspace): an inset panel-field well with no border, the same shape as SelectTrigger size="xs" and ScrubField on the neighbouring rows of an inspector — use it for a due date in a PropertyRow instead of a native date input.

props.name: formatOptions
props.description: How the trigger writes the chosen date, as Intl.DateTimeFormat options in the reader's locale — { month: "short", day: "numeric" } for "Oct 23" where the rest of a list writes dates that way. Omitted: "Oct 23, 2026" (with "at 14:30" under granularity="minute").

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the trigger.

props.name: id / aria-label / aria-labelledby / aria-describedby / aria-invalid / aria-required
props.description: Forwarded to the trigger, so a wrapping Field ties its label to the picker and announces its description and error. Pass them yourself only when labelling the picker without a Field.

a11y: Trigger opens on click/Enter/Space; the popover traps focus and restores it to the trigger on close (Base UI Popover).
The calendar grid (react-day-picker) provides a roving tabindex, arrow-key day navigation, and aria-selected on the chosen day.
Navigation chevrons render through the Icon adapter and inherit the calendar's button labels.
Esc and outside press dismiss the popover.

With granularity="minute" the hour and minute Selects are full Base UI listboxes (typeahead, ARIA) labelled "Hour" and "Minute"; selecting a day keeps the chosen time-of-day, so day and time can be set in any order.

examples.label: In an inspector row
examples.code:
<PanelSection title="Properties">
	<PropertyRow label="Due date">
		<DatePicker size="xs" aria-label="Due date" value={due} onValueChange={setDue} formatOptions={{ month: "short", day: "numeric" }} />
	</PropertyRow>
</PanelSection>

examples.code:
const [date, setDate] = useState<Date>()
<DatePicker value={date} onValueChange={setDate} />

examples.code: <DatePicker placeholder="Schedule for…" value={date} onValueChange={setDate} />

examples.code:

<DatePicker granularity="minute" value={start} onValueChange={setStart} minDate={new Date()} defaultTime="09:00" minuteStep={15} />

examples.code: <DatePicker disabled />

components.name: DateTile
components.composition: a <time> element with the type tiers, on a surface utility
components.summary: A calendar-page date: the short month on a primary band over the day number, in a <time> element. The leading visual of an event, booking or deadline row.

usage.description: Use DateTile as the leading visual when the date is what a reader scans a list or card by — events, bookings, deadlines, releases. It sits beside a title and a time line, usually in an Entity's `leading` slot or a flex row in a CardContent. For a date inside a sentence or a row's metadata, use text or RelativeTime instead.

bestPractices.description: Pair the tile with a title and the full time or range in text beside it; the tile only names the day.
Keep every row of a list on DateTile so the dates line up as one column.
Use it for timestamps ("2 hours ago", "Oct 14, 10:02") — that is RelativeTime or plain metadata text.
Stretch it to its neighbour's height or restyle the band per row; the tile is a fixed shape so a column of them reads as one calendar.

anatomy.name: Band
anatomy.description: The short month name on the primary colour.

anatomy.name: Day
anatomy.description: The day of the month, on the muted surface.

props.name: date
props.description: The day to show, read in local time. Rendered as `<time dateTime="YYYY-MM-DD">`.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale for the month name.

motion.why: A static label; it appears with whatever row or card holds it.
Not interactive.
It has no states to move between.
Nothing runs in the background.

a11y: Renders a <time> with a machine-readable `dateTime`, so the day is announced as text ("Oct 14") and parsable as a date.
The tile names only the day — state the weekday, time or range in the text beside it, where it is read in order.

examples.label: Event row
examples.code: Design review Tuesday, 2:00 – 2:45 PM

examples.label: In an Entity list
examples.code:
<CardList>
	<Entity leading={<DateTile date={new Date(2026, 9, 14)} />} title="Design review" subtitle="Tuesday, 2:00 PM" />
	<Entity leading={<DateTile date={new Date(2026, 9, 21)} />} title="Launch" subtitle="Tuesday, all day" />
</CardList>

components.name: DestructiveActionModal
components.summary: Confirmation modal for irreversible actions, built on AlertDialog (role=alertdialog; a backdrop click does not dismiss). Pairs a secondary Cancel with a destructive confirm; awaits an async onConfirm (spinner + stays open on failure) or takes an external pending flag; optional body slot and type-to-confirm guard for high-stakes deletions.

usage.description: Use DestructiveActionModal to confirm irreversible or high-risk actions before they run.

bestPractices.description: Name the affected object and the consequence of the action in plain language.
Make the destructive action visually distinct from the cancel path.
Do not use it for routine low-risk actions where undo or inline confirmation would be faster.
Do not put the destructive action where Cancel usually sits, or make it the default focus. A confirmation dialog exists to add friction; autofocusing Delete removes the friction it was added for.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the open state should change (Esc, Cancel, or confirm). A backdrop click does not dismiss.

props.name: title
props.description: Modal heading — names the irreversible action.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional supporting copy explaining the consequence.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: Label for the destructive confirm button.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: Label for the dismissing secondary button.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Called when the user confirms. If it returns a Promise the modal shows an in-flight spinner, closes on resolve, and stays open on reject; if void it closes immediately (unless pending is controlled).

props.name: pending
props.description: Externally-driven in-flight state. Overrides the internal await tracking; the parent owns closing (the modal stays open on a synchronous confirm).

props.name: confirmingLabel
props.description: Confirm-button label shown while the action is in flight.

props.name: children
props.description: Body content rendered between the description and the type-to-confirm Input / footer — e.g. a warning <Note>.

props.name: confirmText
props.description: When set, renders an Input the user must type matching to enable the destructive confirm button.

a11y: Built on AlertDialog (Base UI): role="alertdialog", focus trapping, scroll lock, and aria-modal. Esc dismisses; a click on the backdrop does not, so a stray click can't throw away the decision.
Focus opens on Cancel — the safe action — even when a type-to-confirm Input comes first, so a reflexive Enter never fires the destructive action.
The title labels the modal; the description describes it.
The type-to-confirm Input is wired to its label via htmlFor; the destructive Button is disabled (not just hidden) until the text matches.
While a confirm is in flight (awaited onConfirm or pending), both buttons disable, the confirm Button sets aria-busy, and Esc dismissal is blocked so the action can't be interrupted or double-fired.

examples.label: Basic
examples.code: <DestructiveActionModal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title='Delete post?' description='This permanently removes the post. This cannot be undone.' onConfirm={handleDelete} />

examples.label: Async confirm (awaited spinner)
examples.code: <DestructiveActionModal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title='Block user?' description='They can no longer interact with you.' confirmLabel='Block' confirmingLabel='Blocking…' onConfirm={() => blockUser(id)} />

examples.label: Body slot + type-to-confirm
examples.code: <DestructiveActionModal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title='Delete this post?' confirmText='gold rush' confirmLabel='Delete forever' onConfirm={handleDelete}><Note tone='warning'>People you shared this post with lose access to it.</Note></DestructiveActionModal>

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: Modal surface over Base UI Dialog (focus trap, scroll lock, Esc/outside dismissal). Centered on desktop; max-width 500px. size="fullscreen" is the full-bleed media viewer (image, video, Carousel) over a near-opaque scrim.

usage.description: Use Dialog for focused decisions, short modal forms, confirmations, and content that temporarily blocks the underlying page. Prefer Sheet for side-panel workflows, Popover for lightweight anchored content, and inline sections for content that should remain part of the page.

bestPractices.description: Always include DialogTitle and usually DialogDescription so the modal has an accessible name and context.
Keep the footer actions explicit: a safe escape path plus the primary or destructive action.
Use showCloseButton for dismissible informational dialogs; keep destructive confirmations action-led.
In a destructive confirmation, state the consequence in DialogDescription ("This is permanent.") and reserve the destructive button variant for actions that cannot be undone.
Put large multipage workflows in a centered dialog. Use Sheet or a page route when the task needs space.

Use size="fullscreen" when an image, video, or gallery needs a larger view than the layout can give it. Give the popup an accessible name (aria-label on DialogContent, or a visually hidden DialogTitle) and alt text on the media.

Use size="fullscreen" for forms, confirmations, or anything that isn't media. A dialog that happens to need room is a Sheet or a page; the fullscreen affordances (dark scrim, corner close, centred content) all assume something to look at.
Hide the close button at size="fullscreen" without another visible way out. A full-bleed viewer that only Esc dismisses is a dead end for anyone who doesn't know the key.
Open a dialog for passive status updates. Use Toast, Banner, or InlineStatus instead.

Open a dialog from your own button with controlled open/onOpenChange when the trigger is not a DialogTrigger (a menu item, a row action, a keyboard shortcut). Focus returns on close to whatever held it when the dialog opened, with no finalFocus wiring; pass finalFocus only to send it somewhere else.

Set keepMounted on DialogContent for a draft the user may come back to (a compose form, a long comment, a half-filled request). Closing by Esc or a stray click then hides the dialog instead of unmounting it, so the fields are still filled when it reopens. Clear the draft yourself on submit or discard.

Set keepMounted by default. A dialog that should open fresh (a confirmation, a create form after a successful save) would show stale input, and live content (polling, video) keeps running while hidden.

Use the AlertDialog family for a confirmation that must be answered (discard changes, leave without saving). It looks identical but is role="alertdialog" and a backdrop click does not dismiss it — only Cancel, Esc, or the action. For irreversible deletes, use DestructiveActionModal, which is built on it.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: The element that opens the dialog when using the composed trigger pattern.

anatomy.name: Overlay
anatomy.description: The dimming backdrop behind the modal content.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: The modal surface that receives focus trap, labelled-by, and described-by wiring.

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: Title and optional description that explain the decision or task.

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Action row for cancel, confirm, submit, or destructive choices.

props.name: Dialog (Root)
props.type: Base UI Dialog.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, modal)
props.description: Controls open state. Uncontrolled by default. Records the element that holds focus when the dialog opens (through a DialogTrigger, or your own button flipping a controlled open) and returns focus there on close.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with onOpenChange — for a dialog opened from your own button instead of a DialogTrigger.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the dialog asks to open or close (a trigger, Esc, an outside click, DialogClose).

subcomponents.name: DialogContent
subcomponents.type: Base UI Popup props (initialFocus, finalFocus) + size?: "default" | "fullscreen" + showCloseButton?: boolean + scroll?: boolean + keepMounted?: boolean + className
subcomponents.description: Backdrop + popup; portals to <body>. Composes DialogOverlay by default. size="fullscreen" is the media viewer: a near-opaque scrim (bg-overlay/95), an edge-to-edge popup that centres its children with no card chrome, motion-fade instead of motion-pop, and a safe-area-aware floating close button (Button variant="floating"); at that size showCloseButton defaults to true and scroll to false, and the media fits itself with max-h-full max-w-full object-contain. At the default size, showCloseButton (defaults to false) renders a built-in close (X) button in the top-end corner, and the header leaves room for it (Icon name="xmark"). The popup caps at the viewport height less a 1rem margin and wraps its children in a scrolling region, so a tall dialog scrolls instead of overflowing a viewport whose own scroll is locked; pass scroll={false} when the dialog owns its internal layout (a pinned header over a scrolling body) and supplies its own min-h-0 scroll region. keepMounted (default false) keeps the content mounted and hidden while closed, so a draft survives close and reopen. finalFocus defaults to the element focused when the dialog opened, trigger or not; an explicit finalFocus (a ref, a function, or false) wins.

subcomponents.name: DialogOverlay
subcomponents.type: Base UI Backdrop props + size?: "default" | "fullscreen" + className
subcomponents.description: The styleable scrim/backdrop — bg-overlay/(--scrim-alpha) by default (50% light, 72% dark, so it dims a near-black page as visibly as a white one), near-opaque bg-overlay/95 at size="fullscreen". Composed into DialogContent (at the matching size) by default; exported for manual styling.

subcomponents.name: DialogTrigger
subcomponents.description: Element that opens the dialog. Compose via render prop.

subcomponents.name: DialogClose
subcomponents.description: Element that dismisses the dialog. Compose via render prop.

subcomponents.name: DialogHeader
subcomponents.description: Top section holding DialogTitle/DialogDescription.

subcomponents.name: DialogTitle
subcomponents.description: The dialog's accessible name — wires aria-labelledby on the popup.

subcomponents.name: DialogDescription
subcomponents.description: Muted supporting line; wires aria-describedby.

subcomponents.name: DialogFooter
subcomponents.description: Bottom action row (right-aligned buttons).

subcomponents.name: AlertDialog (Root)
subcomponents.type: Base UI AlertDialog.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange)
subcomponents.description: Root for a confirmation that needs an answer. Always modal; the popup is role="alertdialog" and a click outside does not dismiss — only an AlertDialogClose, an action that sets open to false, or Esc. Returns focus on close to the element focused when it opened, exactly as Dialog does.

subcomponents.name: AlertDialogTrigger
subcomponents.description: Opens the alert dialog.

subcomponents.name: AlertDialogContent / AlertDialogOverlay / AlertDialogTitle / AlertDialogDescription / AlertDialogHeader / AlertDialogFooter / AlertDialogClose
subcomponents.type: Same props as the matching Dialog part
subcomponents.description: The Dialog parts under AlertDialog names — Base UI shares the popup, backdrop, title, description and close parts between the two, so the surface is identical. Pass initialFocus to AlertDialogContent (a ref to the Cancel button) to open focus on the safe action.

motion.why: The scrim is what tells the reader the page behind is no longer live. Appearing at full opacity in one frame reads as a page navigation — the surrounding context vanishes instead of receding.
The panel scales up as the scrim darkens, so the two read as one event. Overlay and panel arriving on separate timings is the most common way a modal feels cheap.
The close affordance is a small icon in a corner and is often the only control a reader looks for. Its hover state has to be findable, not just present.
Exit runs the same recipe in reverse so dismissal is legibly the inverse of opening. A modal that fades out having scaled in leaves the reader unsure whether it closed or navigated away.
The dialog is a container. Work happening inside it is the content's to report — a dialog-level indicator would claim the whole surface is busy when usually one field is.

a11y: Base UI provides focus trapping, scroll lock, aria-modal, and labelled-by wiring (DialogTitle).

Content taller than the viewport scrolls inside the dialog (thin scrollbar, contained overscroll) rather than overflowing off screen — the page behind is scroll-locked, so anything past the edge would be unreachable.

On close, focus returns to the element that held it when the dialog opened, whether a DialogTrigger opened it or your own button set a controlled open. It is captured before the content mounts, so an autoFocus field inside cannot displace it. If that element has left the page, Base UI's default (the trigger, if any) applies; an explicit finalFocus on the content always wins. AlertDialog and Sheet behave the same.
keepMounted hides closed content with the hidden attribute, so a kept draft is out of the accessibility tree and the tab order until the dialog reopens.
Esc and click-outside dismiss by default. AlertDialog keeps Esc but ignores click-outside, and its popup is role="alertdialog".
Animate via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] attributes.

size="fullscreen" has no title chrome, so name the popup yourself: aria-label on DialogContent (or a visually hidden DialogTitle), plus alt text on the media — the zoomed image is a separate image to assistive technology. Its built-in close button carries aria-label="Close" and clears the safe-area insets (notch, home indicator).

components.name: DisclosurePicker
components.summary: A property row that names the current value and opens its list in place, beneath the row, instead of in a popup — for a tool panel or settings column where the choice is made while looking at what it changes. Built on Collapsible; the list is a listbox — arrow keys move, Enter or a click picks, applies and closes — and an optional search field filters long lists.

usage.description: Use DisclosurePicker for one-of-many choices in a docked panel or inspector where a popup would cover the preview the choice is about: the row shows the current value (in its own face, with a tile, as the content warrants), and the list opens beneath it, pushing the panel down. Use Select for a form field or anywhere a popup is fine; use Combobox when people type to find an option among hundreds; use RadioGroup or RadioCard when every option should stay visible. Nothing applies while arrowing through the list — only Enter, Space or a click picks — so it suits choices with a cost (a confirm, a font load, a reset); where each option should apply as focus lands on it, that is a radio group (ThemeSelector, RadioGroup).

bestPractices.description: Enable search (`search` on DisclosurePickerPanel) only for long lists — roughly a dozen options or more, i.e. once the list scrolls. A short list (a handful of presets) reads faster with no field to skip past; the panel then has no search row and no gap.
Show the value as the thing it is: a font row renders the family in its own face, a theme row leads with a ThemePreview tile in `media`. The row is a preview of the choice, not a label for it.

Use `size="xs"` in a property grid (a compact Density / PanelSection), where it sits on the inset panel-field fill beside ScrubField and an xs SelectTrigger. Keep `md` in a settings column or a simple panel.
When several rows share a panel, control `open` from the parent so only one list is open at a time — two open lists push each other and the preview out of view.

Use it for a choice with a cost — one that opens a confirm, loads something, or resets other settings. Arrow keys only move focus; onValueChange fires once, on Enter, Space or a click, and only when the pick differs from `value`.

Give options a leading visual with `media` (a ThemePreview tile, a swatch) instead of nesting another component's list: ThemeSelector's radio list applies each theme as the arrow keys land on it, which defeats commit-on-Enter. A list the picker cannot express (a Tree) can still close the row with `useDisclosurePicker().close()`.
Render DisclosurePickerEmpty in place of the list when a search matches nothing, not inside it — a listbox holds only options.
Use it in a page-register form. A form field that pushes the form down on open reads as a layout jump; that is Select's job.

Rebuild the row from a Collapsible with hand-copied classes. The disclosure, the well, the hover step, the xs field shell, focus return and scroll-into-view all live here; two hand copies of this row in one panel is how it came to exist.
Turn search on for a short list just because the other rows have it. A search field over six options is a control with nothing to do.

anatomy.name: DisclosurePicker
anatomy.description: Root. Owns open state, size, focus return and scroll-into-view.

anatomy.name: DisclosurePickerTrigger
anatomy.description: The row: optional `label` caption, optional `media`, the value, and a chevron that flips when open.

anatomy.name: DisclosurePickerPanel
anatomy.description: What opens beneath the row: the opt-in search field, then the list.

anatomy.name: DisclosurePickerList
anatomy.description: A listbox of options that scrolls past 16rem. Arrow keys move; Enter, Space or a click picks.

anatomy.name: DisclosurePickerOption
anatomy.description: One option row, with optional leading media and trailing note. Chosen, it lifts out of the well; focused, it takes the ring.

anatomy.name: DisclosurePickerEmpty
anatomy.description: The no-match line, rendered in place of the list when a search filters everything out.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with onOpenChange.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Uncontrolled initial open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state — from the trigger, a pick, or Escape.

props.name: size
props.description: md is a --control-md row (40px comfortable) in a settings column, its own well when closed. xs is the property-grid rung: a --control-xs row on the inset panel-field fill with ui-tier type. Height, padding, radius, type and surface move together.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root (layout only — the look comes from size).

subcomponents.name: DisclosurePickerTrigger
subcomponents.type: { label?: ReactNode; media?: ReactNode; children?: ReactNode } + Base UI Collapsible.Trigger props
subcomponents.description: The row. `label` is a muted leading caption on a fixed column so stacked rows align; `media` a leading visual (a ThemePreview tile); children the value, truncated on one line. ArrowDown opens it, and steps into the list once open.

subcomponents.name: DisclosurePickerPanel
subcomponents.type: { search?: { value: string; onValueChange(value: string): void; placeholder?: string; label?: string } } + Collapsible.Panel props
subcomponents.description: Opens beneath the row. `search` opts in to a SearchInput above the list (off by default); it is controlled because the consumer filters, and it is cleared when the row closes. Escape clears a query first, then closes; ArrowDown in the field steps into the list.

subcomponents.name: DisclosurePickerList
subcomponents.type: { value: string; onValueChange(value: string): void; aria-label?: string } + div props
subcomponents.description: A listbox. ArrowUp/ArrowDown, Home/End and type-ahead move focus without applying anything (ArrowUp from the first option returns to the search field); Enter, Space or a click picks the focused option — onValueChange fires once, only when it differs from `value` — and closes the row. Escape closes without a pick.

subcomponents.name: DisclosurePickerOption
subcomponents.type: { value: string; children?: ReactNode; media?: ReactNode; note?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean; textValue?: string; onRemove?: () => void; removeLabel?: string }
subcomponents.description: One option row. `media` is a leading visual (a ThemePreview tile); `note` a muted trailing annotation — options without one show a check when chosen. `disabled` skips it for the keyboard and refuses the pick; `textValue` is what type-ahead matches when the name is not plain text. `onRemove` makes the option removable — for entries the person added (an imported preset, a saved font): a trash glyph at the row's end on hover or focus (always on touch), and Delete or Backspace on the focused row; removing never picks, and focus moves to a neighbour first. `removeLabel` is the glyph's tooltip.

subcomponents.name: DisclosurePickerEmpty
subcomponents.description: The no-match line, rendered in place of the list.

subcomponents.name: useDisclosurePicker
subcomponents.description: For a list the picker does not own (a Tree) that should close the row when something is picked.

motion.why: A property row is present from first paint; animating it in would stage chrome the user is already scanning.
The row reads as a value, not a button; the hover step is what says it opens before it is clicked.
The list pushes the panel down; growing its height ties the movement below to this row rather than to a layout jump.
Nothing is indeterminate: the options are resident. A list that loads should show its own loader inside the panel.

a11y: The trigger is a real <button>; Base UI wires aria-expanded and aria-controls to the panel. Its accessible name is its text (caption + value) unless an aria-label is given.

The list is role="listbox" with role="option" rows; aria-selected marks the committed value, not the focused row, so a screen reader hears both where focus is and what is chosen. Selection does not follow focus: ArrowUp/ArrowDown, Home/End and type-ahead move focus (roving tabindex — one tab stop, so Tab leaves the list in one step) and apply nothing; Enter, Space or a click picks, applies and closes. Disabled options carry aria-disabled and are skipped.

Why a listbox and not a radio group: a radio group's checked state follows focus, so every arrow press would be a pick — wrong for a choice that opens a confirm, loads a font or resets settings. Base UI ships no standalone listbox (Select is popup-only, Combobox's inline list is focus-in-the-input, Composite is internal), so the keyboard model lives here.

Opening from the keyboard (Enter, Space, ArrowDown) moves focus into the panel: the search field when there is one, otherwise the chosen option (or the first). A pointer open focuses the search field on a fine pointer only, so touch does not raise the on-screen keyboard.

Escape closes the row without changing the value (clearing a query first) and returns focus to the trigger; a pick does the same. Focus is not pulled back when it has already moved on, e.g. to a confirm dialog the pick opened.

A removable option (onRemove) announces aria-keyshortcuts="Delete"; Delete or Backspace removes it and focus moves to the next option (or the previous). The trash glyph is a pointer target only (aria-hidden, not focusable): an option's children are presentational, so a nested button would be unreachable by assistive tech anyway.
The panel animates with motion-disclosure, which is static under prefers-reduced-motion or MotionProvider off; the scroll that keeps the row in view is instant, never smooth.

examples.label: A short list — no search
examples.code:
const [preset, setPreset] = useState("comfortable")
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
<DisclosurePicker open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} className="w-72">
  <DisclosurePickerTrigger label="Density">{preset === "compact" ? "Compact" : "Comfortable"}</DisclosurePickerTrigger>
  <DisclosurePickerPanel>
    <DisclosurePickerList aria-label="Density" value={preset} onValueChange={setPreset}>
      <DisclosurePickerOption value="comfortable">Comfortable</DisclosurePickerOption>
      <DisclosurePickerOption value="compact">Compact</DisclosurePickerOption>
    </DisclosurePickerList>
  </DisclosurePickerPanel>
</DisclosurePicker>
examples.imports: import { DisclosurePicker, DisclosurePickerList, DisclosurePickerOption, DisclosurePickerPanel, DisclosurePickerTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: A long list — search opted in
examples.imports: import { DisclosurePicker, DisclosurePickerEmpty, DisclosurePickerList, DisclosurePickerOption, DisclosurePickerPanel, DisclosurePickerTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: A theme picker — media tiles, commit on Enter
examples.imports: import { DisclosurePicker, DisclosurePickerList, DisclosurePickerOption, DisclosurePickerPanel, DisclosurePickerTrigger, ThemePreview, useSableTheme } from "@sableui/react"

const [blend, setBlend] = useState("normal")
<Density value="compact" className="w-64">
  <DisclosurePicker size="xs">
    <DisclosurePickerTrigger label="Blend">{blend}</DisclosurePickerTrigger>
    <DisclosurePickerPanel>

</Density>
