components.name: EmptyState
components.summary: The centered empty / error block: optional icon or error code, title, description and an action. tone="destructive" makes it an announced error, size="lg" a page-level state, surface="card" a self-contained card.

usage.description: Use EmptyState when a content area has no items, no search results, or no first-time setup yet. The title should name the empty condition and the description/action should give the user a next step.

bestPractices.description: Explain what is empty in plain language, such as "No posts yet" or "No matching customers".
Offer one next step when the user can recover, create, clear filters, or start setup.
Keep the icon decorative and make the title carry the meaning.

For a search or filter result, name the query back to the user and offer the way out, such as "No results for 'quarterly'" with a Clear filters action. An empty result that does not say what was searched leaves the user unsure whether the query or the data was wrong.
Use generic copy like "No data"; it gives users and agents no useful path forward.

Park anything the user needs permanently here, such as setup instructions, billing notices, or keyboard shortcuts. An empty state is the one surface guaranteed to disappear the moment content exists, so information that matters after the first item is lost exactly when the user has learned enough to want it.
Use it for a field's validation error — that is Field error messaging. Reserve tone="destructive" for a view or block that failed to load.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: A decorative cue that reinforces the empty condition.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.description: The short message naming what is empty.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Supporting copy that explains why the state exists or what to try next.

anatomy.name: Action
anatomy.description: One clear button or link that moves the user forward.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional glyph above the title — an `<Icon />` takes the muted ink at 3xl; an image or illustration renders as given.

props.name: title
props.description: The headline. Short and direct.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional supporting line beneath the title.

props.name: action
props.description: Optional action below the copy — typically a `<Button />`.

props.name: code
props.description: A large figure above the title, such as an error code (404).

props.name: tone
props.description: destructive is an error state: a destructive icon (a warning by default) and role="alert" so it is announced.

props.name: size
props.description: lg is page-level: the title is an h2 and the block takes more room. md sits in a panel, list or card.

props.name: surface
props.description: card draws it as a Card, for an error or empty block standing on its own in a page.

a11y: Decorative icons should not carry meaning the title doesn't already convey.
Pair with an actionable next step so the zero-state is a path forward, not a dead end.

examples.label: With icon and action
examples.code: <EmptyState icon={<Icon name="info" />} title="No posts yet" description="Create your first." action={<Button>New post</Button>} />

examples.label: No search results
examples.code: <EmptyState icon={<Icon name="search" />} title="No matching posts" description="Try a different keyword or clear your filters." action={<Button variant="secondary">Clear filters</Button>} />

examples.label: First-run setup
examples.code: <EmptyState surface="card" icon={<Icon name="sparkles" />} title="Start your first project" description="Create a project, import one from a file, or invite collaborators." action={<Row gap={1}><Button>Create project</Button><Button variant="ghost">Import</Button></Row>} />
examples.imports: import { Button, EmptyState, Icon, Row } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: Page-level error
examples.code: <EmptyState tone="destructive" size="lg" code="404" title="Page not found" description="The page you are looking for has moved or never existed." action={<Button>Go home</Button>} />

examples.label: Error card
examples.code: <EmptyState tone="destructive" surface="card" title="Could not load this project" description="Check your connection and try again." action={<Button variant="secondary">Retry</Button>} />

examples.label: Empty table body
examples.code: <DataTable data={[]} columns={[{ key: "name", header: "Customer" }, { key: "status", header: "Status" }]} empty={<EmptyState title="No customers yet" description="Customers appear here after the first order." />} />

components.name: Entity
components.summary: A list-row record: leading visual + title/subtitle column + trailing action, with truncating text. Presentational by default (no hover); `interactive` rows gain the hover highlight, focus ring, and keyboard activation, and `selected` marks the current one. Compact/comfortable density.

usage.description: Use Entity to show a compact identity block for a person, organization, file, project, or other object.

bestPractices.description: Use a clear title and one or two useful metadata lines.
Pair with Avatar or Badge (dot for a status) when identity needs state or type.

For a list, stack Entity rows directly in a column; each row owns its padding. For a list in a card, put the rows in CardList, which insets them to the card's own padding and divides them, so the rows line up with the card's header instead of being tuned by hand with px-* classes.
Do not use Entity for long descriptions, editable fields, or full card content.
Do not make the whole row a link when it also carries a trailing action. Nesting an interactive element inside a link is invalid, and the action becomes unreachable by keyboard.

props.name: leading
props.description: Leading visual — typically an Avatar or an Icon.

props.name: title
props.description: Primary line (text-title-sm, truncated). Required.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Secondary line (text-body-sm muted, truncated).

props.name: action
props.description: Trailing slot — typically a ghost icon Button or a StatusDot.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Make the whole row a target: the leading visual and text become a native <button> whose hit area stretches over the row (focus ring, Enter/Space). The action stays outside it. Requires onSelect.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Activation handler for an interactive row (fired on click and Enter/Space). Required when interactive.

props.name: selected
props.description: Interactive rows only: the current row of a selectable list (the record open in a list–detail view). Sets aria-current="true" on the row's button and paints the selected fill, a step off the surface the row sits on, which holds on hover.

props.name: density
props.description: Row padding: compact (12px × 10px, the default) or comfortable (16px × 12px), on the spacing scale. The insets read --entity-px / --entity-py first, which CardList sets from the card's own padding so rows in a card line up with its header.

motion.why: Rows arrive with the list they belong to. Entering one at a time is a stagger, and a stagger on a list someone opened to scan is a delay.

Only the interactive row reacts: its hover fill, a step off the surface it sits on, eases in. A static row never fakes clickability, and an interactive one answers the pointer without flicker as it moves down a list.
`selected` eases the fill onto the current row of a list–detail view, so opening another record reads as the selection moving rather than two rows flashing.
A record row has nothing of its own to wait for. A row whose action is pending puts a loading Button in `action`.

a11y: Default rows are presentational layout; semantics come from the content you place in title/subtitle/action.

interactive rows render a real <button> around the leading visual and text, with its ::after stretched over the whole row — native focus, a focus-visible ring, and Enter/Space. The action slot sits outside that button and above the overlay, so a Button there stays valid HTML and keeps its own clicks.
Give any interactive action an accessible label (e.g. aria-label on a ghost icon Button).
A selected row announces aria-current="true" on its button, so the current record is spoken, not only shown by its fill.

examples.label: Person row
examples.code: <Entity leading={<Avatar fallback="AM" />} title="Alex Morgan" subtitle="@alex" action={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="More"><Icon name="ellipsis" /></Button>} />
examples.imports: import { Avatar, Button, Entity, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: Interactive (selectable) row
examples.code: <Entity interactive onSelect={() => selectUser(user)} leading={<Avatar fallback="AM" />} title="Alex Morgan" subtitle="@alex" />

components.name: Feedback
components.summary: A compact feedback popover. Composes Popover + Textarea + Button + Toggle into a rating row plus a message field; submitting reports the rating + message, shows a brief drawn-check thanks, and closes the popover.

usage.description: Use Feedback to collect lightweight sentiment, usefulness, or quality signals from users.

bestPractices.description: Ask for feedback at a moment when the user has enough context to answer.
Keep the prompt short and optional unless feedback is required by the workflow.
Do not use Feedback for errors, alerts, or required support forms.
Do not require the message field. Most feedback is a rating with no comment, and forcing prose is how a feedback control stops being used.

props.name: label
props.description: Trigger button text.

props.name: heading
props.description: Heading shown above the rating row.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for the message field.

props.name: submitLabel
props.description: Submit button text.

props.name: ratings
props.description: The rating options shown as a row of toggles. Each is { value, label }.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Called with the selected rating + message when the form is submitted. The thanks shows right away; send the report in the background.

props.name: successMessage
props.description: The line shown, and read out, for about 1.2s after sending, before the popover closes on its own.

props.name: motion
props.description: How much motion this component uses: `full` (default) inherits the app's policy, `subtle` keeps feedback and drops the flourish, `off` stills it. It can only turn motion down — it never overrides a reader's reduce-motion setting. The drawn check is the flourish; the thanks line and its dwell stay.

motion.why: The form opens from its trigger, so the eye goes from the button it pressed to the field it should type in. Popover owns the recipe.
The rating row is a choice among a few similar marks. The eased selected fill is what makes the pick read as made, not just hovered.

The mark itself answers the pick: it blooms past its size and settles, so choosing reads as a small decision landing rather than a fill changing. Only the chosen mark, only on choosing — nothing blooms when the form opens or a pick is let go. Expressive: under subtle the fill alone answers.

Sending is the one moment the person needs to know their words arrived. The form fades out in place and a check draws itself in over it, then the popover closes. Without it the popover just vanished, which looks the same as the form being dismissed or the message lost.
The thanks shows as soon as the form is sent; delivery is the app's background work. A spinner for a one-line report would make a quick, optional gesture feel heavy.

a11y: Trigger opens the popover on press; Base UI manages focus into the form and restores it to the trigger on close.
The rating row is a Base UI ToggleGroup with arrow-key roving focus; each toggle carries an aria-label.
The form is named by its heading (aria-labelledby), so it is announced as "Send feedback" rather than an unnamed form.
The message field carries an aria-label matching its placeholder.
Submit is disabled until there is a rating or a non-whitespace message. Either alone is a complete answer.

On send, focus moves to the thanks line (tabIndex=-1), which reads it out, and the form becomes inert so focus cannot land in invisible fields. The line is not also a live region, which read it twice. When the popover closes, Base UI returns focus to the trigger.
The thanks dwell (about 1.2s) is a reading time, not motion, so it is the same under reduced motion.

examples.label: Basic
examples.code: <Feedback onSubmit={({ rating, message }) => console.log(rating, message)} />

examples.label: Custom labels
examples.code: <Feedback label="Tell us" submitLabel="Send it" placeholder="Describe the issue…" />

examples.label: Custom thanks
examples.code: <Feedback successMessage="Got it — thank you." onSubmit={({ rating, message }) => report(rating, message)} />

components.name: Fieldset
components.summary: Form section panel (Card-like bordered surface) over Base UI Fieldset, with Legend/Description/Content/Footer parts; `variant="plain"` is the bare group, for a radio group's shared name.

usage.description: Use Fieldset to group related controls under a shared label or explanation.

bestPractices.description: Use it for grouped form sections such as contact details, preferences, or permissions.
Keep the legend meaningful so assistive tech and agents understand the group purpose.
Do not use Fieldset as a generic spacing wrapper outside forms.

Use `variant="plain"` to name a radio group or a run of checkboxes inside a form or card that is already framed: the legend reads as a field label and nothing draws a second box. Do not strip the card variant with classes instead.
Do not use a Legend that is really a heading. A legend names the group's question for assistive technology; using it as a section title puts a question mark where the outline should be.

anatomy.name: Fieldset
anatomy.description: The bordered group: a native <fieldset> whose disabled state reaches every control inside it.

anatomy.name: Legend
anatomy.description: FieldsetLegend: the question the group's controls answer, announced before each of them.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: FieldsetDescription: muted copy under the legend.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: FieldsetContent: the stacked body, one Field per control.

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: FieldsetFooter: the group's actions on a muted wash.

props.name: variant
props.description: `card` is a bordered, raised section with padded parts. `plain` is the grouping alone (no border, surface or inset) with the legend in the field-label style: the shared name a radio group needs, inside a form that is already framed.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the whole group. Renders <fieldset disabled> (native control disabling) and surfaces data-[disabled] for dimming.

props.name: render
props.description: Base UI render prop to replace or compose the underlying element.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto each part via cn() for one-off overrides.

subcomponents.name: FieldsetLegend
subcomponents.description: The group's name — the question its controls answer. Base UI renders it as a <div> wired to the <fieldset> through aria-labelledby, so a screen reader announces it before each control in the group. This is the whole reason to reach for Fieldset.

subcomponents.name: FieldsetDescription
subcomponents.description: Muted supporting copy under the legend.

subcomponents.name: FieldsetContent
subcomponents.description: The stacked body holding one Field per control.

subcomponents.name: FieldsetFooter
subcomponents.description: Optional right-aligned action bar on a muted wash.

a11y: Base.Root renders a native <fieldset>; Base.Legend renders an auto-associated label, so screen readers announce the group name.
disabled propagates as native <fieldset disabled>, disabling all contained controls.
Wrap each control inside FieldsetContent in a Field, which wires its own label, description and error to the control.

examples.label: A grouped question
examples.code:
<Fieldset>
	<FieldsetLegend>Notify me about</FieldsetLegend>
	<FieldsetDescription>Pick what reaches your inbox.</FieldsetDescription>
	<FieldsetContent>
		<Field label="Mentions" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox defaultChecked /></Field>
		<Field label="Replies" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox /></Field>
		<Field label="Direct messages" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox /></Field>
	</FieldsetContent>
	<FieldsetFooter>
		<Button>Save preferences</Button>
	</FieldsetFooter>
</Fieldset>
examples.imports: import { Button, Checkbox, Field, Fieldset, FieldsetContent, FieldsetDescription, FieldsetFooter, FieldsetLegend } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: Why a fieldset, and when it is wrong
examples.imports: import { Field, Fieldset, FieldsetContent, FieldsetLegend, Radio, RadioGroup } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: A radio group's name, without a second box
examples.code:
<Card>
  <CardContent>
    <Fieldset variant="plain">
      <FieldsetLegend>Delivery</FieldsetLegend>
      <RadioGroup defaultValue="standard">
        <RadioCard value="standard" title="Standard" description="3–5 working days" trailing="Free" />
        <RadioCard value="express" title="Express" description="Next working day" trailing="$12.00" />
      </RadioGroup>
    </Fieldset>
  </CardContent>
</Card>
examples.imports: import { Card, CardContent, Fieldset, FieldsetLegend, RadioCard, RadioGroup } from "@sableui/react"

components.name: FileDropzone
components.summary: Drag-and-drop target and file picker in one keyboard-operable button. Checks accept, maxSize and maxFiles on every selection, announces each rejection with how to fix it, and hands accepted files to you to list as Attachments.

usage.description: Use FileDropzone where adding files is the main job of a section — an upload step, an import screen, a document request. It gives the drag gesture a visible target and the same action a button for everyone who does not drag. It holds no list: render accepted files as Attachments beneath it, where progress, retry and remove belong.

bestPractices.description: State the constraints in `description` ("PNG or PDF, up to 10 MB") and give `acceptLabel` the same words, so a rejection repeats the rule the user already read.
Pair it with a list of Attachment rows that you own. Once files are added, switch to `size="sm"` so the target stays available without pushing the list below the fold.

Cap the total by passing `maxFiles={limit - files.length}`; the dropzone only sees one selection at a time. When none remain, set `disabled` and say why in `description` ("Remove one to add another").
Do not use it for an incidental attach action inside a composer or a toolbar. A paperclip Button that opens the picker is the right weight there; ChatComposer already has one.
Do not rely on `accept` alone to protect the server. The dropzone's checks are for the user's benefit; validate type and size again where the file is received.
Do not silently drop rejected files. The zone announces each one, but if you also discard files later (a server-side limit), say so on the Attachment with `status="error"` and a fix.

anatomy.name: Zone
anatomy.description: A full-width button with a dashed border. Click, Enter or Space opens the picker; it is also the drop target.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: A decorative mark that lifts while a file is dragged over the zone.

anatomy.name: Label and description
anatomy.description: The call to action and the constraints. Together they form the button's accessible name.

anatomy.name: Status
anatomy.description: A role=status region, present from the first render, that lists each rejected file and how to fix it.

props.name: accept
props.description: Native accept syntax — `.pdf`, `application/pdf`, `image/*`, comma-separated. Enforced on drop and on pick.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Largest accepted file, in bytes.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Accept more than one file per selection.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description: Most files accepted from one selection when `multiple`. Pass the remaining capacity to cap a total.

props.name: onFilesAccepted
props.description: Files that passed every check, in selection order.

props.name: onFilesRejected
props.description: Files that failed, each with `code` (file-invalid-type, file-too-large, too-many-files) and the announced `message`.

props.name: label
props.description: The visible call to action. Pluralised automatically when `multiple`.

props.name: description
props.description: The constraints in words, shown under the label.

props.name: acceptLabel
props.description: How the accepted types complete "Use … instead" in an error ("PNG or PDF", "an image or PDF"). Without it a type error can only say "Choose a different file".

props.name: formatError
props.description: Replace the rejection copy, e.g. to localize it.

props.name: icon
props.description: Semantic icon name.

props.name: size
props.description: `md` is the empty-section target; `sm` is a single-row strip above an existing list.

props.name: disabled / required / id / aria-invalid
props.description: Standard form-control props. `id` lands on the button, so `<Field>` labels it; `aria-invalid` draws the destructive border.

motion.why: The zone is the section's content, present from the start. An entrance would only delay the drop target someone is already dragging toward.
Hover strengthens the border to primary, which confirms the whole dashed area — not just the word "browse" — is the click target.

When a file crosses into the zone the icon fills and lifts and the surface tints. That is the only signal that releasing here will work; without it users drop on the page and the browser opens the file instead.
The zone hands files off immediately and never uploads. Transfer progress belongs on each Attachment, where it can be per-file and retryable.

a11y: The zone is a native button: Enter or Space opens the system picker, so dragging is never the only way in.
Rejections render into a role=status region that exists from the first render, and the button's aria-describedby points at it while it has content, so the reason is still read when focus returns.
Every error names the file and says how to fix it ("Choose a smaller file"), rather than only what failed.
The underlying file input is visually hidden and removed from the tab order; the button is the single focus stop.

examples.label: Images and PDFs
examples.code: <FileDropzone accept="image/*,.pdf" acceptLabel="an image or PDF" maxSize={10 * 1024 * 1024} multiple description="Images or PDFs, up to 10 MB each" onFilesAccepted={(files) => console.log(files)} />

examples.label: With an Attachment list
examples.code: console.log(files)} />

examples.label: In a field
examples.code: <Field label="Proof of address" description="A bill or statement from the last 3 months."><FileDropzone accept=".pdf" acceptLabel="a PDF" maxSize={5 * 1024 * 1024} description="PDF, up to 5 MB" /></Field>

components.name: FontPicker
components.summary: A DisclosurePicker for a typeface: the row names the chosen family in its own face and opens in place into a searchable list of families, each drawn in itself. The app supplies the families and loads the faces; Sable bundles no catalog.

usage.description: Use FontPicker wherever someone chooses a typeface for a role (body, headings, code) in a panel that shows the result: a theme editor, a document inspector, a brand customizer. It is a DisclosurePicker, so the list opens beneath the row rather than over the preview; arrow keys walk the families (each drawn in its own face) without applying or loading anything, and Enter, Space or a click picks one, loads it and closes the row.

bestPractices.description: Pass `loadFont` and load faces lazily: `"preview"` fires for every family when the list opens (load just the glyphs of its name — Google Fonts' `text=` parameter makes a 20-font list cost a few KB), `"use"` for the chosen one (load its real weights). Make it idempotent and define it once, outside render.
Put non-font choices — "Preset (Figtree)", "Same as body" — in `options`, with a short `valueLabel` for the row. They list first and render in the app's face, so they never read as a family.
Give each row a role `label` ("Body", "Headings", "Mono") and stack them; the caption column aligns. Control `open` from the parent so only one list is open at a time.
Leave search on for a short curated list — under a dozen families, pass `searchable={false}`. Search is on by default because font lists are usually long.
Use a Select of family names for this. A popup covers the text it changes, and a family name set in the app's face says nothing about the face.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen family, or the value of one of `options`.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called once a family (or option) is picked — Enter, Space or a click — and only when it differs from `value`; the row then closes. Arrow keys and type-ahead only move focus; Escape closes without a pick.

props.name: fonts
props.type: readonly { family: string; note?: string; stack?: string }[]
props.description: The families to offer, in order. `note` is a muted annotation (searched too); `stack` the CSS font-family to draw it in (default `"<family>"`).

props.name: options
props.type: readonly { value: string; label: string; valueLabel?: string }[]
props.description: Non-font choices listed above the fonts, in the app's face. `valueLabel` is what the row shows while it is chosen.

props.name: label
props.description: The row's leading caption — the role the font plays.

props.name: listLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the list.

props.name: searchable
props.description: A search field above the list, filtering by family and note. Pass false for a short curated list (under a dozen).

props.name: searchLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the search field.

props.name: loadFont
props.description: Loads a face on demand: "preview" for every family when the list opens, "use" for the chosen one once it is picked (never while the list is only being walked). Receives your own font objects. Idempotent.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state, as DisclosurePicker. Control it to keep one of several rows open at a time.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Uncontrolled initial open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state.

props.name: size
props.description: md for a settings column; xs for the property-grid rung (see DisclosurePicker).

motion.why: A property row is present from first paint.
Inherited from DisclosurePicker: the hover step says the value row opens.
Inherited from DisclosurePicker: the list grows in place, tying the panel's movement to this row.
Faces load in the background and swap in when ready; the names are legible in the fallback meanwhile, so there is nothing to wait on.

a11y: Inherits DisclosurePicker: a button trigger with aria-expanded/controls whose name is the caption plus the family; a listbox named by `listLabel`, aria-selected on the chosen family.

Keyboard open focuses the search field; ArrowDown steps from it into the list (ArrowUp from the first option steps back); arrows, Home/End and type-ahead move without applying; Enter or Space picks and closes; Escape clears the query, then closes without a pick and returns focus to the row.
Each family is set in its own face, but its name is still plain text, so a screen reader reads the name, not the glyphs.

components.name: Form
components.summary: A styled <form> plus Field — the form orchestration layer, built on Base UI Form and Field. Field wires a label, control, helper text, and error message together with correct a11y (htmlFor, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, required) automatically, around any Sable control. Validation-library-agnostic: pass each Field an error string, or let Form check native constraints and Field validate functions on submit.

usage.description: Use Form and Field as the default wrapper for Sable form controls. Field owns the label, description, required state, and error wiring so agents do not hand-roll inconsistent label/input relationships.

bestPractices.description: Wrap each control in Field unless a specialized component already owns its label and error semantics.
Use Field error for validation messages so aria-invalid and aria-describedby are wired together.

For built-in checks, put required / type="email" / minLength on the control (or a validate function on Field) inside a Form: on submit the message appears under the field and the first invalid control is focused. Pass server errors to Form errors, keyed by Field name.
Use horizontal Field orientation only for one-line boolean controls like Checkbox, Switch, or Radio.
Use placeholder text as the only label. A visible label should identify the field.
Wrap multiple controls in one Field. Field expects a single child control and wires that one control (an Input or Textarea nested in a wrapper is still found through context).

anatomy.name: Form
anatomy.description: The native form element (Base UI Form) with vertical field spacing; validates its Fields on submit.

anatomy.name: Field
anatomy.description: The label/control/helper/error wrapper for one control.

anatomy.name: Control
anatomy.description: The single Sable control. Base UI-backed controls register with Field through context; the child is also cloned with the same wiring.

anatomy.name: Error
anatomy.description: Validation copy associated with the control: the error prop when set, otherwise the Base UI validation message (native constraint, validate function, or Form errors).

props.name: Form
props.type: { validationMode?: "onSubmit" | "onBlur" | "onChange"; errors?: Record<string, string | string[]>; onFormSubmit?: (values, details) => void; actionsRef?: RefObject<Form.Actions> } + ComponentPropsWithRef<"form">
props.description: A <form> laid out as a vertical column with comfortable field spacing (override with className, e.g. gap-4). On submit it validates every Field (native constraints plus Field validate), shows each message under its field, focuses the first invalid control, and only then calls onSubmit. validationMode defaults to "onSubmit" (then live re-validation on change). errors shows external (e.g. server) messages keyed by Field name and clears one when its field is edited. onFormSubmit receives the named Field values and prevents the native submit. A control outside any Field is still checked by the browser before onSubmit runs. Validating in your own code (react-hook-form, a schema, state)? Pass noValidate: onSubmit always runs and each Field shows the error you set; without it an empty required Field stops the submit before your handler can set that error. Either way, once onSubmit returns (or the promise it returns settles), the first control a Field marks invalid takes focus.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: The native submit handler. It may return a promise. When it returns, or its promise settles, the first control a Field marks invalid takes focus, so errors your own code sets get the same treatment as Sable's validation.

props.name: validationMode
props.description: When Fields validate. After the first submit, fields re-check as the user edits. A Field's own validationMode wins.

props.name: errors
props.description: External (e.g. server) messages keyed by Field name, shown under that field. Each clears when its field is edited.

props.name: onFormSubmit
props.description: Called with the named Field values after validation passes; prevents the native submit.

props.name: noValidate
props.description: Your code owns validation: nothing is checked before onSubmit (neither the Fields nor the browser), so it always runs and each Field shows the error you pass. required Fields keep their asterisk and aria-required. validationMode, errors, onFormSubmit and actionsRef do nothing with it.

props.name: actionsRef
props.description: Imperative handle to validate every field, or one by name.

subcomponents.name: Field
subcomponents.type: { label?: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; error?: ReactNode; required?: boolean; messages?: Partial<Record<"valueMissing" | "typeMismatch" | "patternMismatch" | "tooShort" | "tooLong" | "rangeUnderflow" | "rangeOverflow" | "stepMismatch" | "badInput", ReactNode>>; disabled?: boolean; name?: string; validate?: (value, formValues) => string | string[] | null | Promise<…>; validationMode?: "onSubmit" | "onBlur" | "onChange"; validationDebounceTime?: number; orientation?: "vertical" | "horizontal"; trailing?: ReactNode; className?: string; children: ReactElement } + other div props on the root
subcomponents.description: Wraps a single control element (e.g. <Input />) on Base UI Field and wires label (htmlFor + aria-labelledby), helper text and error (aria-describedby), aria-invalid, and required onto it automatically. Base UI-backed controls (Input, Textarea, Select, Combobox, NumberField, Checkbox, Switch, Slider, OtpField…) register through context; the child is also cloned so plain elements keep the same wiring. error renders a destructive message and takes precedence; without it the slot shows the field's messages entry for the native constraint that failed (messages={{ valueMissing: "Enter a subject." }}), else Base UI's validation message (the browser's wording for a native constraint, validate, or Form errors). required adds the native attribute plus a visual asterisk (defaults to false). disabled disables the control and dims the label. name keys the field in Form errors / onFormSubmit. validationMode overrides the Form's. orientation defaults to "vertical" (label → control); "horizontal" places control then label inline for a single checkbox / switch / radio — the control centres on the label's first line (it stays there when the label wraps) and description/error sit in the label's column. trailing puts something at the end of the control's row: vertically, beside the control (a promo code's Apply button, the control taking the rest); horizontally, at the end of the label's first line (a facet count). Other props (data-*, id, aria-*) land on the root. The root, label, description, error and control carry data-invalid / data-valid, data-touched, data-dirty, data-filled, data-focused and data-disabled for state styling.

a11y: Field auto-wires label htmlFor ↔ control id, aria-describedby (description + error), and aria-invalid — so the label, helper, and error are all announced for the control.
required adds the native `required` attribute (not just a visual asterisk); the asterisk is aria-hidden.
Error text is associated via aria-describedby and reinforced by the destructive color, not color alone.
Inside Form, a failed submit focuses the first invalid control and shows its message inline instead of a browser bubble.

components.name: GlidingHighlight
components.summary: One highlight that travels to the active item, instead of each item toggling its own background. Measured, not assumed, so rows of unequal height stay exact.

usage.description: Use GlidingHighlight for a set of items where one is active at a time and the pointer or arrow keys move between them — a menu, an option list, a command palette, a segmented control. It replaces per-item `hover:bg-*` with a single element that moves.

bestPractices.description: Pass `hovered ?? selected`. The fallback is what makes the pointer leaving a menu return the highlight to the current choice instead of dropping it, so the reader's place is never lost.

Reach for it wherever a list is keyboard-navigable. The gain is largest for arrow keys: a background that teleports between rows makes the eye re-find the highlight at every step, where one that moves can be tracked while it travels — which is what keeps a long list readable in motion rather than only at rest.
Keep selection semantics on the items — `aria-selected`, `aria-current`, `data-selected`. The highlight is `aria-hidden` decoration over whatever the children already announce.

Do not use it for items that are not mutually exclusive. A travelling highlight says 'one of these, and it is this one'; over a multi-select list it contradicts the checkboxes beside it, and only one of the two can be right.

Do not put non-item chrome among the direct children — a group heading, a separator, a footer hint. Every direct child is a measurable row, so `active` counts them, and the highlight lands one row off from the index the caller is reasoning about. Wrap the items in their own GlidingHighlight, or move the chrome outside.

Do not drive it from a scroll position or a timer. It is an affordance for a set with a discrete active member; a highlight that moves without an item becoming active reads as the interface selecting things on its own.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: Positioning context for the highlight. Each direct child is measured as one item.

anatomy.name: Highlight
anatomy.description: The travelling element. `aria-hidden`, absolutely positioned, invisible until something is active.

props.name: active
props.description: Index of the item the highlight sits behind, or `null` for none. Pass `hovered ?? selected`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Deprecated and ignored: the highlight measures both axes, so a horizontal row needs no flag.

props.name: onPointerLeave
props.description: The container is a plain div, so its props pass through. For a hover-following list, reset the hovered index here so the highlight returns to the selected row when the pointer leaves.

props.name: highlightClassName
props.description: Class for the travelling highlight itself, for changing its fill or radius. The radius defaults to `sable-frame-inner`, so inside a `sable-frame` container it nests concentrically; in any other rounded, inset container pass `rounded-concentric-<outer>/<inset>` here and on the rows. The container's own `className` styles the list.

motion.why: It deliberately does not animate in. Fading it up at rest position — usually row 0 — makes a menu look like it opened with the first item pre-selected, which is a claim about state that is not true. It stays invisible until something is genuinely active.
The container is not the control; the items are, and they own their own pointer states. This draws the result.

The travel IS the component — a highlight that jumps is just a background toggle with extra machinery. Position, size and opacity ride one declaration so a tall row's height cannot catch up after its position has, which would read as the highlight stretching into place rather than moving.
Nothing here is indeterminate. A list still loading its options shows a Skeleton in place of the rows.

a11y: The highlight is `aria-hidden` and carries no semantics — it renders selection, it does not declare it. Keep `aria-selected` / `aria-current` on the items themselves.
Pointer-free by construction (`pointer-events-none`), so it can never intercept a click meant for the item beneath it.
Works with roving-tabindex and `aria-activedescendant` lists alike: it reads an index the caller already owns, and does not manage focus.
Under reduced motion or with MotionProvider off, the highlight moves instantly rather than gliding — the active item is still shown, which is the part that carries meaning.

examples.label: A hoverable menu, returning home on leave
examples.code: <GlidingHighlight active={hovered ?? selected} className="sable-frame sable-surface sable-surface-popover sable-frame-popover" onPointerLeave={() => setHovered(null)}>{items.map((item, i) => (<button key={item.id} type="button" className="sable-frame-inner px-2 py-1.5 text-start" onPointerEnter={() => setHovered(i)} onClick={() => setSelected(i)}>{item.label}</button>))}</GlidingHighlight>

examples.label: Horizontal, as a segmented control
examples.code: <GlidingHighlight active={tab} className="sable-well flex gap-1 rounded-md p-1" highlightClassName="rounded-concentric-md/1">{tabs.map((t, i) => (<button key={t} type="button" className="rounded-concentric-md/1 px-3 py-1" onClick={() => setTab(i)}>{t}</button>))}</GlidingHighlight>

components.name: GradientArt
components.summary: Placeholder artwork painted by a static WebGL shader from the preset's own art direction (the --art-* tokens: palette, ground, warp, softness, grain) — Ember burns, Prism airbrushes, Meridian is grainy monochrome — with a CSS gradient underneath for prerendered pages and browsers without WebGL2.

usage.description: Use GradientArt where a real image belongs but none exists yet, or where the image is decoration: a product cover before upload, a profile banner, an album tile, an avatar with no photo. It reads the theme's own tokens, so it follows every preset, mode and live edit; `seed` fixes each item's composition so a list of covers or avatars stays individually recognisable. `intensity="soft"` paints the same art as a pastel wash — the iridescent aura AI products use as a card or modal header band, and as a stage for floating chips and logo tiles.

bestPractices.description: Pass a stable `seed` per item — the name for an avatar, the title for a cover. Each item then keeps the same art across renders, reloads and themes, which is what lets someone recognise it.
Size it with layout classes (`aspect-[4/3]`, `h-20`, `size-10 rounded-full`) and put any glyph or initials inside as children; they render above the art.

Keep the default `mesh` for covers, tiles and avatars. Reach for `grain` where a printed, tactile surface suits — a banner, a hero card — and keep one variant per surface type so art reads as a system.

Use `intensity="soft"` as a stage: a card or modal header band, the art on an integration or pricing card, a field behind floating prompt chips or rounded logo tiles. Make the tiles and chips floating surfaces (`bg-popover` with `border-border-floating` and a shadow, or a `floating` Button) so they lift off the wash; soft stays light in dark mode too, so the same composition holds in both.

Do not put text straight on soft art with `text-overlay-foreground` ink. Soft is a light ground in every mode, so overlay ink washes out on it; put the content on a Card or a chip over the art, or use the default vivid intensity for a short overlay label.

Do not put body text over it. The art spans the palette's lightest and most saturated tones, so no single ink is guaranteed to clear contrast across it; reserve overlays for a short label on a scrim or an avatar's initials.

Do not pass colours, and reach for `tones` rarely. The art follows the preset's --art-* tokens on purpose; to change how a product's art looks, set the --theme-art-* hooks in its theme or preset, so every cover, banner and avatar changes together.
Do not use it as a page or hero background. It paints at the element's pixel size, so a full-viewport instance costs a large frame on every theme change; it is sized for covers, banners and tiles.

props.name: variant
props.description: mesh: soft spots of colour pulled together by gentle waves. grain: glowing light over deep corners with a printed texture.

props.name: tones
props.description: Paint these `--tone-*` colours instead of the preset's art palette. Leave unset to follow the preset's art direction.

props.name: seed
props.description: Fixes the composition: the same seed paints the same art in every theme. Pass a stable id.

props.name: intensity
props.description: vivid: the preset's art at full strength. soft: every colour and the ground lifted to a light pastel of itself (high lightness, half chroma) — a wash for header bands and for staging chips and logo tiles, light in both modes.

props.name: children
props.description: Rendered above the art — initials, a glyph, a short label.

props.name: className
props.description: Size and shape: aspect, height, rounding.

motion.why: The shader frame fades in over the CSS gradient it replaces, so the swap from fallback to shader reads as the art settling rather than a flash.
Artwork, not a control: it does not react to the pointer.
A theme change repaints the frame in place on the next animation frame; there are no states to move between.
Static by design: nothing animates between paints, so it costs nothing while idle and respects reduced motion without a branch.

a11y: Decorative by default: the canvas is aria-hidden. When the art stands for something (an avatar), label the element that contains it, not the art.
Children render above the art in the normal reading order, so initials or a label are announced as usual.

components.name: InlineStatus
components.summary: A borderless single-line status message — a leading semantic icon + one line of text over the canonical tone scale (neutral/info/success/warning/destructive). The non-boxed sibling of Note for inline affirmations, errors, and progress; pass a custom icon (e.g. a Spinner) for a pending row.

usage.description: Use InlineStatus for short state messages placed near the thing they describe.

bestPractices.description: Use it beside inputs, rows, actions, or settings that need local status.
Keep the message brief and pair color with text.
Do not use InlineStatus for global announcements or page-level alerts.
Do not use tone as the only signal. Colour alone fails for colour-blind users — the leading icon is what carries the meaning, so never hide it.

props.name: tone
props.description: Severity tone — drives the leading icon (name + color) and the text color. The shared status-tone vocabulary (STATUS_TONES).

props.name: size
props.description: Text size: sm (text-body-sm) or md (text-body-md). sm is the default for inline placement under a control; md matches surrounding body copy.

props.name: icon
props.description: Override the leading glyph (e.g. a <Spinner />); otherwise the tone selects it.

a11y: Color reinforces, never replaces, meaning — the leading icon and the message text carry the status.
For a live status (e.g. a form submit result), render it in an aria-live region or pair it with the field's error wiring so the change is announced.

examples.label: Tones
examples.code: <Stack gap={1}><InlineStatus tone="success">Top-up confirmed.</InlineStatus><InlineStatus tone="destructive">Insufficient balance.</InlineStatus></Stack>

examples.label: Pending (custom icon)
examples.code: <InlineStatus tone="neutral" icon={<Spinner size="sm" />}>Preparing transaction…</InlineStatus>

components.name: Input
components.summary: Styled native text input. Soft-square (rounded-sm), the theme's field surface (outlined or filled), 2px focus ring; aria-invalid raises the destructive error treatment.

usage.description: Use Input for short freeform text, search, email, password, file, and native input types. In forms, wrap Input in Field so label, description, required state, and validation messaging stay accessible and consistent.

bestPractices.description: Pair every Input with a visible label through Field or an explicit label/htmlFor connection.
Use type, inputMode, autoComplete, and placeholder as progressive hints, not as the only label.
Set aria-invalid or use Field error copy when validation fails.

Keep a focusable field at 16px or larger on mobile. iOS Safari zooms the whole page when a focused input computes under 16px and never zooms back out. Input handles this itself — below the sm breakpoint it renders text-body-lg (17px) and returns to text-body-md at sm and up. Build a custom field the same way: a second paired tier under a max-sm: variant, never a hand-set font-size.

Choose outlined or filled fields once, in the theme: `--theme-field: var(--muted)` with `--theme-field-border: transparent` turns every Input, Textarea, Select, Combobox, SearchInput, InputGroup and ChatComposer into a borderless filled well; unset, they are outlined on the card. Every field reads the `field` / `field-border` pair, so they change together.
Restyle one Input as a filled chip with `bg-muted border-transparent`. It drifts from every other field on the page, and the theme can no longer move them together; set the field tokens instead.
Override an Input's type with a page tier below 16px (text-body-md, text-body-sm, text-label-*) without a >=16px mobile arm — that reintroduces the iOS focus zoom.
Use placeholder text as the label; it disappears once the user types and is not enough context.
Use Input for long body copy. Use Textarea for multi-line content.

anatomy.name: Input
anatomy.description: The native input element with Sable surface, disabled, focus, and invalid styling.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Usually provided by Field or a separate Label. It gives the input its visible purpose.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Optional helper copy connected through aria-describedby when using Field.

anatomy.name: Error
anatomy.description: Validation message paired with aria-invalid and destructive styling.

props.name: size
props.description: md is the form field. xs is the dense inset field of a tool panel (an inset panel-field fill, no outline, tight padding) — the same ladder as Select and Combobox. Use it instead of overriding the height with className.

props.name: type
props.description: Native input type (text, email, password, search, number, file, …). type="file" themes the native selector button via file: token utilities.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the control and blocks pointer interaction.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Surfaces the destructive border + ring. Base UI form fields set this automatically.

props.name: ...props
props.description: All native input attributes (placeholder, value, onChange, ref, …) pass through.

a11y: Renders a native <input> — labels, keyboard, and form semantics come for free.
Renders through Base UI's Input (Field.Control): inside a Field it picks up the label, description, error and validity wiring from context, even when nested in a wrapper.
Always associate a <label htmlFor> (or wrap) — placeholder text is not a label.
Focus-visible ring uses the --ring token at 40% opacity.
Set aria-invalid='true' on error so the destructive treatment is conveyed, not color-only.

components.name: InputGroup
components.summary: An Input with addons inside the same field: a prefix or suffix ("https://", ".com", "$"), an icon, or a borderless Button such as copy or reveal. One shell, one focus ring, one error state; a Field's label and error wiring reaches the Input inside.

usage.description: Use InputGroup when something belongs inside the field with the text: a unit, a fixed prefix, an icon, or a small action on the value itself (copy, reveal, clear). Use Field's `trailing` for an action beside the field (Apply next to a promo code), SearchInput for search, and NumberField for numbers with steppers.

bestPractices.description: Keep text addons short and fixed ("https://", "kg", "USD"). They are part of the field, not its label.
For a button addon, use a borderless Button (`variant="ghost"`, `size="icon-sm"`) with an aria-label. The addon tightens around it, so it sits as far from the edge as from the top and bottom.
Wrap the group in Field for a label and errors: `<Field label="Website"><InputGroup leading="https://"><Input /></InputGroup></Field>`.
Do not put the value's meaning only in an addon. A screen reader hears the label and the text, so "Price (USD)" belongs in the label too.
Do not restyle an Input to fake an addon; the group owns the border, the fill and the ring.

props.name: leading
props.description: Inside the field, before the text: a prefix ("https://", "$"), an icon, or a borderless Button.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Inside the field, after the text: a suffix (".com", "kg"), an icon, or a borderless Button (copy, reveal, clear).

props.name: children
props.description: The single `<Input />`. It keeps its own props and type; the group takes over its border, fill and focus ring.

props.name: id / required / disabled / aria-describedby / aria-invalid
props.description: Forwarded to the Input, not set on the group. This is how a Field's wiring reaches the text box when the group is its child.

props.name: className
props.description: Layout classes for the group (width, margins).

motion.why: It arrives with the form it belongs to. A field that animated in on its own would be briefly unusable for no stated reason.
The shell owns one focus ring for the input and its addons and eases it in, so focusing the text, or tabbing to a copy button inside the field, reads as the one field taking focus.
An invalid value turns the shell's edge destructive on the same ease, so the error lands as the field changing state rather than a red box swapping in.
A field does no work of its own. A pending check (an availability lookup) puts a Spinner in `trailing`, which is where its answer will appear.

a11y: The Input stays the focusable control; the group draws the focus ring around the whole field while it is focused.
Inside a Field, the label, description and error are wired to the Input itself, not the group.
Text addons are plain text beside the input, read in order; put a unit or currency in the label as well so it is not only visual.
A button addon is a real Button with its own focus stop and needs an aria-label.
