components.name: NumberTicker
components.summary: A number that rolls to its new value digit by digit, like an odometer. Formatted with Intl.NumberFormat (currency, percent, compact, any locale); separators, signs and units hold still while each digit column turns, and a digit that appears or goes away eases its width so nothing around it jumps. At rest on first paint; under subtle or reduced motion the value simply updates.

usage.description: Use NumberTicker for a figure that changes in place while someone is looking at it — a dashboard total after a filter changes, a live count, a price as a plan's options change, a score. The roll says "this number moved, and by roughly this much"; the reader sees the change happen instead of noticing, later, that a number is different.

bestPractices.description: Use it for the headline figure that a control on the same screen changes — the total above a chart, the price beside a quantity stepper — so cause and effect are seen together.
Format through `format` (currency, percent, compact) rather than pre-formatting a string, so separators and units stay put while only the digits roll.
Pass `aria-live="polite"` only when the change itself is news the reader would otherwise miss; most tickers sit beside the control that changed them and need no announcement.
Do not use it for values that change many times a second (a stopwatch, a stock tick, a progress percentage) — the rolls never land and read as a blur. Render the number as plain tabular text.
Do not use it for numbers that are names rather than amounts — an order ID, a phone number, a year, a version. Rolling implies a quantity going up or down.
Do not animate a number on page load to make it feel alive. The first paint is at rest on purpose; for an entrance, reveal the card it sits in (the Reveal motion primitive).
Do not use it for a value inside a known range that needs a picture of how full it is — show a Meter, with the number beside it.

props.name: value
props.description: The number to show. When it changes, the digits roll to it.

props.name: format
props.description: How to write the number — `{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }`, `{ style: "percent" }`, `{ notation: "compact" }`, fraction digits. Passed to Intl.NumberFormat; an inline object is fine (it is compared by value).

props.name: locales
props.description: BCP 47 locale(s) for the formatting. Digits roll through the locale's own numbering system.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Before the number. A string becomes part of the number's text (and rolls in or out with it); an element is rendered as given.

props.name: suffix
props.description: After the number ("+", " pts"). A string becomes part of the number's text; an element is rendered as given.

props.name: trend
props.description: Which way the digits roll. `auto` rolls up as the value grows and down as it shrinks; `up` / `down` fix it (a countdown, a score that only climbs).

props.name: motion
props.description: How much motion this component uses: `full` (default) inherits the app's policy, `subtle` keeps feedback and drops the flourish, `off` stills it. It can only turn motion down — it never overrides a reader's reduce-motion setting. The roll is expressive, so `subtle` updates the value in place.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root span. Set the type tier here (`text-heading-2`, `text-display-lg`); the ticker adds tabular figures so widths hold still.

props.name: ...span props
props.description: Remaining span attributes pass through to the root — `aria-live` to announce changes, `id`, data attributes.

motion.why: The first paint is at rest. A number counting up on page load is decoration that delays the reading; the roll is kept for the moment the value actually changes.
It is a reading, not a control; the control that changes it gives the feedback.

Each digit column turns to its new place on the expressive roll (the slower token, emphasized easing, staggered from the ones column), and arriving or departing columns ease their width. The roll is what shows a change happened and how big it was — the hundreds turning reads as a bigger move than the ones. No recipe can translate per-digit columns, so it is custom; it is multiplied by --motion-expressive, so `subtle` and reduced motion land the value at once.
A number has no working state; show a Skeleton while it loads.

a11y: The whole written number (with any string prefix or suffix) is real text in a visually hidden span; the rolling columns are aria-hidden and draw their glyphs as generated content, so screen readers, find-in-page and copy all get "$1,234.50", never a stack of digits.

It is not a live region by default — a figure that changes because the reader moved a control is already where their attention is. Pass `aria-live="polite"` when a change elsewhere should be announced.
Tabular figures keep every digit the same width, so a roll never shifts the text around it.

examples.code: <NumberTicker value={1284} className="text-heading-2" />

examples.code: <NumberTicker value={92} suffix=" pts" motion="subtle" />

components.name: OtpField
components.summary: One-time-code entry over Base UI's OTP Field — one slot per character, SMS autofill on the first slot, paste fills every slot, and only one tab stop for the whole code.

usage.description: Use OtpField for a short, fixed-length code the user copies from somewhere else — an SMS or email verification code, an authenticator app, a device pairing PIN. The slots show how long the code is and where the user is in it, which a plain Input cannot.

bestPractices.description: Set `length` to the exact length the server sends, and verify in `onValueComplete` (or with `autoSubmit` inside a form). Most users paste or autofill the whole code at once, so the moment of completion is the natural submit.
Label it through a `Field` ("Verification code") and say where the code was sent in the description. The first slot takes the field's name; the rest are announced by position.
Use `groupSize` for codes of 6 or more so the user can check the code in chunks against the message they are reading from.

Do not use OtpField for a password, an arbitrary-length PIN, or anything the user types from memory. Slots promise a fixed length; use Input with `type="password"` and `autocomplete="current-password"` instead.

Clear the error as soon as the user edits the code (`onValueChange` → reset the error), and set it again when the next code is refused. Each refusal is then a fresh change to invalid, so the field shakes for every wrong code, not only the first.

Do not intercept paste or clear the field on a wrong code before the user has seen the error. Blocking paste breaks SMS autofill and password managers, and wiping the slots erases the evidence of which digit was wrong.
Do not swap it for NumberField because the code is digits. A code is an identifier, not a quantity: NumberField strips leading zeros and offers steppers that make no sense here.

anatomy.name: Root
anatomy.description: A role=group that holds the value, carries the field label and description, and reports completion.

anatomy.name: Slot
anatomy.description: One input per character. The first carries autocomplete="one-time-code" and accepts the whole code.

anatomy.name: Group gap
anatomy.description: A decorative dash inserted every `groupSize` slots; hidden from assistive tech.

props.name: length
props.description: Number of character slots. Completion fires when every slot is filled.

props.name: groupSize
props.description: Insert a visual gap every N slots (3 renders 123 – 456). The value stays one contiguous string.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled / uncontrolled code.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on every edit. `details.reason` is input-change, input-clear, input-paste or keyboard.

props.name: onValueComplete
props.description: Fires once every slot is filled — the place to verify the code. Also fires when a complete code is pasted over a complete value.

props.name: onValueInvalid
props.description: Fires when typed or pasted text contains characters `validationType` rejects, so you can explain the rejection rather than letting it vanish.

props.name: validationType
props.description: Which characters a slot accepts. Also picks the virtual keyboard (numeric → number pad).

props.name: autoSubmit
props.description: Submit the owning form when the code becomes complete.

props.name: mask
props.description: Render slots as password inputs. Only for codes that are secret on screen, such as a card PIN.

props.name: getSlotLabel
props.description: Accessible name for slots after the first. Override to localize.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Marks every slot invalid (destructive border and digits). Turning it on after mount shakes the field once. `<Field error>` sets it for you.

props.name: motion
props.description: How much motion this component uses: `full` (default) inherits the app's policy, `subtle` keeps feedback and drops the flourish, `off` stills it. It can only turn motion down — it never overrides a reader's reduce-motion setting. The shake is the flourish; the destructive colour stays at every level.

props.name: disabled / readOnly / required / name / id / form
props.description: Standard form-control props. `id` lands on the first slot, so `<Field>` and `<label htmlFor>` name the field.

motion.why: A code field is part of the form it sits in and appears with it. Animating it in would delay the one thing the user arrived to do — paste the code they just copied.
Focus moves between slots on every keystroke. The eased ring and border are what let the eye follow the cursor across six identical boxes instead of hunting for it after each digit.
A filled slot strengthens its border, so a pasted code visibly lands in every slot at once. Easing it reads as the code arriving rather than the field flickering.

A refused code shakes the field once as it turns invalid — the short horizontal no that makes a second wrong code feel noticed rather than ignored. It never carries the refusal alone: the digits and borders turn destructive and the Field says why. It plays on the change to invalid, not on mount, and is expressive, so `subtle` keeps only the colour.
Verifying the code is the form's work, not the field's. Show it on the submit Button's `loading` state, where the user expects the answer to appear.

a11y: The root is a role=group named by the field label; the first slot shares the label through `id`/`htmlFor`, and later slots are announced by position ("Character 2 of 6").
Only one slot is in the tab order. Arrow keys, Home/End and Backspace move between slots; Tab leaves the whole field.
The first slot carries autocomplete="one-time-code" and the numeric virtual keyboard, so iOS and Android offer the SMS code above the keyboard.
Slots render at 20px (`text-mono-lg`), above the 16px floor that stops iOS Safari zooming on focus.

An invalid code is never signalled by motion alone: every slot carries aria-invalid, the digits and borders turn destructive, and the Field's error message is wired through aria-describedby. The shake resolves instantly under reduced motion and `subtle`.

examples.label: Six digits
examples.code: <Field label="Verification code"><OtpField length={6} onValueComplete={verify} /></Field>

examples.label: In a field, grouped
examples.code: <Field label="Verification code" description="Enter the 6-digit code we sent to your phone."><OtpField length={6} groupSize={3} /></Field>

examples.label: With an error
examples.code: <Field label="Verification code" error="That code has expired. Request a new code and try again."><OtpField length={6} groupSize={3} defaultValue="482913" /></Field>

examples.label: Verify on completion, shake on a wrong code
Alphanumeric
examples.code: <Field label="Pairing code"><OtpField length={8} groupSize={4} validationType="alphanumeric" /></Field>

components.name: OverflowMenu
components.summary: An overflow ellipsis icon button that opens a Menu. Composes our Menu + Button + Icon — pass MenuItems as children and it wires the ghost icon trigger, accessible label, and portal-rendered content. All keyboard, focus, and dismissal behavior comes through Menu.

usage.description: Use OverflowMenu for compact overflow actions when the primary action is already visible elsewhere.

bestPractices.description: Use it for secondary commands that belong to a row, card, or toolbar item.
Keep labels explicit so the icon-only trigger does not obscure the command meaning.

For actions that fit inline on a wide screen but not a narrow one, render them twice: inline (a Row inside a wrapper shown from a container width; Row sets its own display, so the wrapper does the hiding), and as MenuItems in an OverflowMenu hidden from that width (`@container` + `@md:`). display:none takes the hidden copy out of the accessibility tree, so only one set is ever announced. Keep the primary action inline at every width.
Do not hide the most important or most frequent action inside OverflowMenu.
Do not use it as the only affordance on a touch surface. It is revealed on hover in most layouts, and hover does not exist on touch — pair it with a visible action or make it always-visible there.

props.name: children
props.description: The menu rows — MenuItem / MenuSeparator / MenuGroup, etc. Rendered inside MenuContent.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of the popup along its side. Overflow menus typically right-align under the trigger; 'start' anchors the popup's left edge to the trigger instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label (aria-label) for the icon-only trigger button.

props.name: icon
props.description: Semantic icon name rendered in the trigger, always at the solid weight.

props.name: size
props.description: The trigger's rung on the icon-button ladder. 'icon' for a card or page header; 'icon-sm' or 'icon-xs' in a list row or dense toolbar, so the trigger does not set the row height.

a11y: The icon-only trigger is labeled via aria-label (label prop, default 'More actions').
Menu provides role=menu/menuitem, roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and typeahead via Base UI.
Esc and outside-press dismiss; focus returns to the trigger on close.

examples.label: Basic
examples.code: <OverflowMenu label="Post actions"><MenuItem>Edit</MenuItem><MenuItem>Share</MenuItem><MenuSeparator /><MenuItem variant="destructive">Delete</MenuItem></OverflowMenu>

components.name: PageHeader
components.summary: In-flow page heading block: a title row (optional back control + actions) over an optional description, with room for children (filters, tabs) below.

usage.description: Use PageHeader to establish a page's title, supporting description, and primary page actions.

bestPractices.description: Use one PageHeader per major page or route.
Keep the title literal and put explanation in the lede or nearby content.

Use size="lg" for an editorial page (a personal site, a marketing page, an article index): a display-tier title over a body-lg lede. Pair it with SectionHeader size="lg" for the sections below, so the steps stay display → heading-2 → body.

Use size="lg" on product routes (settings, lists, dashboards). Display type is never product chrome: there it competes with the content it frames. Keep md, and do not restyle the title with a display class through className either.
Do not use PageHeader inside repeated cards, dialogs, or compact panels.
Do not use a second PageHeader for a section of the page. It is the route's one h1; each section below it takes a SectionHeader (an h2 with the same title row, description and actions).
Do not put it outside the Region that holds the page content. It then sits at a different measure from what it introduces, and the page reads as two documents.

props.name: title
props.description: The page title (renders an <h1>).

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting copy beneath the title.

props.name: back
props.description: Leading element before the title — typically a back control on drill-in routes. Keep it a ghost icon Button (size="icon", variant="ghost", aria-label="Back") so it stays quieter than the title. A ghost back control bleeds by its inset at the start, so its glyph lines up with the content edge below (Button bleed="none" opts out).

props.name: actions
props.description: Trailing actions aligned to the title row's end. They drop under the title when the title would have less than 20rem beside them (on a phone, nearly always), and the title wraps rather than truncating. A ghost or link Button at either end of the group bleeds by its own padding, so its label meets the content edge (the end on the title row, the start once wrapped); filled buttons keep their edge on the line. Direct children only.

props.name: titleAs
props.description: The title's heading element. Keep h1 — the route's one h1. Use h2 only when something above already owns the h1: a shell that renders the route title, or a page showing a PageHeader as an example.

props.name: size
props.description: The title's scale. md: text-heading-2 over a text-body-sm description, for product pages. lg: text-display-lg over a text-body-lg lede capped at the prose measure, with more space between and below, for an editorial page (personal site, marketing page, article index). Beside actions or a back control, a title line taller than the controls lifts by half the difference, so its first line stays centred on them.

a11y: Renders the title as an <h1>; use one PageHeader per page.

Its title renders the route's `h1`. Do not render another `h1` elsewhere on the page: heading navigation would report two documents, and the outline a screen-reader user builds from it stops matching the page.

examples.label: With actions
examples.code: <PageHeader title="Storage credits" description="Fund permanent storage." actions={<Button>Top up</Button>} />

examples.label: Editorial page title (size lg)
examples.code: <PageHeader size="lg" title="Field notes" description="Essays on making things slowly, from a studio by the sea." actions={<Button variant="outline">Subscribe</Button>} />

examples.label: One per page, inside the region

components.name: PageLoader
components.summary: Full-screen branded loading splash: the screen fades in, the mark breathes, and an indeterminate Progress bar pulses beneath it. All motion is token-driven, so it freezes to a calm static screen when motion is off/reduced.

usage.description: Use PageLoader for full-route or full-page pending states where the entire view is not ready yet.

bestPractices.description: Use it during route transitions, auth checks, or initial data loading.
Prefer a clear page-level message when the wait may take noticeable time.
Do not use PageLoader for small inline waits; use Spinner, an indeterminate Progress, or Skeleton.
Do not leave it mounted if the route's data can fail. It covers the whole viewport, so a PageLoader that never resolves is indistinguishable from a hung application — always give it a failure path.

props.name: children
props.description: Brand mark / logo shown at center. Falls back to a neutral pulsing mark.

props.name: label
props.description: Caption beneath the mark; also the accessible label on the role=status region.

props.name: fullscreen
props.description: Cover the viewport (fixed) vs fill the nearest positioned parent (absolute).

props.name: hideBar
props.description: Hide the indeterminate Progress bar under the mark.

a11y: role=status with an aria-label (the label prop) announces the loading state politely.
Decorative mark and bar are aria-hidden.
Motion respects the policy: under off/reduced the pulses hold their first frame (static).

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: Page navigation built from our own Button + Icon (no Base UI). A <nav aria-label='Pagination'> with prev/next icon buttons that disable at the bounds and numbered page buttons; the current page is a secondary button marked aria-current. With pageLink every control is a real link (crawlable, opens in a new tab, any router through render). Collapses to first/last/current plus a sibling window, bridging skipped runs with an ellipsis.

usage.description: Use Pagination when a result set is split into discrete pages and the user needs predictable movement through them. Pair it with DataTable, list results, or server-paged views; use a load-more Button or infinite scroll when page numbers are not meaningful.

bestPractices.description: Keep page state controlled by the parent route or data layer so URL, filters, and result fetches stay in sync.
Use a specific label when multiple pagers appear on a page, such as "Customer pages".

Pass pageLink when the page lives in the URL (search results, a blog, a catalogue): each page becomes a link a crawler can follow and a reader can open in a new tab. Use a router's Link there so navigation stays in the app.
Reset to page 1 when filters or search terms materially change the result set.
Use Pagination for tiny lists where all items fit comfortably on one page.
Hide disabled previous/next buttons at the bounds; disabled controls make the current position clearer.

anatomy.name: Nav
anatomy.description: The labelled pagination landmark.

anatomy.name: Previous/next
anatomy.description: Icon buttons for adjacent page movement, disabled at the bounds.

anatomy.name: Page buttons
anatomy.description: Numbered buttons with aria-current on the active page.

anatomy.name: Ellipsis
anatomy.description: Non-interactive marker for skipped page ranges.

props.name: page
props.description: The active page (1-based). Clamped into the valid range.

props.name: total
props.description: Total number of pages.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Called with the next page when a control is activated. No-op for out-of-range or unchanged values. Optional with pageLink, where the URL is the page state.

props.name: pageLink
props.description: Render each page control as a link: return the element for a page, (page) => <a href={`?page=${page}`} /> or a router's <Link to={`?page=${page}`} />. The current page keeps aria-current; previous/next at the bounds stay disabled buttons. onPageChange becomes optional and, if set, still fires on click.

props.name: siblingCount
props.description: Page buttons shown on each side of the current page before the list collapses into ellipses. First and last pages are always shown.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label applied to the surrounding nav element.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the nav.

a11y: Renders a landmark <nav> with aria-label so assistive tech can jump to the pager.
The current page button carries aria-current='page'.
Prev/next buttons are real <button>s with aria-label and become disabled at the bounds.
With pageLink the controls are real <a> links (or the router's), so they are crawlable and open in a new tab; a bound arrow stays a disabled button rather than a link to nowhere.
Ellipsis slots are aria-hidden — they convey no navigable target.

const [page, setPage] = useState(1)
<Pagination page={page} total={10} onPageChange={setPage} />

examples.label: Many pages (ellipsis)

<Pagination page={page} total={20} onPageChange={setPage} />

examples.label: Table results footer
examples.code: <Stack gap={2}><DataTable data={rows} columns={columns} rowKey={(row) => row.id} /><Pagination label="Customer pages" page={page} total={12} onPageChange={setPage} /></Stack>

examples.label: Page links (URL is the state)
examples.code: <Pagination page={page} total={pageCount} pageLink={(page) => <Link to={`/search?q=${query}&page=${page}`} />} />

import { Pagination } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<Pagination page={page} total={pageCount} onPageChange={(next) => { setPage(next); loadPage(next) }} />

components.name: PanelGroup
components.summary: A row of docked chrome panels around a flexible centre, with draggable and keyboard-resizable edges and optional persisted widths.

usage.description: Use PanelGroup for the body of a tool workspace: fixed-width Panels docked left and/or right, a flexible Panel in the middle for the canvas, and a PanelResizer between them. Panels scroll internally and the group never scrolls. This is the workspace-register counterpart to SplitPane, which only switches between side-by-side and stacked at a breakpoint and cannot be resized.

bestPractices.description: Give every docked Panel a fixed width and leave the centre Panel width-less so it absorbs the remaining space.
Drive the width with usePanelWidth and pass a storageKey, so a user's layout survives a reload. Spread its bounds onto the PanelResizer rather than repeating min and max by hand.
Label every Panel — they are landmarks, and 'Layers' or 'Properties' is what a screen-reader user navigates by.

Decide what each docked Panel becomes on a phone with `narrow`: "sheet" for an inspector or a navigation rail the user opens on demand, "hidden" for chrome a phone does without. Drive a sheet's `open` from the same state that selects the record, so selecting a row opens the inspector at every width.
Render the same inspector twice, once in a Panel and once in a Sheet behind a hand-rolled viewport check. `narrow="sheet"` renders the content once, in whichever place applies.
Let the group scroll. Only panels and the canvas scroll; a scrolling group means the shell lost its height constraint.
Use it for page content columns — that's Grid or Columns. PanelGroup is chrome, and it sits outside the content grid.
Omit PanelResizer to save effort and then let users live with a fixed panel. If a panel holds a tree or a property grid, its width is a preference.

anatomy.name: PanelGroup
anatomy.description: The flex row. Sets min-h-0/min-w-0 so children can actually shrink and scroll.

anatomy.name: Panel
anatomy.description: One column. Fixed-width when `width` is set, flexible otherwise. Scrolls internally.

anatomy.name: PanelResizer
anatomy.description: The draggable edge between two panels: a 1px hairline with a wider hit area, operable by pointer and keyboard.

subcomponents.name: Panel
subcomponents.type: { label: string; width?: number; scroll?: boolean; narrow?: "dock" | "sheet" | "hidden"; open?: boolean; onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void; side?: "left" | "right"; below?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" }
subcomponents.description: A docked or flexible column. Below `below` (default lg, where Sidebar and BottomNav swap), `narrow` decides what it becomes: "dock" (default) stays docked, "sheet" renders the same content once inside a Sheet from `side` (default "right"; a panel before the canvas is "left"), titled by `label`, open while `open` is true and closed through `onOpenChange` (Esc, scrim, swipe), and "hidden" drops it. `open` defaults to true docked (false removes the column, so the canvas takes its width) and false as a sheet. Crossing the breakpoint remounts the content, so keep state that must survive it in the app. `label` names the landmark; omit `width` for the flexible centre. `scroll` defaults to true — set it false for a header + scrolling body + pinned footer, so the footer doesn't scroll away with the list. When you own the layout, give the header and footer shrink-0 and the middle min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto. overflow-y-auto only activates if every flex ancestor can shrink: a single missing min-h-0 anywhere up the chain makes the panel grow instead of scroll, and nothing reports it.

subcomponents.name: PanelResizer
subcomponents.type: { side: 'left' | 'right'; width: number; onWidthChange: (n: number) => void; label: string; min?: number; max?: number; step?: number }
subcomponents.description: The draggable edge. `side` says which side the resized panel is on, so the drag delta's sign is right.

subcomponents.name: usePanelWidth
subcomponents.type: (defaultWidth: number, options?: { storageKey?: string; min?: number; max?: number }) => readonly [number, (n: number) => void, { min: number; max: number }]
subcomponents.description: Controlled width for a Panel, clamped and optionally persisted to localStorage (only when `storageKey` is passed). Read through useSyncExternalStore, so there is no server/client hydration mismatch and no setState in an effect; do not hand-roll a localStorage read during render or a write from an effect. Without `storageKey` the width is kept in memory per hook instance. The third element is the `{ min, max }` it clamps to: spread it onto the paired PanelResizer so the separator's aria-valuemin/max and Home/End match the real clamp.

motion.why: Panels are the app's frame, present from first paint. A dock that slid in on load would make the workspace look like it is still assembling.
The hairline widens into a visible bar on hover and turns primary on keyboard focus, eased, so a 1px edge says it can be grabbed before the pointer commits.

Width tracks the pointer one-to-one while dragging, and keyboard steps land at once. An eased width would trail the cursor, and resizing is a layout change: easing it would reflow the canvas beside the panel on every frame.
Layout chrome has no working state.

a11y: PanelResizer is a role=separator with aria-orientation, aria-valuenow/min/max, and is focusable — a pointer-only resizer is a keyboard trap.
Arrow keys resize by `step`; Home and End jump to the minimum and maximum.
Each Panel renders an <aside> with an accessible name from `label`, so panels are navigable landmarks.

components.name: PanelSection
components.summary: A flush group of property rows inside a docked panel — eyebrow header, hairline separator, rows beneath. The workspace register's answer to Card, which does not belong in a panel.

usage.description: Use PanelSection to group properties inside an inspector or docked panel, with PropertyRow for one label-plus-control line and PropertyPair for two controls side by side. This is the workspace register's grouping primitive: it separates with a hairline and nothing else, because a Card inside a 240px panel spends its border and inset on nothing and pushes every row inward.

bestPractices.description: Group related properties under a short functional title — Blending, Layout, Fill — the way a tool inspector names its sections.
Reach for PropertyPair before giving each property its own full-width row; pairing halves the vertical cost in a narrow panel.
Put a section-scoped control (a visibility toggle, an add action) in the action slot rather than inventing a second header row.
Wrap panel content in Card. Cards are page-register furniture; in a panel they read as a page pasted into chrome.
Repeat the panel's own title as the section title. If the header above already names the selection, title the section by what it controls (Parameters, Blending).

Hand-roll a property line (`
Opacity
`). Use PropertyRow for every label-plus-control line: when each property type invents its own arrangement, a panel of fifteen properties ends up with fifteen layouts.
Use PropertyRow for page forms — use Field, which carries label/description/error semantics. PropertyRow is a dense chrome row, not a form control.

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: The section title in the UI section tier, with an optional trailing action.

anatomy.name: PropertyRow
anatomy.description: One property: label left, control right. `stacked` moves the control to its own line for full-width controls.

anatomy.name: PropertyPair
anatomy.description: Two controls side by side, with optional captions above each.

anatomy.name: PropertyGroup
anatomy.description: A set of properties folded behind one row that names the group and summarises its value, opening with +/− to the controls beneath.

props.name: title
props.description: Section name, rendered as the header in the UI section tier.

props.name: action
props.description: Optional trailing control in the header — a visibility toggle, an add action.

subcomponents.name: PropertyRow
subcomponents.type: { label: ReactNode; htmlFor?: string; hint?: string; stacked?: boolean; scrub?: { value, onValueChange, step?, min?, max?, onGestureStart?, onGestureEnd?, disabled? } }
subcomponents.description: One property line. `hint` becomes the label's hover explanation; `stacked` puts the control on its own line. `scrub` makes the property NAME a drag handle for its value — the Figma/Framer/Paper convention, and the answer for a numeric row with no honest glyph to put in a ScrubField (a schema-generated `levels` or `seed`, where a `#` would be noise pretending to be meaning). Opt-in and additive: a row without it is unchanged. The label stays a real `<label htmlFor>` — a 2px jitter threshold keeps a click a click, and the click synthesised after a real drag is swallowed so a scrub does not also select the field's text.

subcomponents.name: PropertyPair
subcomponents.description: Two controls side by side in a 2-up grid, with optional captions above each.

subcomponents.name: PropertyGroup
subcomponents.type: { label: ReactNode; summary?: ReactNode; defaultOpen?: boolean; open?: boolean; onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void }
subcomponents.description: A collapsible set of properties inside a section, at the panel's scale (an Accordion is page furniture). The row shows the label, then the summary (the group's value, readable while closed: a word, a few swatches, or both), then a + that turns to − when open. Groups open independently and stack with a hairline between them. Built on Collapsible.

motion.why: Sections are part of the inspector they sit in and arrive with it. Animating each in would make a panel switch look like a page load.
The fold row eases its focus ring, so arrowing down a dense inspector shows where the keyboard is without the ring flickering from row to row.
The group opens by easing its height, so the rows below slide down to make room instead of jumping. In an inspector, the next section moving is otherwise how you lose your place.
The + collapses into − as the group opens, both glyphs stacked as one mark, so the indicator reads as this row changing state rather than a different icon landing.
The inspector edits values in place; nothing in it loads.

a11y: PropertyGroup's row is a real button with aria-expanded (Collapsible); its summary is part of the button's name, so a closed group still announces its value.
PropertyRow renders a real <label>; pass htmlFor with the control's id so clicking the label focuses it.
The section title is an h3, so panels contribute a real heading outline rather than styled divs.
`hint` is exposed as the label's title attribute — keep the essential meaning in the label itself, since title text is not reliably announced.

A `scrub` label does not replace keyboard editing and must not be the only way to set the value: the drag is a pointer affordance, so the control it names still has to accept typing and arrow keys. It also keeps its `htmlFor` behaviour, which is the reason the gesture arms on a 2px threshold rather than on pointerdown.

examples.label: Groups that fold behind their value

<PanelSection title="Color">
  <PropertyGroup label="Tones" summary="Brand only">
    <PropertyRow label="Scheme">
      <Select value="brand">
        <SelectTrigger size="xs" />
        <SelectContent>
          <SelectItem value="brand">Brand only</SelectItem>
          <SelectItem value="harmonize">Harmonize</SelectItem>
        </SelectContent>
      </Select>
    </PropertyRow>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <PropertyGroup label="Grid" summary="8px">
    <PropertyRow label="Size">
      <ScrubField label="Grid size" value={8} min={1} max={64} suffix="px" />
    </PropertyRow>
  </PropertyGroup>
</PanelSection>

components.name: Phone
components.summary: A current smartphone frame at iPhone proportions: a dark body with a titanium band, thin bezels, an island, an optional status bar and a scrollable screen.

usage.description: Use Phone to frame a mobile product preview when the device context is useful.

bestPractices.description: Use it for mobile UI demos, screenshots, and responsive previews.
Keep the framed content legible and avoid stuffing full desktop layouts into the phone frame.
Do not use Phone as a generic panel, card, or production app shell.
Do not use it to test responsive behaviour. The frame is a fixed aspect box, not a viewport, so media queries inside key off the real window.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered inside the scrollable screen region.

props.name: statusBar
props.description: Draw a status bar (time, signal, battery) across the top of the screen. Turn it off to frame a screenshot that already has one.

props.name: systemChrome
props.description: Draw the camera pill and home indicator. Turn it off when the content draws its own system chrome, such as an iOS prototype framed by PhoneFrame from @sableui/react/ios/preview.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes merged onto the outer wrapper (set the width here; the screen keeps its proportions).

a11y: Purely presentational frame; the screen region scrolls when content overflows. Add headings/landmarks in the content as needed.

The frame's chrome (status bar, camera, buttons) is aria-hidden, so the content inside carries the entire accessible meaning. A screenshot with no alt text makes the whole mockup announce as nothing at all.

components.name: PieChart
components.summary: Parts of a whole as slices: a pie or donut, concentric rings for several measures, a total in the hole, slice labels inside or out, and an active slice that pulls outward. Slices sweep in clockwise as the chart scrolls into view.

usage.description: Use PieChart for a share of one total across two to six categories — traffic sources, a budget split, survey answers. A donut leaves room for the total in the middle (`centerLabel`). With more categories, or to compare values precisely, use BarChart; for a breakdown inside a stat card, SegmentedBar is lighter.

bestPractices.description: Put the total, or the headline slice, in a donut's centerLabel.
Configure slice names, tones and icons with categories, keyed by each slice's value in the data.
Use more than six slices — merge the tail into "Other" or use BarChart.

Use it for data-heavy views — streaming or real-time data, thousands of points, zoom and brushing, trading charts. Those belong on a charting library (Recharts, visx, ECharts); Sable's charts are for dashboards, landing pages and decks.

props.name: data
props.description: One row per slice.

props.name: index
props.description: The datum field naming each slice.

props.name: valueKey
props.description: The datum field holding each slice's amount — or several fields, drawn as concentric rings, outer first.

props.name: label
props.description: What the chart shows. Its accessible name and the caption of the data table assistive tech reads.

props.name: categories
props.type: Record<string, { label?: string; tone?: ChartTone; color?: string; icon?: string }>
props.description: Labels, tones and icons per slice, keyed by the slice's name. Unlisted slices take the tones in order.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the chart. Set a height.

props.name: donut
props.description: Cut out the middle: `true` for a ring at 60% of the radius, or a ratio (0–0.9).

props.name: centerLabel
props.description: A value and caption in the hole of a donut. The value holds the centre and the caption hangs below it. A number is formatted for you: in full up to 9,999, compact from 10,000 (10.2K, 102.1K, 1.2M); pass a string for units.

props.name: separator
props.description: A hairline in the surface colour between slices.

props.name: labels
props.description: Label each slice outside the pie or inside it.

props.name: labelContent
props.description: What a slice label says.

props.name: legend
props.description: Show the legend.

props.name: tooltip
props.type: boolean | { indicator?: "dot" | "line" | "dashed" | "none"; hideLabel?: boolean; labelFormatter?: (label, datum) => ReactNode; showTotal?: boolean }
props.description: Show a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus, or configure it: the row marker, hiding the heading, rewriting it, adding a Total row.

props.name: valueFormatter
props.description: Format values everywhere (axis, labels, tooltip, table) — units like "$12,480". Default: compact on the axis, full elsewhere.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale for default number and date formatting.

props.name: motion
props.description: How much motion this component uses: `full` (default) inherits the app's policy, `subtle` keeps feedback and drops the flourish, `off` stills it. It can only turn motion down — it never overrides a reader's reduce-motion setting. The sweep, the slice morph and the rolling centre number are the flourish; the hover pull-out and dim are the feedback `subtle` keeps.

props.name: animate
props.description: Sweep the slices in clockwise when the chart scrolls into view. `animate={false}` is `motion="subtle"`.
props.deprecated: motion="subtle" (what animate={false} now maps to: no arrival, hover kept) or motion="off"

props.name: activeIndex
props.description: The highlighted row (controlled); `null` for none.

props.name: defaultActiveIndex
props.description: The row highlighted at first — a tooltip already open before anyone hovers.

props.name: onActiveIndexChange
props.description: Called as the pointer or keyboard moves between rows.

motion.why: Once on screen the slices are revealed by a mask that sweeps clockwise from 12 o'clock — the whole is read as it fills. On the motion tokens; reduced motion shows the finished chart. The arrival is expressive: it plays at the full motion level only, so `motion="subtle"` (or a subtle app policy) shows the finished chart while hover feedback stays.
The hovered slice pulls outward and the rest dim at once (mixed toward the surface, not faded); the geometry change itself eases (see transition). Essential: `subtle` keeps it.

A numeric centre value rolls to its new total digit by digit (NumberTicker) when the data changes, so the headline is seen moving with the slices instead of being found different afterwards. Expressive: under `subtle` it updates in place.

Geometry eases from the old shape to the new one through a CSS `d` transition on the motion tokens (no recipe animates path geometry); browsers without `d` transitions update in place. Expressive, like the arrival: under `subtle` new data swaps in place.
A chart has no indeterminate state; show a Skeleton while the data loads.

a11y: The drawing is aria-hidden; the same numbers are in a visually hidden data table (captioned by `label`) that the chart is aria-describedby, so assistive tech reads values, not shapes.

With a tooltip, the chart is one tab stop (role=group, aria-roledescription="chart"): arrow keys, Home and End step through the data, Escape clears, and each step is announced in a polite live region.
Colour is never the only key: series are named in the legend, tooltip and table.

examples.code:
const sources = [
	{ source: "Search", visitors: 275 },
	{ source: "Direct", visitors: 200 },
	{ source: "Social", visitors: 187 },
	{ source: "Email", visitors: 90 },
]

<PieChart
	label="Visitors by source"
	data={sources}
	index="source"
	valueKey="visitors"
	donut
	centerLabel={{ value: 752, label: "Visitors" }}
/>

	valueKey="visitors"
	labels="outside"
	labelContent="percent"
	categories={{ Search: { tone: "primary" }, Email: { tone: "neutral" } }}
/>

components.name: Pill
components.summary: A chip someone clicks: a filter, a tag choice, an option in a row. Always a button with aria-pressed. appearance="solid" (filters; selected lifts onto the primary surface) or "outline" (quiet chips that annotate content, like reactions); size lg, md or sm. A static label is a Badge.

usage.description: Use Pill for a row of filters or choices a person clicks to narrow or toggle what they see. For a label that only describes something, use Badge.

bestPractices.description: Use short text that names the filter or choice.
Reflect the current choice with selected, so the active filter reads at a glance.

In a toolbar where filter chips share a row with a search field ("All 8 · Products 5 · Open source 2 … [Find a project]"), pair Pill size="lg" with SearchInput size="sm", and Button size="sm" for any action beside them. All three stand on --control-sm (32px, 28 compact), the rung the spacing doctrine gives toolbar controls, so the row is one height in either density. Pill md (28px) has no text field of its height in the page register, so md beside a field always reads as a mismatch.
Do not use Pill as a static label. A pressable-looking chip that does nothing is the most common cause of dead clicks in a filter row — that is a Badge.
Do not use Pill for primary actions or important system status.

Do not restyle a Pill with border or background classes to get a quieter chip. That is appearance="outline" (and size="sm" for a small one); an override is a look that exists nowhere else in the system. Likewise never set h-* on a Pill to match a neighbour: pick the size that shares its rung.

props.name: selected
props.description: Marks the pill as chosen. Solid lifts onto the primary surface; outline takes a primary tint and soft primary edge. Sets aria-pressed.

props.name: appearance
props.description: solid for a filter row; outline for quiet chips that annotate other content (a reaction under a message, a tag on a card), where a filled chip would compete with what it annotates.

props.name: size
props.description: lg sits on --control-sm (32px, 28 compact), the toolbar rung it shares with SearchInput sm and Button sm, for a filter row beside a search field. md sits on --control-xs (28px, 24 compact), the chip in a row of its own or among content. sm is a fixed 24px (the target floor, which density does not shrink), for chips under or inside other content.

props.name: tone
props.description: neutral is the chip as described. A palette family colours it as a category, like the choices in a tag picker: a wash at rest, the solid family colour when selected. Painted from the theme's generated palette.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional leading glyph (e.g. <Icon name="lock" />), rendered before the children with the base gap.

motion.why: Pills arrive with the filter row or the content they annotate. A chip that animated in alone would read as a filter someone just added.
The hover wash eases, so sweeping the pointer along a filter row reads as one cursor moving rather than chips flashing in turn.
A pill often toggles a filter that takes a moment to reach the results; the settle on press confirms the click landed before they change.
`selected` lifts the chip onto its selected surface on the same ease, so toggling reads as this chip changing state, not a different chip appearing in its place.
A chip is a choice, not a process. If applying it is slow, the results show it.

a11y: Renders a native <button type="button"> for focus and keyboard activation.
Selected state is exposed via aria-pressed.

components.name: Popover
components.summary: Click-triggered overlay over Base UI Popover (focus management, collision-aware positioning, Esc/outside dismissal). Holds interactive content; 18rem-wide surface.

usage.description: Use Popover for anchored secondary content that needs more room than a tooltip but less commitment than a dialog.

bestPractices.description: Use it for small pickers, summaries, or contextual controls tied to a trigger.
Keep focus behavior and dismissal predictable.
Do not use Popover for blocking confirmations, long forms, or critical information.
Do not put a form that can fail validation inside one. A popover dismisses on outside click, which discards what the user typed with no warning — that is a Dialog.

anatomy.name: PopoverTrigger
anatomy.description: The element that anchors and opens the popover.

anatomy.name: PopoverContent
anatomy.description: The floating content surface.

anatomy.name: PopoverTitle
anatomy.description: An optional heading for the content.

anatomy.name: PopoverDescription
anatomy.description: Optional supporting copy.

anatomy.name: PopoverClose
anatomy.description: An explicit close control when helpful.

anatomy.name: PopoverArrow
anatomy.description: An optional arrow pointing to the trigger.

props.name: Popover (Root)
props.type: Base UI Popover.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, modal)
props.description: Groups the trigger and content. Uncontrolled by default.

subcomponents.name: PopoverTrigger
subcomponents.description: The anchor element. Use render={<Button/>} to compose with another component.

subcomponents.name: PopoverContent
subcomponents.type: Base UI Popup props + side: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" | "inline-*" + align: "start" | "center" | "end" + sideOffset: number + anchor: Element | Ref | (() => Element) | VirtualElement + className
subcomponents.description: Portals + positions + paints the popup. side picks which side of the trigger to render against (auto-flips on collision; defaults to "bottom"); align sets alignment along that side (defaults to "center"); sideOffset is the gap in px (defaults to 8). anchor positions against a different element/ref/getter than the trigger — Base UI 1.5 has no separate Anchor part, so pass it here to decouple the open-location from the trigger.

subcomponents.name: PopoverTitle
subcomponents.description: Accessible heading; Base UI wires aria-labelledby to the popup.

subcomponents.name: PopoverDescription
subcomponents.description: Supplementary copy; Base UI wires aria-describedby to the popup.

subcomponents.name: PopoverClose
subcomponents.description: A button that closes the popover. Use render={<Button/>} to compose.

subcomponents.name: PopoverArrow
subcomponents.description: Optional pointer connecting the popup to its trigger. Place inside PopoverContent.

a11y: Base UI manages focus into and out of the popup, traps focus when modal, and restores focus to the trigger on close.
Opens on trigger press (click/Enter/Space); dismisses on Esc and outside press.
PopoverTitle/PopoverDescription wire aria-labelledby/aria-describedby on the popup.
Enters and exits on the motion-pop recipe (Base UI starting/ending-style attributes), so it follows the motion policy.

components.name: Progress
components.summary: Linear progress bar over Base UI Progress — value 0–100 drives the fill; omit value (or pass null) for an indeterminate, pulsing bar.

usage.description: Use Progress to communicate determinate or indeterminate completion for a task or process.

bestPractices.description: Use determinate values when progress can be measured.
Pair the visual indicator with text when users need context or exact values.
Do not use Progress as a decorative divider or status color bar.
Do not use a determinate Progress for an unknown duration. A bar that sits at 90% is worse than a Spinner, because it makes a promise about time that you cannot keep.

anatomy.name: ProgressTrack
anatomy.description: The background track that defines the range.

anatomy.name: ProgressIndicator
anatomy.description: The filled or animated progress indicator.

anatomy.name: ProgressLabel
anatomy.description: A text label for the progress task.

anatomy.name: ProgressValue
anatomy.description: A readable value such as 45 percent.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value between min and max. null (or omitted) renders the indeterminate state.

props.name: min
props.description: The minimum value of the range.

props.name: max
props.description: The maximum value of the range.

props.name: format
props.description: Formatting options for ProgressValue (e.g. style: 'percent', or a currency).

props.name: getAriaValueText
props.description: Returns a human-readable text alternative for aria-valuenow.

props.name: size
props.description: Bar thickness, on the same three rails as Meter so the two match on one page. ProgressTrack inherits it.

subcomponents.name: ProgressTrack
subcomponents.description: The rail. Rendered automatically when Progress has no children; renders a ProgressIndicator child by default. Takes `size` (inherited from Progress) for its thickness — use that rather than a className height.

subcomponents.name: ProgressIndicator
subcomponents.description: The fill. Width is set by Base UI from the value; spans full width and pulses while indeterminate.

subcomponents.name: ProgressLabel
subcomponents.description: Accessible label; wires aria-labelledby on the Root.

subcomponents.name: ProgressValue
subcomponents.description: Formatted value readout. Accepts a render-function child for custom formatting.

motion.why: A progress bar appears because work started. Staging its entrance delays the one piece of information the reader is waiting for.
It reports; it does not accept input. A bar that reacted to the pointer would read as a Slider, which is a control the reader can drag.

Fill width eases between values on the motion tokens (no recipe animates width), so the bar reads as filling rather than as a series of unrelated widths. It matters most where progress arrives in coarse jumps — four chunked upload callbacks look like a glitching bar without it.

Indeterminate (value null) has no width to animate, so the pulse carries the whole signal that work is still happening. Without it the indeterminate state is a static bar — indistinguishable from a stalled determinate one.

a11y: Base UI sets role=progressbar with aria-valuenow / aria-valuemin / aria-valuemax and reports status to screen readers.
Indeterminate state (value null) omits aria-valuenow per the ARIA spec.
Pair ProgressLabel with the bar for a visible, associated name; ProgressValue exposes the formatted value.
