items.name: LandingPage
items.summary: Product / open-source landing page: a centered hero with an eyebrow Badge, one display headline, lede, two CTAs and a copyable install command; a Browser-framed product preview composed from real components; a six-up feature grid; a setup section with tabbed code; an agent-workflow section with terminal output; a CTA card; and a link-column footer.
items.intent: Reach for this for the marketing route of a developer product, library, or tool: the page where the product shows itself working and the reader installs or signs up. For a branded, editorial marketing site use BrandLandingPage. Not for product UI (display type and one-per-view rules forbid it inside the app).
notes: Display type is the marketing voice: exactly one display headline per page (`text-display-lg` on phones, `text-display-2xl` from `sm`). Every section below uses `text-heading-1` with a `text-overline` kicker.
The eyebrow is a small outline Badge (`size="sm"`): the badge's own size, never a type class forced onto its label. Hierarchy above the fold is eyebrow, display, lede, CTAs, install command.
The lede is body-lg capped at the prose measure. The headline may be wide; reading text may not.
Two CTAs max per row: one primary, one quiet outline. The install line is a `CodeBlock` with `prompt="$"`, so it truncates on one line and copy takes only the command.

Show the product instead of describing it. The preview is real components (PageHeader, metric Cards, a Meter, a CardList of Entity rows, Message and Bubble, ChatComposer) inside `Browser`, wrapped in an `inert` div so the picture's controls never take focus. Secondary columns hide on small screens rather than stacking into a long mock.
Features are Cards in a fixed `Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }}`, so six items always land as full rows (3 x 2, 2 x 3, 1 x 6) without an orphan.

Multi-line code uses `CodeBlock` with a filename; switch related snippets with `Tabs`, defaulting to the most complete one. Terminal output passes `highlight={false}` so a code highlighter does not colour prose.
Reveal wraps below-the-fold blocks only (features, code, CTA). It no-ops under reduced motion via the motion policy.
Hide nav groups on narrow screens by wrapping them in a `max-md:hidden` div: a `Row` or `Button` sets its own display, which a `hidden` class on the same element does not reliably override.
a11y: The hero headline is the page h1; section titles are h2s and feature and step titles are h3s. Footer column labels are h2s inside the footer nav.

The product preview is a `figure` with a visible figcaption. Its content is `inert`, which removes it from the tab order and the accessibility tree, so its headings and buttons do not pollute the outline.
Reveal renders content immediately (no animation) when prefers-reduced-motion is set.
CTA buttons are real links with visible text, with no icon-only CTAs. Footer links keep a 36px minimum row height for touch.

items.name: ListDetailPage
items.summary: Searchable list beside the selected record's detail: interactive Entity rows in a CardList (5 of 12 columns) and a sticky detail pane (7) with an editable field, a label/value list, record actions with a destructive confirmation, and recent activity. Below lg it becomes a drill-in.
items.intent: Reach for this when a route lists records AND works on one at a time (members + member, inbox + message, orders + order). For pure browsing with no selection, a single-column FeedPage or a DashboardPage table is simpler.
notes: Region cap is `wide`; Columns 12 → Col 5 (list) + Col 7 (detail). Below lg the list and detail share one column as a drill-in: selecting a row shows the detail with an `All members` back button (lg:hidden), and the back button returns to the list. The panes swap with `max-lg:hidden`, so desktop always shows both.

Rows are interactive Entity inside one Card + CardList. Selection is Entity `selected`; `sable-surface` on the list card makes its selected step 12% ink off the card, so a selected row stays distinct from its muted avatar.
Search filters the list in place (name, email, role). No matches swap the CardList for an EmptyState with a Clear search action; the selected detail stays open.
A pending invite lives in the same list: a mail glyph in the Avatar, an `Invited` Badge, and an invite-specific detail (role on joining, sent, expires, invited by; Resend and Revoke actions).
The role Select edits the record in place; its Field description states what the role can do. The owner's role is read-only and the owner has no remove action.
Read-only facts are a native `<dl className="sable-list-dl sable-list-dl-2">` inside an `@container`, so pairs go two-up only when the pane is wide enough.
Remove / revoke run through DestructiveActionModal; on confirm the next row is selected. Page-level counts (members, pending, seats) live in the PageHeader description and update with the list.
The detail pane is sticky (lg:top-6) so it stays in view while a long list scrolls.
a11y: Each row is a real button (Entity `interactive` + `onSelect`): Tab moves through rows, Enter/Space selects. The selected row is Entity `selected`, which paints the selected fill and sets aria-current; list avatars are aria-hidden so initials are not read before the name.
The detail pane is a labelled region (`Member details`) whose title is a level-2 heading.

On a phone, drilling in moves focus to the back button; going back returns focus to the row that was open. After a remove, focus lands on the newly selected row; after Clear search, on the search field.

items.name: SettingsPage
items.summary: Account settings inside the app shell: a sticky SideNav section rail beside a column of section Cards — a Profile form with the page's one explicit save, Card + CardList + Entity rows with Switches that apply instantly, a read-only payouts summary, account rows, and a delete card confirmed through DestructiveActionModal.
items.intent: Reach for this for account/profile/workspace settings and any 'edit a handful of grouped preferences' route. Not for a single short form (use AuthPage's centered form shape) or bulk record editing (use DashboardPage + DataTable).
notes: Region cap is `wide`, split on a 12-column track: a 3-column SideNav rail and a 9-column section column. The rail fills the space a lone content-width column would leave empty and gives the page its table of contents.
The rail is `SideNav` (the documented settings sub-nav), sticky, with in-page anchor items; it hides below lg, where the sections simply stack and the shell's BottomNav carries app navigation.

One save model, stated in the copy: drafted text (the Profile form) commits through its single footer save; toggles apply the moment they change, and the Notifications description says so. Never pair a Switch with a Save button.
Settings rows are Card + CardList + Entity with the Switch in `action` — the row owns its title and one-line description; keep descriptions short, because Entity truncates its subtitle.
Each section is a Card whose CardTitle holds an h2, so the page has a real heading outline under PageHeader's h1; Cards carry the anchor id and `scroll-mt-*` so anchor jumps clear the top edge.
Field wires label/description/error a11y automatically; never hand-roll <label> + <input> pairs. Pair fields side by side with Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2 }}.
The destructive action is last and isolated in its own Card, and it never acts directly: it opens DestructiveActionModal with type-to-confirm on the handle.
Lives in the same AppShell as DashboardPage: Sidebar from lg up, AppHeader + BottomNav below it, with Settings marked active in both.
a11y: AppShell provides the skip link and <main id="main-content"> landmark; the active SidebarItem and BottomNavItem carry aria-current.
The section rail is a labelled <nav> ("Settings sections") distinct from the primary navigation; its active item carries aria-current.
Every section has an h2, so screen-reader heading navigation mirrors the rail.
Each Switch takes its row title as aria-label, since the Entity title is not a <label>.
Field auto-wires htmlFor/id, aria-describedby (description + error), aria-invalid, and required.
DestructiveActionModal is an alertdialog: focus opens on Cancel, the backdrop does not dismiss, and the confirm stays disabled until the handle is typed.

items.name: TrackerPage
items.summary: Records workspace in the tool register: a Sidebar rail of grouped views ending in an account menu, a WorkspaceBar of Breadcrumbs over pill Tabs, a filter row, one grouped DataTable, and a docked inspector of PanelSection property rows with a pinned comment form. Below lg the rail and the inspector become sheets and a BottomNav takes the last row.
items.intent: Reach for this when a team works through records in a dense tool — an issue tracker, a support queue, a pipeline: a grouped list, a docked inspector for the selected record, and a rail of views. For records a person reads and edits one at a time on a page, ListDetailPage is the page-register shape; for monitoring with headline numbers, DashboardPage.
notes: Workspace sets the compact density for everything inside: 32px rail rows, 28px tables, 24px property fields. Nothing in the pattern sizes a control or a row by hand. The Overview tab is a reading view, so it sits in `<Density value="comfortable">` and its prose gets page type back.

The rail is Sable's own parts on one grid: SidebarBrand, SidebarGroup, SidebarItem and SidebarAccount share the icon and label columns. The account row is the trigger of the account Menu, which holds Settings, an Appearance submenu wired to useSableTheme (light, dark, system) and Sign out. No Settings button or badge sits in the footer.

There is no Workspace `toolbar`: the bars belong to the list column, so the inspector runs the full height beside them. The first WorkspaceBar carries Breadcrumbs; the second carries pill Tabs, a view switch in chrome, which sits beside the bar's other controls rather than drawing a rule.

One DataTable groups the rows (`groupBy`, `groups`): one header for every group, a StatusDot, a count and an add action per group header, and Done starting closed. The segmented ToggleGroup switches the grouping between status and assignee. Filtering to nothing swaps the table for an EmptyState with a Clear filters action.
Workflow states map onto StatusDot tones once (`STATUSES`), so group headers and the status Select read from one place. A product with a richer status glyph keeps that one mapping and swaps the icon.

The inspector is a Panel with `narrow="sheet"`: docked at 320px from lg, a right sheet below it, its content rendered once. Below lg it opens only when a row is picked (`inspecting`), so a phone never loads with a sheet over the list. Properties are PanelSection + PropertyRow with xs Select triggers and an xs DatePicker; Activity uses RelativeTime; the comment Form is pinned under the scrolling body.

The rail is a Panel with `narrow="sheet" side="left"`, opened from a `lg:hidden` menu button in the first bar; in the sheet the Sidebar fills its width. Workspace `bottomNav` reserves the BottomNav's row below lg, so the status bar ends above it.
a11y: Workspace renders a skip link to the canvas (`Skip to issues`) and WorkspaceCanvas is the main landmark; the rail and the inspector are labelled complementary regions (`Workspace navigation`, `Issue details`), and as sheets they keep those labels as their dialog titles.
The page has one level-1 heading (visually hidden; the breadcrumb shows the place) and the inspector's title is a level-2 heading.
Group header rows are real buttons with aria-expanded; rows open the inspector from the keyboard (DataTable's row activation). Every icon-only action has an accessible name and a tooltip.
Each SidebarGroup is a named group; the account row names the person, and its menu is a standard Menu with a radio group for the colour mode.

blocks.about: Section-sized compositions — a sign-in card, a pricing card, an order tracker — smaller than a page shell and with no behaviour of their own. Copy the code (imports included) and edit the content constants at the top, or import the same component from `@sableui/react/blocks` to see it in place first. Props are the block contract only: `className` (a card block fills its container up to its designed `width.max`; size it from the parent or with className), `framed` on Card-built blocks (false drops the surface for a Sheet, Dialog or section that already frames it), and the primary action's callback. Content is never a prop.

items.name: ApiKeysBlock
items.summary: An API keys card: each key's name with its masked hint in Code, when it was created and last used, and an OverflowMenu to rename, roll or revoke.
items.intent: Reach for this for developer settings — API keys, access tokens, webhook secrets. Show a newly created key once, in a Dialog with a copy button; this list only ever shows the masked hint.
notes: Only the last four characters are shown. A full key never appears in a list, so there is no copy action here.
"Last used" sits in the detail line: it is what tells someone a key is safe to revoke.
Revoke is the destructive item, last and after a separator; confirm it in your handler with DestructiveActionModal.
a11y: Each OverflowMenu is labelled with the key's name, so the triggers are distinguishable.
The masked hint is a Code element inside the title, read after the key's name.
items.imports: import { Button, Card, CardAction, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardList, CardTitle, cn, Code, Entity, Icon, MenuItem, MenuSeparator, OverflowMenu } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: ApprovalBlock
items.summary: An agent asking permission for one tool call: the question, what is at stake, the call itself as a ToolCall with its exact input, and Deny / Always allow / Allow once.
items.intent: Reach for this in a chat or agent run when a tool call waits on the person — running a command, sending, paying, deleting, publishing. It wraps the call's own ToolCall, which shows status="awaiting" until the person answers and then "complete" or "denied". A destructive action outside an agent is DestructiveActionModal.
notes: The title is the question in plain words ("Run this command?"); the description says what is at stake. That sentence is what the person is deciding on.
The call is shown as the agent made it — tool name and raw input, open on arrival — because the exact arguments are what a careful person checks. Do not paraphrase them into a form.

Three answers, as agent products settle on: Deny on the start edge, then Always allow and Allow once, the primary on the end. Neither is focused on arrival: an approval that a stray Enter can grant is not an approval.
After a decision the buttons give way to one InlineStatus line saying what happened, and the ToolCall shows the outcome, so the thread keeps a record of the answer.
a11y: Focus moves to the outcome line when the buttons leave, instead of dropping to the page; the line is a role=status region, so the decision is announced.
The ToolCall announces its own status change, and its input is a labelled code view.

items.name: ChatThreadBlock
items.summary: A short message thread on a card: Message rows with incoming muted Bubbles on the start side and your own primary Bubbles on the end.
items.intent: Reach for this to show a conversation excerpt — a support preview, a comment thread on a dashboard, a recent-DM card. A working chat with a composer, streaming and history is the ChatPanel page shell.
notes: Sit it on a card, not straight on a muted page: incoming bubbles are the muted surface, and would vanish into it.
Your own messages align to the end with the primary Bubble; everyone else's align to the start.
a11y: Each Message carries a messageId, so a thread can be addressed and announced item by item.
Direction is shown by alignment and colour; when senders matter, add the sender's name to each Message.

items.name: CommandPaletteBlock
items.summary: An inline command palette: CommandMenuPanel with a filter field and grouped actions, each with an icon and its keyboard shortcut.
items.intent: Reach for this to show a command list in place — an empty state that teaches shortcuts, an onboarding step, a quick-actions card. The ⌘K palette that opens over the app is CommandMenu; this is its panel without the dialog.
notes: Each command shows its shortcut as a Kbd hint, so the palette also teaches the keys.
`onCommand` receives the command's id; ids also key the rows, so two commands may share a label.
No card around it: the panel is its own surface, lifted with `shadow-sm` when it sits on a muted section.
a11y: CommandMenuPanel wires the filter input to the list as a combobox, with arrow-key navigation and the active row announced.
Shortcut hints are Kbd elements, read as keys.

items.intent: Reach for this as the last section before the footer, repeating the hero's primary action once the reader has seen the case. Mid-page prompts to sign up belong inline, not in a band.
notes: Copied from the LandingPage page shell's closing call to action.
The primary action matches the hero's, so the page asks for one thing twice rather than two things once.
Sitting on a Card lifts it from the page without a coloured band, so it follows any preset.
a11y: The section is labelled by its h2.
Both actions are links styled as Buttons, because they navigate.

items.name: DangerZoneBlock
items.summary: A delete-account card: what deleting removes and what survives, one destructive Button, and a DestructiveActionModal that asks for the handle to be typed before it acts.
items.intent: Reach for this as the last section of account, workspace or project settings. Deleting a single record from a list is an OverflowMenu item that opens DestructiveActionModal directly, not a card.
notes: Copied from the SettingsPage page shell's Delete account section.
The button never acts directly: it opens the modal, whose confirm stays disabled until the handle is typed.
The description says what is lost AND what is kept ("Files you shared stay with your team"), which is what people want to know before they decide.
a11y: DestructiveActionModal is an alertdialog: focus opens on Cancel and the backdrop does not dismiss it.
The CardTitle is an h2, so the section is reachable by heading.

items.name: DeviceComparisonBlock

items.intent: Reach for this when two or three measures share a page and the reader looks at one at a time — devices, regions, plans. To see them together, plot both in one BarChart or LineChart instead.
notes: The totals are the switch: Toggles in a labelled ToggleGroup, so the number and the control are one thing, with the group's own pressed and hover states.
Switching eases every bar to its new height rather than redrawing.
Below sm the tiles stack under the title and divide with a top rule instead of a side rule.
a11y: Each total is a Toggle (aria-pressed) named by its label and value, in a ToggleGroup labelled "Device" with arrow-key movement between tiles.
The chart's name says which series is plotted, so the data table is unambiguous.

a11y: DateTile is a <time> with a machine-readable date; the time range is plain text read in order after the title.
The AvatarGroup's aria-label states the total attendee count.

items.name: FaqBlock
items.summary: A FAQ section: the heading and a way to ask beside an Accordion of questions, each answer one or two sentences.
items.intent: Reach for this near pricing or at the end of a landing page, for the questions that block a decision. Long help content belongs in docs, not an accordion.
notes: Every question starts closed: the list of questions is itself the useful summary.
The way to ask a human sits beside the heading, so it is found before the reader scrolls the list.
Capped at the `content` region width; questions wider than that are hard to scan.
a11y: Accordion triggers are buttons with aria-expanded, inside headings, so the questions are navigable by heading and operable by keyboard.
The contact link is a real <a> inside the lede sentence.

items.intent: Reach for this to explain what a product does in six or fewer points. For a sequence (first this, then that), use StepsBlock; for one proof point with numbers, TestimonialBlock.
notes: Copied from the LandingPage page shell's features section.
Six features fill 3 × 2 evenly; keep the count a multiple of three, or drop to cols={{ lg: 2 }}.
Each body is one sentence. A feature that needs a paragraph needs its own section.
Icons sit in a `sable-well`, which derives its fill from the card surface it is on.
a11y: Each feature is an <article> with an h3 under the section's h2.
The icons are decorative; each title says what the feature is.

items.name: FeedbackFormBlock
items.summary: A feedback card: a one-to-five rating as a full-width ToggleGroup, an optional notes field, and Skip / Send feedback.
items.intent: Reach for this for a post-session or post-purchase survey in a Sheet, Dialog or end-of-flow screen. For a feedback control anchored to a button in the app chrome, use the Feedback component (a popover).
notes: The rating is preselected, so one tap on Send is a complete answer; the notes are optional and say so.
Skip is a ghost Button before the primary, so dismissing is always available and never competes with sending.
`onDone` reports whether feedback was sent and, if so, the score and notes.
a11y: The ToggleGroup carries aria-label="Rating"; each Toggle's number is its name.
The Textarea carries aria-label="Notes"; its placeholder is a prompt, not the label.

items.name: GoalProgressBlock
items.summary: A goals card: a ring per goal in a RadialChart against its track (a full ring is 100%), a legend, and which goals are behind in the footer.
items.intent: Reach for this for progress toward two to four targets — a quarter's goals, a plan's limits, onboarding steps. A single reading in a settings row is a Meter; many goals are a list of Progress bars.
notes: max={100} makes a full ring mean done; each ring draws round from 12 o'clock as the card scrolls into view.
The footer names what is behind, so the card is actionable without reading the rings.
Values are formatted as percents in the tooltip and data table.
a11y: The rings' data table lists each goal and its percent.
Arrowing through the rings announces each goal; the legend names every ring's colour.

The headline is the page's only h1 — place one HeroBlock per page.
Two actions, one primary. The install command is the third, quieter way in for developers who already decided.
The lede is capped at the prose measure and the headline at max-w-4xl, so both stay readable on wide screens.
a11y: Calls to action are links styled as Buttons (render={<a />}), because they navigate.
The CodeBlock's copy button is labelled and announces when it has copied.

items.intent: Reach for this for team or project invites in onboarding, an empty workspace, or a settings section. For managing an existing member list with roles, use a CardList of Entity rows instead.

The AvatarGroup ring matches the card surface when framed and inherits the host surface when not.
a11y: The AvatarGroup carries an aria-label with the count, so the stack reads as one item, not four initials.
The email Input carries aria-label; there is no visible label in this compact layout.

Amounts are a numeric column — right-aligned with tabular figures — so they compare by eye.
On a narrow screen the table scrolls sideways inside the card (with a quiet scrollbar) rather than squeezing its columns.
a11y: The download column has a screen-reader-only header, and each button names its invoice ("Download INV-0042").
Status is text in a Badge; the dot's colour only reinforces it.

items.summary: A KPI row with trends: three stat cards, each the value in the metric mono tier, a Sparkline of its last twelve weeks, and the change as a Badge.
items.intent: Reach for this at the top of a dashboard or a landing page's proof section, where each number needs its recent shape. Without the trend, StatRowBlock is calmer; for one headline trend, TrafficTrendBlock.

The sparklines draw on as the row scrolls into view.
One column on a phone, three from sm.

The change is stated in text (+8.2% vs last quarter) with an arrow icon; colour only reinforces it.

items.name: MediaPlayerBlock
items.summary: A now-playing card: cover, title and artist as an Entity with a Like action, a position Slider with elapsed and remaining time, and previous / play-pause / next.
items.intent: Reach for this for audio or video playback controls outside the media itself — a mini player, a podcast card, a preview in a feed. Playback over the video frame is the Video component's own chrome.
notes: Play/pause is the one filled control, centred between two ghost skips.
Times are `text-mono-caption`, so the digits do not shift as they count.
The cover is painted from the palette as a placeholder; swap it for the real artwork.
a11y: Every icon-only Button carries aria-label, and play/pause's label follows its state.
The Slider carries aria-label="Position". Give it aria-valuetext in your player ("1:24 of 3:40") so the position is read as time, not a percentage.

items.name: MessageReactionsBlock
items.summary: A short thread you can react to: right-click or long-press a bubble for a menu with a row of quick reactions above Reply and Copy, or use the add-reaction pill under a message. A new reaction blooms in and sprays copies of its emoji.
items.intent: Reach for this when a conversation excerpt should be reactable — a team thread, a comment card, a support transcript. A read-only excerpt is ChatThreadBlock; a working chat with a composer and history is the ChatPanel page shell.
notes: Two ways in, on purpose: the right-click / long-press menu is fast once you know it is there, and the add-reaction pill is how a first-time reader finds reactions at all.
The quick row in the menu is MenuReactions (checkbox menu items) and the one in the pill's popover is ReactionPicker (a toolbar), so each is reachable by the keyboard model of the surface it sits in.
Only the reader's own reaction celebrates. Counts from other people roll quietly, and the reactions a page loads with never play.
The add-reaction pill appears only on messages that already have reactions; a message with none is reacted to from its menu, which keeps quiet rows quiet.
a11y: Each bubble is focusable, and its menu opens on right click, long press, Shift+F10 or the Menu key; its reactions are checkbox items reporting whether the reader has used each one.
Each reaction pill is a toggle named by its meaning and count ("Party, 3") with `aria-pressed`; the emoji and the burst are hidden from assistive tech.
Under reduced motion the reaction appears and the count changes at once; nothing else is lost.

The field and button sit side by side from sm up and stack on a phone, where the button goes full width.

The CardTitle renders an h2, so the sign-up is reachable by heading in a footer.

Unread is a quiet info dot before the time, so the times keep one right edge — the list stays calm when most items are unread.

a11y: The unread dot is decorative; each unread row also carries a screen-reader-only "(unread)" after the name.

notes: Switches apply the moment they change; never pair them with a Save button. `onChange` receives the row id and the new state.
Rows are Card + CardList + Entity, so they inset with the card's padding at any density.

Keep details to one line — Entity truncates its subtitle.

The status Badge restates the current stage in one word so the card scans without reading the steps.

The price is a heading tier because it is the card's headline; its unit and billing note sit beside and below it in muted body text.
`onStart` receives the period showing, so checkout opens on the plan the person was looking at.
a11y: The ToggleGroup carries aria-label="Billing period"; each Toggle's text is its name.
The check icons are decorative beside each feature's text.

items.summary: A stat card with a breakdown: the KPI in the metric mono tier, its trend Badge, a SegmentedBar of how the total divides, and a StatusDot legend.
items.intent: Reach for this when a headline number is worth splitting into a few categories — revenue by product, storage by type, tickets by priority. A plain KPI with no split is a smaller stat card (see DashboardPage's stat row).

The legend reflows from two columns to one by measuring in em, so larger type or a narrower card never truncates a label.
Each category keeps the same tone in the bar and its legend dot; reuse those tones wherever the category appears.

The trend Badge states the change as text (+8.2%), not by colour.

items.name: SignInBlock
items.summary: A sign-in card: email and password, a primary Sign in, and a passkey alternative under an "or" separator.
items.intent: Reach for this wherever someone signs in inside a surface you already have — a Sheet, a Dialog, a gated panel. For a whole sign-in route with brand art beside the form, start from the AuthPage page shell instead.
notes: One primary action. The passkey is an outline Button under a labelled Separator, so it reads as an alternative, not a second submit.
The fields are a real <form>: Enter submits, and the browser's password manager recognises the autocomplete hints.
framed={false} keeps the padding and drops the surface, for a Sheet or Dialog that is already the frame.
a11y: Inputs carry aria-label because the design shows placeholders, not visible labels; add Field labels if your brief wants them visible.
`onSignIn` receives "password" or "passkey", so focus and error handling stay with the caller's auth flow.
items.imports: import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Icon, Input, Separator } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: SignUpBlock
items.summary: A sign-up card: name, work email and password as labelled Fields, one full-width Create account, and a link to sign in instead.
items.intent: Reach for this to create an account inside a surface you already have, or as the form of a sign-up route. For the whole route with brand art beside it, start from the AuthPage page shell and drop this card in.
notes: Visible labels, not placeholders: someone filling a new form needs to see what each field is after typing in it.
The password rule is stated up front in the Field description, before anyone fails it.
`onSignUp` receives the fields only after the browser's own validation (required, type=email, minLength) passes.
a11y: Field wires each label, description and error to its input; never hand-roll <label> + <input> pairs.
autoComplete hints (name, email, new-password) let password managers offer to generate and save the password.
items.imports: import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Field, Form, Input } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: SiteFooterBlock
items.summary: A site footer: the brand and a one-line tagline beside link groups in a labelled Footer nav, over a copyright line.
items.intent: Reach for this at the foot of a marketing or docs site. App screens inside an AppShell take no footer; their navigation lives in the sidebar.
notes: Copied from the LandingPage page shell's footer.
Every link is at least 36px tall (min-h-9), so the dense list is still an easy touch target.
Groups go two up on a phone and three up from sm; add a group only if it has three links or more.
a11y: Renders <footer> with a <nav aria-label="Footer">, distinct from the page's main navigation.
Group titles are h2s, so the footer's structure is navigable by heading.
items.imports: import { cn, Region, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: StatRowBlock
items.summary: A KPI row: four stat cards, each a label, the value in the metric mono tier, and a trend Badge with its comparison note — 2 × 2 on a phone, one row from xl.
items.intent: Reach for this at the top of a dashboard or report, above the tables and charts it summarises. One headline number worth splitting into categories is RevenueBreakdownBlock.
notes: Copied from the DashboardPage page shell's stat row.
Values are `text-mono-xl` — tabular figures, never a heading tier — so the four numbers align digit for digit.
The trend Badge sits with its note in CardContent, so the value keeps the full card width when the row folds to 2 × 2.
Keep it to four. A fifth stat is a sign one of them belongs in a table.
a11y: The trend is stated in text (+8.2%) with an arrow icon; the tone is reinforcement, not the signal.
Each card's label is read before its value, in source order.
items.imports: import { Badge, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, cn, Grid, Icon, Row } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: StepsBlock
items.summary: A how-it-works section: the heading, lede and a guide link on the left; three numbered steps on the right, each under a strong rule.
items.intent: Reach for this when the pitch is a sequence — onboarding, a workflow, a setup. Parallel benefits with no order are FeatureGridBlock; progress through a live process is a Stepper.
notes: Copied from the BrandLandingPage page shell's how-it-works section.
The steps are an <ol>, so the order is semantic and the 01 / 02 / 03 numbers are its visual echo, set in the mono tier.
Three steps fit the 1 : 2 split on desktop; on a phone everything stacks with the intro first.
a11y: Each step has an h3 under the section's h2.
The guide link is an <a> styled as an outline Button, because it navigates.
items.imports:
import { useId } from "react"
import { Button, cn, Icon, Region, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: TaskListBlock
items.summary: A checklist card: a titled list of Checkbox rows with a category Badge each, a live count of what is left, and a quiet Add task action.
items.intent: Reach for this for a short, personal to-do list on a dashboard or in onboarding. A team's task board with assignees and status columns needs a Table or DataTable.
notes: Finishing a task strikes it through and mutes it rather than removing it, so the list does not jump under the pointer.
The count in CardAction updates with every check, so progress reads without counting rows.
Add task is a ghost Button in the footer — present, but quieter than the list.
a11y: Every Checkbox has a real <Label htmlFor>, so the whole title is the click target and the accessible name.
Category Badges carry text; the tone only groups them visually.
items.imports:
import { useState, useId } from "react"
import { Badge, Button, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, Checkbox, cn, Icon, Label } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: TeamMembersBlock
items.summary: A members card: Entity rows with avatar, name and email, a role Badge, and an OverflowMenu of role changes and removal; pending invites sit in the same list.
items.intent: Reach for this to manage who is in a workspace, project or team. For inviting people when the list is empty or short, InviteTeamBlock is the lighter shape; for hundreds of members with filters, use a DataTable.
notes: Each row's menu offers only what applies to it: Make admin or Make member, Resend invite for pending rows, then the destructive action after a separator.
The owner has no menu — ownership is transferred elsewhere — and a control-sized spacer keeps the role badges aligned.
Pending invites are outline Badges in the same list, so the team's full size reads in one place.
a11y: Each OverflowMenu is labelled with the member's name ("Manage Mara Okafor"), so the triggers are distinguishable in a list.
Roles are text in a Badge; tone only distinguishes the owner.
items.imports: import { Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, CardAction, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardList, CardTitle, cn, Entity, Icon, MenuItem, MenuSeparator, OverflowMenu } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: TestimonialBlock
items.summary: A customer story: one large blockquote with the person's avatar, name and role, beside three outcome figures separated by rules.
items.intent: Reach for this for one strong, attributable quote backed by numbers. A wall of short quotes is a different section; a logo row is Marquee.

The quote and the outcomes share one Card as a <figure>; the outcomes move under the quote below lg.
Outcome values use display sizes because they are the proof; their labels say what each number counts.

The section is labelled "Customer story" so it is reachable as a landmark.

items.name: TrafficSourcesBlock
items.summary: A share card: a donut PieChart of where a total comes from, the total in the hole, a legend, and the headline share in words in the footer.
items.intent: Reach for this for a split of one total into four or fewer parts — traffic sources, revenue by plan, tickets by channel. More parts, or values to compare exactly, belong in a horizontal BarChart.
notes: The total sits in the donut's hole, so the card answers "how many" and "from where" at once.
The footer puts the biggest share in a sentence — the takeaway does not depend on reading the slices.
The slices sweep in clockwise as the card scrolls into view.
a11y: The chart's data table lists every source and its count; the legend repeats it visually.
Hovering or arrowing through the slices pulls each out and announces it.

items.name: TrafficTrendBlock
items.summary: A trend card: a stacked gradient AreaChart of two series by day, a time-range ToggleGroup in the header, and a one-line takeaway with its direction in the footer.
items.intent: Reach for this as the headline chart of a dashboard or an analytics section on a landing page. For a single number with a small trend beside it, KpiSparklineBlock is lighter.
notes: Switching the range eases the chart from one shape to the next instead of redrawing it.
The footer states the takeaway in words, so the card says something even before the chart is read.
The tooltip heading spells out the weekday; the axis keeps short dates so they fit.
a11y: The chart's accessible name includes the range showing, and its data table updates with it.
The range control is a labelled ToggleGroup; the chart is one tab stop with arrow-key navigation.

items.name: UploadListBlock
items.summary: An upload queue: full-width Attachment rows — one uploading with progress and a cancel button, one finished with a success check.
items.intent: Reach for this under a FileDropzone, or anywhere files are in flight — a composer, an import step, a document form. For files attached to a message, Attachment chips in the composer fit better.
notes: Rows, not chips: each Attachment drops its chip cap (`max-w-none`) to fill the block's width.
The success check sits in a control-sized box so it lines up with the cancel button on the row above.
No card: Attachment rows are their own surfaces. Wrap the block in a Card if it needs a header.
a11y: Attachment announces upload progress; the cancel Button carries aria-label.
The finished row's check carries aria-label="Uploaded", so the state is spoken, not only coloured.
items.imports: import { Attachment, Button, cn, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: VerifyCodeBlock
items.summary: A one-time-code card: where the code went, a six-slot OtpField grouped 3 + 3 under a visible label, and a quiet Resend.
items.intent: Reach for this for email or SMS verification, two-factor sign-in, or confirming a sensitive change. For a code someone copies out (a recovery key), show it with Code and a copy button instead.
notes: No submit button: the code verifies the moment the last slot fills, which is what people expect from a code field.
The destination is named in the description, so a mistyped address is caught before the wait.
Resend is a ghost Button — present for the stuck case, never competing with the field.
a11y: OtpField names each slot ("Character 1 of 6") and accepts a pasted code into all six at once.
Field labels the group and reads the expiry as its description.

items.name: WalletBlock
items.summary: A balance card: the balance in the metric mono tier, Send and Receive as an equal pair, and recent activity as Entity rows with signed amounts.
items.intent: Reach for this for an account balance, store credit or credits summary with its latest movements. For a full transaction history with filters, use a DataTable.
notes: The balance is CardTitle at `text-mono-xl` — tabular figures, never a heading tier — under its label as CardDescription.
Send is primary and Receive secondary, side by side at equal width: two directions of one action, with sending the riskier and more frequent.
Incoming amounts are `text-success`; outgoing stay muted rather than red, because a payout or refund is not an error.
a11y: Each activity row's leading swatch is aria-hidden; the title and detail carry the meaning.
Amounts keep their sign in text (+49.00 / -850.00), so the direction does not depend on colour.

foundations.title: Typography
foundations.summary: Type is a closed vocabulary of paired utilities. Each one bundles size, weight, line-height and tracking, and is picked by role rather than by size.
foundations.headline: 6 families · 8 everyday tiers · 2 text colors · 1 utility per text node

vocabularies.title: The everyday set
vocabularies.note: Product UI is built almost entirely from these eight. Reach outside them on purpose.

terms.name: text-heading-1
terms.use: The page title. Exactly one per route.

terms.name: text-heading-2
terms.use: A major section of the page.

terms.name: text-title-lg
terms.use: Names a component: card, dialog, sheet, list row.

terms.name: text-title-sm
terms.use: Names a dense component: compact card, table section.

terms.name: text-body-md
terms.use: The default paragraph, description and help text.

terms.name: text-body-sm
terms.use: Secondary copy and table cells.

terms.name: text-label-lg
terms.use: Buttons, field labels, tabs.

terms.name: text-caption
terms.use: Timestamps, footnotes, meta rows.

vocabularies.title: The six families
vocabularies.note: Every tier belongs to one family, and the family is the decision. Size follows from it.

terms.name: Display  display-lg…4xl
terms.use: Type as image: landing heroes, campaign numbers. Never in product chrome; never two per view.

terms.name: Heading  heading-1…4
terms.use: The document outline (h1–h4). Keep the order; never skip a level to get a size.

terms.name: Title  title-lg · title-sm
terms.use: Names a UI part without claiming a document heading.

terms.name: Body  body-lg/md/sm/xs
terms.use: Reading text. -lg is the lede (carries text-wrap: pretty); -xs is a dense-UI floor, not a prose size.

terms.name: Label  label-lg/md/sm · caption
terms.use: Functional, scannable text of one to three words. Caption is also the group-label tier: nav sections, menu groups.

terms.name: Mono  mono-xl/lg/md/caption/sm
terms.use: Numbers that are the content, IDs, hashes, code, aligned figures.

terms.name: text-foreground
terms.use: Primary text: headings, body, values.

terms.name: text-muted-foreground
terms.use: Supporting text: descriptions, captions, meta, placeholders.

rules.rule: One paired utility per text node. Compose it with a color and margin only.
rules.why: Each utility is a tuned set of size, weight, leading and tracking. Splitting it into text-* + font-* + tracking-* breaks the tuning and every theme override of it.

rules.rule: Pick the tier by role, not by the size it renders at.
rules.why: A card title is title-lg even when body-lg is the same size: role fixes the weight (600 vs 400) and the rhythm around it.

rules.rule: Two text colors: foreground and muted-foreground.
rules.why: Both are contrast-tested against every surface in every theme. A third grey, or an opacity step, is untested contrast.

rules.rule: One heading-1 per route; headings descend without skipping levels.
rules.why: The heading outline is how screen-reader users navigate a page. Restyle with a tier rather than jumping a level for its size.

rules.rule: Hierarchy comes from a clear jump (heading → title → body), then weight and space, before size.
rules.why: Two sizes one step apart read as the same level. Space and weight separate levels more cheaply than another size.

rules.rule: Cap reading text at --measure-prose (65ch).
rules.why: Past roughly 75 characters the eye loses the line return. A wide region can still hold a 65ch column.

rules.rule: Numbers that must align use a mono tier (tabular figures).
rules.why: Proportional digits change width as values update, so totals and columns shimmy.

rules.rule: text-wrap: balance on headings, pretty on ledes, neither on long prose.
rules.why: balance evens short headlines; pretty only refuses a one-word last line. Both cost layout work that long prose does not repay.

rules.rule: To make all the type smaller or larger, set the base: --type-base: 14 (a unitless px number; 16 is the default). Never retune tiers one by one for it.
rules.why: Every tier is authored on a 16px base and keeps its ratio to it, so one number rebuilds the whole scale, headings to captions, and the baseline step and spacing follow the body. Shrinking tiers individually breaks the ratios between them. Set it on :root, a theme scope or a preset (tokens.shared["type-base"]) so the rhythm follows too.

rules.rule: Inside a Workspace, a panel's title is text-ui-title (14px · 600); compact text-title-lg resolves to it. Code follows too: text-mono-md and text-mono-caption compress to 12 / 11px at their own weight, so a CodeBlock matches the inputs beside it. A reading view inside the tool (an overview, a document, a long form) is wrapped in <Density value="comfortable"> and gets the page tiers back.
rules.why: The compact register remaps page tiers onto the 10-12px chrome ramp, which is right for chrome and wrong for prose: an issue overview set in a tool rendered its paragraphs at 11px. The remap stops at a comfortable boundary, so the wrapper is the whole fix.

rules.rule: A mark attached to a line of type (a dot, a bullet, a timeline marker, a leading icon) sits in a box one line tall (h-[1lh] items-center) and is sized in em.
rules.why: 1lh is the line-height of the text beside it, so the mark centres on that line in every tier, density and theme. A px size with a mt-[3px] nudge is right for one font at one size and wrong everywhere else.

noGos.never: Opacity on text (text-foreground/60, opacity-70 on a paragraph).
noGos.instead: text-muted-foreground.
noGos.why: An alpha step over an unknown surface has unknown contrast, and it shifts per theme.

noGos.never: A hand-picked size, weight or tracking (text-[15px], font-medium, tracking-wide).
noGos.instead: The paired utility for the role.
noGos.why: Off-vocabulary type cannot be retuned by a theme or the customizer, so it drifts the moment either changes.

noGos.never: Uppercase in product chrome: nav and menu group labels, page eyebrows, table headers, section titles.
noGos.instead: Sentence-case text-caption or text-label-md in muted-foreground; hierarchy from size, weight and space.
noGos.why: Tracked capitals spread across a UI read as shouting and slow word recognition. The eyebrow tier (label-xs / overline) is an editorial accent: at most one per marketing view.

noGos.never: Display tiers inside product UI, or two display sizes in one view.
noGos.instead: heading-1 for a page title; mono-xl for a metric.
noGos.why: Display is type as image. In chrome it competes with the content it is supposed to frame.

noGos.never: Justified text, or reading copy below body-sm.
noGos.instead: Ragged-right at body-md; body-xs only for dense data.
noGos.why: Justification opens rivers on the web, which has no hyphenation control; 12px prose fails people with low vision.

noGos.never: Changing the root font-size (html { font-size: 14px }) to make a product denser.
noGos.instead: --type-base: 14, with Workspace or <Density value="compact"> for denser controls.
noGos.why: The root also sizes every rem the app wrote: widths, insets, media queries. --type-base moves only the type and the rhythm built on it, and density moves the controls, so each can be chosen on its own.

noGos.never: A new font family, or raw font-feature-settings / font-variation-settings.
noGos.instead: The theme's sans, mono and optional display; font-variant-numeric and font-weight.
noGos.why: Raw axis tags silently do nothing on a fallback font, and every theme declares a fallback stack.

foundations.title: Spacing & sizing
foundations.summary: One scale, derived from the type: the baseline is one line of body text, split into steps every gap, inset and line height lands on. Space is assigned by role. Controls read a height ladder that a density scope can retune all at once.
foundations.headline: Baseline from the type · 8px steps · 3 roles · 1 control ladder

vocabularies.title: Spacing by role
vocabularies.note: Steps below 2 (8px) are optical correction only.

terms.name: Inset  p-4
terms.use: Padding inside a surface. p-3 for a dense card, px-3 py-2 for a row.

terms.name: Stack, within a group  gap-2
terms.use: Label to field, title to description.

terms.name: Stack, between groups  gap-4 – gap-6
terms.use: Field to field, card to card.

terms.name: Stack, between sections  gap-12+
terms.use: Major regions of a page.

terms.name: Inline  gap-2 – gap-3
terms.use: Icon to label, control to control.

vocabularies.title: The control ladder
vocabularies.note: Comfortable values; data-density="compact" (or <Density>) redefines every step for a region.

terms.name: h-(--control-xs)
terms.use: Inline chips, tree rows.

terms.name: h-(--control-sm)
terms.use: Compact buttons, toolbar controls.

terms.name: h-(--control-md)
terms.use: The default: inputs, buttons, selects, menu triggers.

terms.name: h-(--control-cta)
terms.use: The primary call to action; clears the touch floor on its own.

terms.name: h-(--control-lg)
terms.use: Prominent or touch-first actions.

terms.name: text-base (16px)
terms.use: Inline with label-md / body-sm.

terms.name: text-xl (20px)
terms.use: The default UI glyph beside label-lg.

terms.name: hit-target
terms.use: Keeps a visually small control's hit area at the WCAG floor without moving layout.

rules.rule: Every margin, padding and gap is a step on the scale, and vertical space between blocks is whole baseline steps: an even Tailwind step (2, 4, 6, 8, 12) or a Stack/Row/Grid gap number.
rules.why: The baseline is one line of body text split into steps; line heights round to it. An odd step (3, 5) is half a baseline step. It is a rhythm to keep, not a grid to force: components stay as tall as their content.

rules.rule: Padding, gaps and insets in a component sit on the spacing scale: a step (p-4, gap-2) or --spacing(n) inside an arbitrary value (p-[var(--card-p,--spacing(6))]).
rules.why: --spacing derives from the baseline step and the density (Character) control moves the leading it comes from, so anything on the scale moves with it. A literal p-[1.5rem] or padding: "12px" stays put while everything around it tightens. Keep fixed rem/px for what must not scale: a 1px hairline, a ring width.

rules.rule: Related things sit closer than unrelated things.
rules.why: Proximity groups content without a divider line. Use space first; reach for a border only when space is not enough.

rules.rule: Space lives on the container (gap), not on children (margins).
rules.why: gap survives reordering, conditional children and RTL; per-child margins do not.

rules.rule: Control heights read the --control-* ladder.
rules.why: A density scope retunes every control at once. A hardcoded height has to be found and overridden by hand.

rules.rule: Single-column content inside a card stacks with flex flex-col and a gap, not CSS grid.
rules.why: A grid track sizes to its widest min-content child, so one long unbreakable string (a URL, a code line, a table) blows the column out past the card. A flex column lets children shrink to the card.

rules.rule: A compact surface drops one whole step; a spacious one adds one.
rules.why: Moving in whole steps keeps density changes proportional.

rules.rule: Every interactive element clears a 44×44px hit area.
rules.why: WCAG 2.5.5. Use padding or hit-target to grow the hit area; never a bigger glyph.

rules.rule: Borderless controls get roughly twice the gap of bordered ones.
rules.why: A border declares where a control ends. Two ghost buttons 12px apart read as one target.

noGos.never: Arbitrary values: p-[15px], gap-[7px], mt-[13px].
noGos.instead: The nearest scale step.
noGos.why: Arbitrary values cannot follow density or a customized scale.

noGos.never: h-[40px] on a control.
noGos.instead: h-(--control-md).
noGos.why: It will not follow <Density>.

noGos.never: Icons sized with type utilities (text-body-md on an <Icon>).
noGos.instead: text-{size} scale classes.
noGos.why: Type utilities carry line-height and tracking that misalign glyphs.

noGos.never: A fixed width sized to an English label.
noGos.instead: padding-inline and max-width with wrapping.
noGos.why: German and Finnish run 30–50% longer.

foundations.title: Shape
foundations.summary: Radius signals what something is: tight on containers, full on actions. Nested corners stay concentric, and one edge treatment marks a boundary.
foundations.headline: 7 radius steps · concentric nesting · 1 edge treatment per boundary

vocabularies.title: The radius ladder
vocabularies.note: Each step is 4px apart, so common insets land on a real step. Themes and the customizer retune every step together.

terms.name: rounded-none
terms.use: Full-bleed media.

terms.name: rounded-xs
terms.use: Tags, kbd, small inline marks.

terms.name: rounded-sm
terms.use: Inputs, menu items, list rows.

terms.name: rounded-md
terms.use: Popovers, menus, toasts.

terms.name: rounded-lg
terms.use: Cards, dialogs, sheets.

terms.name: rounded-xl
terms.use: Hero surfaces.

terms.name: rounded-full
terms.use: Buttons (via --button-radius), avatars, pills, dots.

terms.name: border-border
terms.use: The default edge: inputs, cards, badges.

terms.name: border-border-strong
terms.use: Structural rules: table grids, section separators.

terms.name: border-border-floating
terms.use: Every floating surface: popovers, menus, selects, tooltips, dialogs, sheets, toasts. Lighter than border; the shadow carries the elevation.

terms.name: ring-2 ring-ring
terms.use: Focus only. Never a thick border.

rules.rule: Nested corners are concentric: inner radius = outer radius − inset. Write it as rounded-concentric-<outer>/<inset>, not a hardcoded step.
rules.why: A 12px popover with 4px padding takes 8px items. The utility computes the subtraction from the live tokens, so the pair stays concentric when a theme or the customizer rescales the radius ladder; a hardcoded rounded-sm drifts.

rules.rule: A list of rows inside a rounded popup uses popup-inset on the popup, rounded-popup-item on the rows and popup-bleed on a separator.
rules.why: All three derive from the popup's radius: the inset grows to a third of it (never below --spacing(1), so density moves it too), the rows take what is left after the inset and the 1px border, and a separator bleeds by exactly the inset. A rounder look gets more room instead of rows that round into pills; the default ladder lands on a 4px inset and 7px rows.

rules.rule: A Button, Pill or Badge gets its look from a variant, never from override classes.
rules.why: border, bg, rounded, ring and shadow classes on a component fight the variant's own hover, selected and focus states, and give one call site a look no other site can ask for. Use the variant that exists (Button variant="floating" over content, "on-color" on a fill; Pill appearance="outline"; Badge appearance and tone) or add one to the component.

rules.rule: The outer radius is always at least the inner radius.
rules.why: If the inset is larger than the outer radius, square the inner element or step the container up.

rules.rule: Never mix radii within one component.
rules.why: A component reads as one object when its corners agree.

rules.rule: Actions are full; containers are tight.
rules.why: The contrast itself says 'this is a control'. A theme flattens buttons through --button-radius, not by editing each one.

rules.rule: High-contrast outlines (selection, emphasis) are inset rings; hairline chrome is a border.
rules.why: Rings anti-alias on rounded corners at any display scale; a 1px light border on dark snaps to the pixel grid and looks jagged.

rules.rule: One edge treatment per boundary: a border, a ring or a shadow.
rules.why: Stacking all three makes an edge heavier than the content it holds.

rules.rule: Prefer a tonal step or space over a divider line.
rules.why: The flattest thing that reads is best.

noGos.never: rounded-[10px] or any off-ladder radius.
noGos.instead: The ladder step for the role.
noGos.why: Off-ladder radii cannot follow a theme or the customizer's radius control.

noGos.never: A card inside a card with the same radius.
noGos.instead: Flatten the inner one, or use rounded-concentric-*.
noGos.why: Nested surfaces with equal corners look misaligned at every corner.

noGos.never: <Button className="rounded-full">, <Pill className="border bg-card">, a -mx-1 separator in a popup.
noGos.instead: The component's variant (add one if it is missing); popup-bleed for the separator.
noGos.why: An override fights the component's own states and does not follow the radius ladder, the density or a theme.

noGos.never: border-2 for emphasis or focus.
noGos.instead: ring-2 ring-ring for focus; a tonal fill for emphasis.
noGos.why: A thick border shifts layout and competes with the focus ring.

foundations.title: Surfaces & elevation
foundations.summary: Depth is a step up the surface ladder, chosen by how transient a surface is. Dark mode lifts with lighter tones and edge light; light mode adds soft shadows.
foundations.headline: 4 surface tokens · 5 elevation roles · 1 shadow per surface · 1 layer scale

terms.name: bg-background
terms.use: The document body; the furthest-back surface.

terms.name: bg-card
terms.use: Resting containers: cards, panels, dialogs.

terms.name: bg-muted
terms.use: Wells, code blocks, inactive fills inside a card.

terms.name: bg-popover
terms.use: Anything that floats: menus, popovers, selects, tooltips. Always distinct from card, so a menu in a dialog never melts into it.

terms.name: bg-overlay
terms.use: Behind modals, and pills over imagery.

vocabularies.title: Elevation by role
vocabularies.note: Raise by transience — how much a surface floats over content — not by importance.

terms.name: Resting
terms.use: Page content and flat cards. A hairline border if it needs an edge.

terms.name: Raised  shadow-sm
terms.use: A draggable card, a sticky header over scrolled content.

terms.name: Floating  shadow-md
terms.use: Menus, popovers, selects, dropdowns.

terms.name: Modal  shadow-lg
terms.use: Dialogs, sheets, the command menu.

terms.name: Top  shadow-xl
terms.use: The toast stack.

terms.name: z-(--z-sticky)
terms.use: Sticky in-content chrome: table headers.

terms.name: z-(--z-nav)
terms.use: App chrome: header, sidebar, bottom nav.

terms.name: z-(--z-overlay)
terms.use: Every portaled transient surface.

terms.name: z-(--z-toast)
terms.use: Toasts, above modals.

terms.name: z-(--z-skip-link)
terms.use: The skip link, above everything.

rules.rule: Pick the elevation role, not a shadow value.
rules.why: Elevation is a five-step system. A custom box-shadow cannot follow a theme or the light/dark split.

rules.rule: Floating surfaces use bg-popover, resting ones bg-card. Anything with shadow-md or above floats: menus, popovers, selects, tooltips, dialogs, sheets, toasts, a floating panel.
rules.why: In dark mode popover is guaranteed lighter than card, so a menu opened inside a dialog always reads as on top of it. In light mode several presets make background, card and popover the same colour, so the fill alone never carries elevation.

rules.rule: A floating surface's edge is border-border-floating (or ring-border-floating), never the full border-border. The shadow carries the elevation.
rules.why: A full hairline plus a shadow stacks into a heavy dark outline. border-floating is a faint alpha edge: it defines the shape against a same-coloured page in light mode and reads as a lit edge in dark mode, where shadows barely show.

rules.rule: A recessed area inside a surface (a segmented-control track, a pad, a preview well) is sable-well, and it takes no outline. Whatever sits on the well takes the surface's own colour back (bg-popover inside a popover).
rules.why: sable-well mixes a fixed amount of ink into the surface it sits in, so it is the same visible step on the page, in a card or in a floating panel, in every theme and mode. A fixed bg-muted can nearly vanish inside a popover in dark mode, and adding an outline to every well to compensate stacks a panel into boxes.

rules.rule: One shadow per surface; never a heavy shadow with a heavy border.
rules.why: Stacked depth cues read as decoration rather than position.

rules.rule: Do not elevate a static section to make it stand out.
rules.why: Elevation means 'this floats'. Use a tonal step or space for emphasis.

rules.rule: For modals, the scrim is the primary depth cue.
rules.why: The scrim is what tells the user the page behind is inert; the shadow is secondary.

rules.rule: Stack with the named layer scale.
rules.why: Overlays portal to the end of body and order themselves by open order; the layer only has to clear in-flow chrome.

noGos.never: z-[9999] or any raw z-index.
noGos.instead: z-(--z-overlay) and the other named layers.
noGos.why: Raw z-indexes become a bidding war that a future overlay always loses.

noGos.never: shadow-[0_8px_30px_rgba(0,0,0,.2)] or any custom shadow.
noGos.instead: shadow-sm … shadow-xl by role.
noGos.why: Custom shadows ignore the theme's light/dark elevation recipes.

noGos.never: bg-card on a popover, or bg-popover on a resting card.
noGos.instead: Match the token to the role.
noGos.why: Swapping them is how floating surfaces melt into the surface beneath.

foundations.title: Motion
foundations.summary: Motion explains a change: where something came from, what responded, and that work is happening. Components ship crafted by default: one indicator travels instead of two blinking, numbers roll, ticks draw, a refused answer shakes. It is built from named recipes, comes in two levels, and one switch turns it off.
foundations.headline: 4 slots · 3 speeds · 2 levels · enter-only overshoot · 1 kill switch

vocabularies.title: Three speeds
vocabularies.note: Match duration to the distance and size of what moves. Each value is multiplied by --motion-scale. Two edge steps sit outside the three: --motion-duration-instant (75ms) for a checkbox tick or tab swap, and --motion-duration-slower (500ms) for progress and value changes.

terms.name: fast  --motion-duration-fast
terms.use: Hover, press, focus, tooltips, small toggles. Also every exit.

terms.name: base  --motion-duration-base
terms.use: Menus, popovers, tabs, disclosure. The default enter.

terms.name: slow  --motion-duration-slow
terms.use: Dialogs, sheets, page-level transitions.

vocabularies.title: Recipes
vocabularies.note: Reach for one named class before writing a transition.

terms.name: motion-interactive
terms.use: Hover/focus/press chrome on anything clickable. Replaces transition-colors.

terms.name: motion-press
terms.use: Tactile press. Always paired with motion-interactive.

terms.name: motion-fade
terms.use: Scrims and backdrops.

terms.name: motion-pop
terms.use: Anchored or centred surfaces: popovers, menus, dialogs.

terms.name: motion-slide-{up,down,left,right}
terms.use: Directional surfaces: sheets, toasts.

terms.name: motion-disclosure
terms.use: Height changes: accordion, collapsible.

terms.name: motion-icon-swap
terms.use: Two icons of one control trading places: play/pause, outline/fill, copy/check.

terms.name: motion-glide
terms.use: ONE indicator travelling to the selected option: tabs, segmented thumb, active dot.

terms.name: motion-shake
terms.use: A refused answer: wrong code, invalid submit. Plays while data-shake is set (useShake). Never the only signal.

terms.name: motion-tick
terms.use: A check mark that draws itself in. Exits only fade.

terms.name: motion-appear
terms.use: A small control mounting in place: a clear button, a send arrow, a badge. @starting-style, no JS.

terms.name: motion-arrive
terms.use: Items a user action brings into a list: a folder's children on expand, a row just added. Never on every render.

terms.name: motion-size
terms.use: An element easing between intrinsic sizes when its label changes: a two-step confirm, Copy → Copied.

terms.name: motion-bloom
terms.use: A small glyph landing in its on state: a liked heart, a picked rating, a toast's status icon. Remount it (key) to replay; never on the resting state.

terms.name: <Burst>
terms.use: The follow-through behind a bloom, in the theme's palette families. Only on a choice a person made: a like, a star, a finished task.

terms.name: motion-draw
terms.use: SVG line art drawing on when a <Reveal> scrolls in. The path needs pathLength="1"; stagger siblings with --motion-draw-delay.

terms.name: motion-spin · pulse · shimmer · dot-bounce · ping
terms.use: Activity. Scale-aware, so reduced motion freezes them.

terms.name: ease-standard
terms.use: The default for state changes.

terms.name: ease-decelerate
terms.use: Entrances: arrive fast, settle slowly.

terms.name: ease-emphasized
terms.use: Large surfaces covering a lot of distance.

terms.name: ease-spring
terms.use: A gentle pop on enter. Never on exit.

terms.name: ease-bounce
terms.use: A playful pop, opt-in only. Enter only, never on exit.

vocabularies.title: Two levels
vocabularies.note: Essential motion answers the user; expressive motion narrates continuity. Expressive durations are also multiplied by --motion-expressive, which `subtle` sets to 0. Each level can only turn motion down from what surrounds it.

terms.name: essential
terms.use: Colour and focus feedback, press, overlay arrival, disclosure height, loaders, chart hover.

terms.name: expressive
terms.use: Glides, rolling numbers (NumberTicker), drawn ticks, blooms and bursts, shakes, staggers, chart arrival and morph, scroll reveals, spring overshoot.

terms.name: full
terms.use: Both levels play. The crafted default.

terms.name: subtle
terms.use: Essential only; nothing overshoots. For dense tools, embedded widgets, readers who want calm without stillness.

terms.name: off
terms.use: Nothing moves; every state still changes.

terms.name: where
terms.use: <MotionProvider policy> for the app, <MotionScope level> for a region, `motion` on a component that owns a flourish.

vocabularies.title: The four slots
vocabularies.note: Every interactive component answers all four, by filling the slot or declining it with a reason in meta.motion.

terms.name: arrival
terms.use: How does it enter?

terms.name: response
terms.use: What happens under the pointer?

terms.name: transition
terms.use: How does it move between its own states?

terms.name: activity
terms.use: How do you tell working from frozen?

rules.rule: Every motion has a reason: orientation, feedback, continuity or activity.
rules.why: Motion with no reason is latency. If you cannot say which of the four it serves, remove it.

rules.rule: Reach for a recipe first; drop to tokens only when none fits.
rules.why: Recipes are reviewed once and respect the kill switch. A bespoke transition string is reviewed never.

rules.rule: Exits are one step faster than entrances, and never overshoot.
rules.why: Something leaving should get out of the way. A bounce on exit draws the eye to what the user just dismissed.

rules.rule: Animate opacity and transform only.
rules.why: They run on the compositor. Width, height, top and left cause layout on every frame. motion-disclosure is the one sanctioned exception.

rules.rule: Durations come from tokens, so --motion-scale can stop them.
rules.why: prefers-reduced-motion and <MotionProvider> off both set --motion-scale to 0. A raw duration ignores that.

rules.rule: Interactive elements always respond. Something styled for hover with no motion recipe snaps.
rules.why: A snap between states reads as broken. The four prohibitive rules could not catch missing motion, so this one does.

rules.rule: JS motion reads useMotion().enabled and does nothing when it is false.
rules.why: Reduced motion is an accessibility setting, not a style preference.

rules.rule: One thing travels; two things do not blink. When a selection, a value or a mark changes in place, move the one element that represents it.
rules.why: A fill switching off here and on there is two events the eye has to connect. A glide, a roll or a draw is one, and it is most of what makes an interface feel made rather than assembled.

rules.rule: Flourishes are expressive: multiply their durations by --motion-expressive and gate JS ones on useMotion().expressive.
rules.why: `subtle` promises the answers without the choreography. A glide on a plain token keeps playing after someone asked for calm.

rules.rule: A state change finishes its story: refused shakes and says why, success confirms in place, armed asks again.
rules.why: Motion that starts a change and leaves the outcome to a snap reads as unfinished. ConfirmButton, OtpField's invalid shake and the copy-to-check swap are the reference cases.

rules.rule: Amplitude scales with smallness. A 16px glyph that turns on grows from nothing past its size; a surface travels from 0.96 and a press settles to 0.97.
rules.why: The same 4% that is right for a dialog is invisible on an icon, which is why a state change on a small control used to read as a colour swap with no life in it. A dialog that overshot 20% would lurch. Size, not importance, sets how far a thing moves.

rules.rule: Stage a moment: the main object lands first, the follow-through after it.
rules.why: A ring that opens, a glyph that blooms 90ms later, dots thrown 60ms after that read as one event with a cause and an effect. Everything starting on the same frame reads as a flash. LikeButton and the toast's status glyph are the reference cases.

rules.rule: Celebrate only what a person chose, and only at full motion.
rules.why: A burst is a reply. On a like it is delight; on a system event, on load, or on every row of a list it is a notification wearing confetti. Under subtle the fill alone answers.

rules.rule: Component motion props and MotionScope only turn motion down.
rules.why: `full` on a component means inherit. Nothing below the provider can switch motion back on for a reader who asked for it off.

noGos.never: Tailwind's animate-spin / animate-pulse / animate-ping / animate-bounce.
noGos.instead: motion-spin, motion-pulse, motion-ping, motion-dot-bounce.
noGos.why: The built-ins ignore --motion-scale, so reduced motion cannot freeze them.

noGos.never: duration-150, duration-300, or any raw duration utility.
noGos.instead: duration-(--motion-duration-fast) and siblings.
noGos.why: Raw durations bypass the kill switch.

noGos.never: transition-all, or transition-colors on its own.
noGos.instead: motion-interactive, or name the properties you animate.
noGos.why: transition-all animates unrelated layout changes and defeats the browser's pre-computation.

noGos.never: Motion on first paint of static content, or staggered entrances on every list.
noGos.instead: Reveal for one deliberate moment per view.
noGos.why: Entrance choreography repeated everywhere becomes a loading delay.

noGos.never: The motion library in the core package.
noGos.instead: src/motion (WAAPI, IntersectionObserver, View Transitions).
noGos.why: Sable's motion layer is zero-dependency; drag, FLIP and velocity springs belong in an optional adapter.

foundations.title: Scrolling
foundations.summary: Every scroll container declares a policy. Vertical regions get a quiet bar that appears only while you are in them; horizontal strips get edge fades instead of a rail.
foundations.headline: 2 policies · vertical gets a bar · horizontal gets a fade

terms.name: scrollbar-quiet
terms.value: 4px thumb · hidden at rest → 12% active → 16% hovered → 20% dragging
terms.use: The default for vertical scrolling. Grows to 6px under the pointer.

terms.name: scrollbar-hidden
terms.use: Only when something else carries the affordance — and you can name it (an edge fade, paging controls).

terms.name: <Scroller>
terms.use: Horizontal strips: media rows, chip rows, tab overflow.

terms.name: useScrollActivity
terms.use: Lets the bar respond to touch drags and programmatic scrolls, which hover cannot see.

rules.rule: Every overflow-*-auto|scroll declares scrollbar-quiet or scrollbar-hidden.
rules.why: Left bare, the platform draws its own: on Windows, stepper arrows hard against the padding edge that poke out of rounded corners.
rules.enforcedBy: sable-lint: unmanaged-overflow (also checked over every registry example)

rules.rule: Vertical regions get a bar; horizontal regions get an edge fade.
rules.why: A vertical list needs position feedback. A horizontal strip needs 'there is more this way', which a fade says better than a 4px rail.

rules.rule: A horizontal region must work without a horizontal input.
rules.why: Most mice have no horizontal wheel. Scroller maps the vertical wheel sideways and handles arrow keys, Home and End.

rules.rule: Reveal on scrolling, not only on hover.
rules.why: Touch drags and programmatic scrolls (a chat following a reply) hover nothing, and those are the moments a reader needs to see where they are.

noGos.never: scrollbar-hidden on a vertical list with no fade or paging.
noGos.instead: scrollbar-quiet.
noGos.why: It leaves the reader with no sense of position and nothing to discover.

noGos.never: A styled ::-webkit-scrollbar written per component.
noGos.instead: The scrollbar-quiet utility.
noGos.why: Chromium ignores ::-webkit-scrollbar once scrollbar-width is set; the utility handles both engines.

foundations.title: Accessibility
foundations.summary: Sable's components ship accessible behavior from Base UI. These rules cover what an app composing them still has to get right.
foundations.headline: WCAG AA · 44px targets · visible focus · reduced motion · logical properties

terms.name: Contrast
terms.use: Every semantic text/surface pair is checked per theme by contrast.test.ts.

terms.name: Hit area
terms.use: hit-target keeps a small control at the floor without moving layout.

terms.name: Focus
terms.use: Visible on every interactive element, in light, dark and forced-colors.

terms.name: Mobile input text
terms.use: iOS Safari zooms the page on focus below it.

terms.name: Reduced motion
terms.use: Transitions resolve instantly; loaders hold their first frame.

rules.rule: Use the component, not a div with a click handler.
rules.why: Base UI supplies roles, keyboard handling and focus management. A clickable div has none of them.

rules.rule: Every control has an accessible name.
rules.why: Icon-only buttons take aria-label. Fields take a <Label> through <Field>, which also wires aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

rules.rule: A live region exists before it has anything to say.
rules.why: Render role="status" empty from the start and swap its text. A region inserted together with its content is announced inconsistently.

rules.rule: On client-side navigation, update document.title and move focus to the new view's h1.
rules.why: Route changes are silent to assistive technology unless the app announces them. AppShell supplies the skip link and landmarks; the app does the rest.

rules.rule: Keep submit enabled; validate on submit and focus the first invalid field.
rules.why: A disabled submit hides why it is disabled. Focus is the only way a screen-reader user finds the error.

rules.rule: Use logical properties: ms-/me-/ps-/pe-/text-start/inset-inline-*.
rules.why: Flex and grid mirror for free under dir="rtl"; hand-positioned elements do not.

rules.rule: Decorative layers over content take pointer-events-none and aria-hidden.
rules.why: Scrims, glows and fades otherwise swallow clicks on the controls beneath.

rules.rule: Check focus and disabled states under forced-colors: active.
rules.why: Windows High Contrast overrides ring colors and erases opacity-based disabled styling.

noGos.never: Color as the only signal (a red border with no message).
noGos.instead: Color plus text or an icon.
noGos.why: Roughly 1 in 12 men cannot tell red from green.

noGos.never: Opacity on the focus ring.
noGos.instead: ring-ring at full opacity; tune the token in the theme.
noGos.why: A faded ring loses the contrast the theme tested.

noGos.never: A brand or status fill retuned under its old label — dark ink on a bright red that passes 4.5:1 at APCA Lc 42.
noGos.instead: A label that clears 4.5:1 and APCA Lc 60 in both modes. Move the fill's lightness, not its hue, keeping the ink its colour takes. A status colour on a surface is its own token (`--destructive-text`), so the fill can move freely.
noGos.why: The ratio alone passes labels that read muddy. A deliberate brand pair is allowed with a recorded reason (lint disable or preset exceptions).

noGos.never: A label fill painted on a mark that carries no text — a meter, a segmented bar, a status dot, a chart series, a soft tint.
noGos.instead: The colour's `-mark` token (`bg-success-mark`, `bg-tone-warning-mark/15`): the same hue lifted and saturated, held to 2:1 on the page. Text contrast is for text; a graphic owes visibility, and 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) only when it is the sole carrier of its meaning.
noGos.why: A fill is pinned dark enough for a white label. On a bar or dot with nothing to label, that darkness only reads as mud: a brown warning, a forest-green success.

noGos.never: Blocking paste, or type="number" for codes and card numbers.
noGos.instead: type="text" inputMode="numeric" with the right autocomplete.
noGos.why: Blocking paste breaks password managers; number inputs scroll-change identifiers.

noGos.never: forced-color-adjust: none to 'fix' high-contrast mode.
noGos.instead: Let the system colors apply; verify the result.
noGos.why: It removes the user's chosen colors exactly where they need them.

noGos.never: outline: none without a replacement.
noGos.instead: focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring.
noGos.why: Keyboard users lose their place.

utilities.about: The CSS layer between tokens and components: relative surfaces that derive hover and well fills from the surface they sit in, frames that compute concentric inner radii, state variants that match Base UI data attributes and ARIA alike, scroll policies, chrome type tiers, and the motion recipes. Reach for these before hand-writing CSS, mixing colours or writing a transition. Generated from src/utilities/utility-docs.ts — do not hand-edit.

elsewhere.typography: The paired `text-*` page tiers (`text-heading-1`, `text-body-md`, `text-label-sm`, `text-mono-md`, …) are documented as `registry.json → tokens.typography` (named without the `text-` prefix). Retrieve one with `sable utility text-heading-1`, all with `sable token typography`.

items.name: sable-surface
items.intent: Paints an element as a semantic surface (card by default) and DERIVES its hover and active fills from it — background, ink, edge and both state colours from one role.
items.whenToUse: A bespoke container whose rows or buttons need hover/selected fills that sit the right step off the container in every theme. Pick the role with a modifier (`sable-surface-muted`, `-popover`, `-accent`); descendants using `sable-surface-interactive` or `sable-well` then compute against it.
items.insteadOf: `bg-card text-card-foreground border-border` plus a hand-mixed hover like `hover:bg-[color-mix(in_oklab,var(--foreground)_8%,var(--card))]`.
