The utility computes the same mix from whatever role you pick, so it stays one visible step in every preset and mode. Use a component (`Card`, `Panel`) first when one fits.

items.name: sable-surface-muted
items.intent: Switches a `sable-surface` to the `muted` role: recessed background, `foreground` ink, `border` edge. Sets the surface variables only; it does not paint on its own.
items.whenToUse: With `sable-surface`, for a quiet, recessed container whose interactive rows still need derived hover/selected fills.
items.insteadOf: `bg-muted` alone, which leaves descendants' hover fills computed against the wrong surface. For a small recessed area INSIDE another surface (a track, a pad) use `sable-well` instead.

items.name: sable-surface-popover
items.intent: Switches the surface context to the `popover` role (popover fill and ink, `border-floating` edge). Sets the variables only, so it can also be used ALONE to declare 'descendants sit on a popover'.
items.whenToUse: On a hand-composed floating panel (an inspector, a toolbar over a canvas) so `sable-well` and `sable-surface-interactive` inside it derive from the popover rather than the page. Alone, alongside `bg-popover text-popover-foreground`, it is purely that context hint; with `sable-surface` it also paints.
items.insteadOf: leaving the context unset. Then `sable-well` falls back to `--background`, which inside a popover in some dark modes lands within a step of the panel: the bug that tempts an outline on every well.
items.example: <aside className="sable-surface-popover bg-popover text-popover-foreground rounded-lg ring-1 ring-border-floating shadow-lg">…</aside>

items.name: sable-surface-accent
items.intent: Switches a `sable-surface` to the `accent` role: the transient-state fill with its paired ink. Sets the variables only.
items.whenToUse: With `sable-surface`, for a container that is itself in a highlighted/current state and still hosts interactive rows whose hover must step off it.
items.insteadOf: `bg-accent text-accent-foreground` on a container whose children then hover against the page colour. Accent is a STATE, not a decoration — don't use it to make a static section stand out.

items.name: sable-surface-interactive
items.intent: Hover / highlighted and pressed / selected fills for a row or button, derived from the surface it sits on. Hover = the surface's hover step (8% ink); active, selected or checked = its active step (12% ink inside a `sable-surface`, `accent` outside one).
items.whenToUse: A clickable row, list item or bespoke button inside a surface, where the hover colour must be one consistent step off THAT surface. Matches `:hover`, `[data-highlighted]` / `[data-active]` and `:active`, `[data-selected]` / `[data-checked]` / `aria-selected` / `aria-checked`, so Base UI items work without extra variants. Pair with `motion-interactive` for the transition.
items.insteadOf: `hover:bg-accent`, `hover:bg-muted` or a hand-written `color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 8%, …)` hover. A fixed hover token is right on one surface and invisible or loud on the next; this one is computed from where the row actually is. Reach for `ListItem`, `Menu` or `Button variant="ghost"` first when they fit.
items.example: <button className="sable-surface-interactive sable-frame-inner motion-interactive px-3 py-2 text-start text-body-sm">Rename</button>

items.name: sable-well
items.intent: A recessed area ON whatever surface it sits in: 7% ink mixed into the inherited surface (`--sable-surface-bg`, the page background by default), so it is the same visible step on the page, in a card or in a popover.
items.whenToUse: A segmented-control track, a colour or XY pad, a preview well, a readout block inside a panel. Sable's Card (default), Popover, Dialog and Sheet declare their surface, so a well inside them derives from them automatically; on a hand-composed panel, put `sable-surface-popover` (or set `--sable-surface-bg`) on the panel yourself. Whatever sits ON the well takes the surface's own colour back (`bg-popover` inside a popover). A well takes no outline.
items.insteadOf: `bg-muted`, which is fixed: inside a popover it can sit within a step of the panel in some dark modes. And never a hand-mixed `color-mix(… var(--foreground) …)` or an outline on every well to compensate — that turns a panel into a stack of boxes. For a segmented control itself, use `ToggleGroup`; the well is for what no component draws.

items.name: sable-frame
items.intent: A bordered, padded, rounded container that computes the radius its children need: `--sable-frame-inner-radius` = radius − padding − border width, floored at `radius-sm`.
items.whenToUse: A container whose children have their own rounded backgrounds (rows, tiles, a nested preview), so the corners nest concentrically and keep doing so when the radius ladder is rescaled. Defaults: `radius-lg`, `--spacing(4)` padding (1rem at the default scale, and it follows the density control), a 1px edge from the surface (`--sable-surface-edge`, else `border`). Size it with `sable-frame-r-*` / `sable-frame-p-*`; children take `sable-frame-inner`.
items.insteadOf: `rounded-lg p-4 border` on the parent plus a guessed `rounded-sm` on each child — the guess is concentric only at the default ladder. For a one-off nested corner without a frame, `rounded-concentric-*`.
items.example: …

items.name: sable-frame-popover
items.intent: The popup frame recipe: `radius-md`, `--spacing(1)` padding, the `border-floating` edge and `shadow-lg`, applied over `sable-frame`.
items.whenToUse: A hand-composed floating list or panel that must match Sable's menus (with `sable-frame sable-surface sable-surface-popover`); rows inside take `sable-frame-inner`.
items.insteadOf: Copying a Menu's class string. And use `Menu`, `Select`, `Popover` or `Combobox` first — they own focus and dismissal; this is only for floating chrome no component covers.

items.name: sable-frame-tool
items.intent: The frame for edge-to-edge tool chrome at the theme's radius, with no padding. It publishes concentric geometry for what's inside: `--panel-inset` (row side padding, grown so rows clear the corner), `--panel-field-radius` (compact fields curve parallel to the frame) and `--panel-edge` (the first and last section's extra top and bottom). PanelSection and the xs field shell read them. Applied over `sable-frame`.
items.whenToUse: Framing PanelSections, ScrubFields, a Tree, a StatusBar or a PanelGroup outside a Workspace (a docs demo, a floating inspector). Add `overflow-hidden` to clip to the corners.
items.insteadOf: `rounded-lg border overflow-hidden` by hand: the panel keeps its square-column 8px inset and small field radius, so a rounded preset crowds the first label and last field into the curve.
items.example: …

items.name: sable-frame-borderless
items.intent: Sets a `sable-frame`'s border width to 0 while keeping the inner-radius math correct.
items.whenToUse: A frame that separates by fill or space rather than an edge (a well, a tinted group) but still needs concentric children.
items.insteadOf: `border-0` on a `sable-frame`, which removes the border but leaves 1px in the inner-radius calculation.

items.name: sable-frame-r-*
items.intent: Sets a `sable-frame`'s outer radius from the radius ladder (`sable-frame-r-lg`) or an arbitrary value (`sable-frame-r-[14px]`).
items.whenToUse: Whenever a frame should not be the default `radius-lg`. The inner radius follows automatically.
items.insteadOf: `rounded-*` on a `sable-frame` — that changes the painted corner but not `--sable-frame-inner-radius`, so the children stop nesting.

items.name: sable-frame-p-*
items.intent: Sets a `sable-frame`'s padding on the spacing scale (`sable-frame-p-2` = `--spacing(2)`), feeding the inner-radius math. On the scale, so the density control moves it.
items.whenToUse: Whenever a frame's inset is not the default `--spacing(4)`.
items.insteadOf: `p-*` on a `sable-frame` — the padding changes but the inner radius is still computed from the default `--spacing(4)`, so the children's corners are wrong.

items.name: sable-frame-inner
items.intent: Takes the radius its `sable-frame` ancestor computed (outer − inset − border), never below `radius-sm`: concentric when the child sits near the frame edge (a popover row), the theme's small radius when it sits deep inside a padded card (where the subtraction would leave a near-square row). Falls back to `radius-sm` outside a frame.
items.whenToUse: On every rounded child of a `sable-frame`: rows, tiles, an inner well, a nested image.
items.insteadOf: A hardcoded `rounded-sm` on the child, which drifts the moment a theme or the customizer rescales radii.

items.name: rounded-concentric-*
items.intent: A border radius computed as an outer radius minus an inset: `rounded-concentric-<radius>/<spacing>`, floored at `radius-xs` so a deep inset never leaves a 1-2px sliver. `rounded-concentric-md/1` = `radius-md` − `spacing-1`.
items.whenToUse: A one-off rounded element nested inside another — a tab trigger inside a tab list, a thumb inside a track, a row inside a well — where a `sable-frame` would be overkill. The outer radius and the inset are the parent's.
items.insteadOf: Picking the next ladder step down by eye (`rounded-sm` inside `rounded-md p-1`). That is concentric only at the default ladder; the utility recomputes from live tokens. Registered in `cn()` as a radius, so it correctly overrides a component's own `rounded-*`.

items.name: popup-inset
items.intent: The padding of a popup list, derived from the popup's radius: a third of `radius-md`, at least `--spacing(1)`. A rounder popup gets more room, and the floor is on the spacing scale, so the density control moves it.
items.whenToUse: On a hand-composed rounded-md popup that holds a list of rows. Sable's Menu, Select, Combobox and ContextMenu already use it.
items.insteadOf: `p-1`. A fixed inset at a larger radius preset leaves the rows' corners approaching half their height, so every row turns into a pill.

items.name: rounded-popup-item
items.intent: The row radius that nests inside a `popup-inset` popup: `radius-md` minus the popup inset, clamped at zero.
items.whenToUse: On every row inside a `popup-inset` container.
items.insteadOf: `rounded-sm` on menu rows, which matches no ladder exactly (a 12px popup with a 4px inset and 1px border wants 7px rows).

items.name: popup-bleed
items.intent: A negative inline margin of exactly one `popup-inset`, so a separator inside a padded popup runs edge to edge at every radius and density.
items.whenToUse: On a hand-composed separator (a 1px rule) inside a `popup-inset` popup. Sable's MenuSeparator, ContextMenuSeparator and SelectSeparator already use it.
items.insteadOf: `-mx-1`, which matches the inset only at the default ladder and stops short of both edges once a rounder preset or a roomier density grows it. design-lint flags it (`popup-separator-bleed`).

items.name: sable-highlighted
items.intent: A variant (`sable-highlighted:`) matching the keyboard/pointer-highlighted item: `[data-highlighted]`, `[data-active]`, `[data-active-item]`.
items.whenToUse: Styling the current item in a list, menu, combobox or listbox — Base UI and ARIA-style composites mark it differently, this matches all of them.
items.insteadOf: `data-[highlighted]:bg-accent data-[active]:bg-accent …` repeated per attribute, or `hover:` alone (which misses keyboard navigation).

items.name: sable-selected
items.intent: A variant (`sable-selected:`) matching a selected or checked element: `[data-selected]`, `[data-checked]`, `[aria-selected=true]`, `[aria-checked=true]`.
items.whenToUse: The chosen row, the pressed segment, the checked option — whichever attribute the primitive happens to set.
items.insteadOf: Separate `data-[selected]:` / `data-[checked]:` / `aria-selected:` classes, one of which is always forgotten.

items.name: sable-open
items.intent: A variant (`sable-open:`) matching an open trigger or disclosure: `[data-open]`, `[data-popup-open]`, `[data-panel-open]`, `[aria-expanded=true]`.
items.whenToUse: Rotating a chevron, holding a trigger's pressed look while its menu or panel is open.
items.insteadOf: `data-[popup-open]:` on one trigger and `aria-expanded:` on the next.

items.name: sable-disabled
items.intent: A variant (`sable-disabled:`) matching a disabled element: `:disabled`, `[disabled]`, `[data-disabled]`, `[aria-disabled=true]`.
items.whenToUse: Dimming or locking a bespoke element regardless of whether it is natively or ARIA-disabled.
items.insteadOf: `disabled:` alone, which misses `aria-disabled` and Base UI's `data-disabled` — the cases that stay focusable.

items.name: sable-invalid
items.intent: A variant (`sable-invalid:`) matching an invalid field: `[aria-invalid=true]`, `[data-invalid]`.
items.whenToUse: The error edge or ink on a bespoke field wrapper. Use `Field` / `Input` first; they already style it.
items.insteadOf: `aria-invalid:` or `data-[invalid]:` alone — Base UI's Field sets one, native validation wiring the other.

items.name: scrollbar-quiet
items.intent: A thin floating scrollbar: no stepper arrows, a 4px thumb inset from the edges, invisible at rest and fading in while the region is scrolled, hovered or focused.
items.whenToUse: Every VERTICAL scroll container (anything with `overflow-y: auto` or `scroll`). Add `useScrollActivity` so the thumb also appears on touch drags and programmatic scrolls. Required by design-lint's `unmanaged-overflow`.
items.insteadOf: A scroll container with no policy, which on Windows draws stepper arrows hard against the padding edge and out of any rounded corner. Never set `scrollbar-width` yourself — in Chromium it disables this utility.

items.name: scrollbar-hidden
items.intent: Scrolls without ever drawing a bar.
items.whenToUse: HORIZONTAL strips whose edge fade or paging controls carry the 'there is more' affordance (it is `Scroller`'s horizontal default), a canvas panned by drag. You should be able to name what carries the affordance instead.
items.insteadOf: `scrollbar-quiet` on a vertical list. A vertical region with no bar and no fade tells a reader nothing about how far through they are.

items.name: sable-list
items.intent: A bulleted list as typography: body type, a hanging muted marker, and item rhythm. Put it on a native `<ul>`.
items.whenToUse: Running content with bullets: release notes, a feature list, steps that are not ordered.
items.insteadOf: A stack of `<div>`s with a hand-drawn dot, or an unstyled `<ul>` that inherits the reset (no markers, no indent).

items.name: sable-list-numbered
items.intent: A numbered list as typography: `sable-list` with decimal markers in tabular figures. Put it on a native `<ol>`.
items.whenToUse: Ordered content in running text: setup steps, a ranked list. For a stepped flow with state, use Stepper.
items.insteadOf: Numbers typed into the text, which neither renumber nor read as a list to assistive tech.

items.name: sable-list-dl
items.intent: Label/value pairs on a native `<dl>`: muted label-tier `<dt>`s and body-tier `<dd>`s on a baseline-aligned two-column grid; long values wrap inside their column. Colour a status value with a `text-*` utility on its `<dd>`.
items.whenToUse: Read-only details: an order summary, a record's metadata, a settings summary, profile stats.
items.insteadOf: A grid of `<div>`s (screen readers lose the term/value pairing), or Table for a single record. For editable values use Form and Field.

items.name: sable-list-dl-2
items.intent: Two label/value pairs a row once the nearest `@container` ancestor is at least 28rem wide. Add to `sable-list-dl`.
items.whenToUse: A compact metadata block in a wide card or panel. Put `@container` on a parent so it measures the room it actually has.
items.insteadOf: A viewport breakpoint, which gives a narrow card on a wide screen four columns it cannot fit.

items.name: text-overline
items.intent: The eyebrow / overline / kicker tier: small, letter-spaced, uppercase by default (a theme may set sentence case via `--type-overline-transform`).
items.whenToUse: A section eyebrow above a heading, a stat's label, a badge-style category line. Sits ABOVE and categorises.
items.insteadOf: `text-label-xs uppercase tracking-wider` assembled by hand, or `text-caption`, which sits BELOW and explains. In tool chrome, panel headers use `text-ui-section` instead.

items.name: text-ui-title
items.intent: The title of what a panel or inspector shows — the open issue, the selected object: 14px at 600 on a 20px line, one step above `text-ui-md`.
items.whenToUse: The one title at the top of an inspector, a docked panel or a peek view inside the workspace register. Compact `text-title-lg` resolves to it on its own.
items.insteadOf: `text-ui-md` made heavier (a title the size of the description under it reads as a label), or `text-heading-*`, which is page structure rather than chrome.

items.name: text-ui-md
items.intent: Workspace-register chrome text, the default tier: ~12px at weight ~500 on 16px leading.
items.whenToUse: Labels and values in tool chrome — panels, inspectors, toolbars, trees — inside the workspace register.
items.insteadOf: `text-label-sm` or `text-body-sm` in a dense panel (the page register's weights read as shouting at this size), or a size class plus a weight class composed by hand.

items.name: text-ui-sm
items.intent: Workspace chrome text, the compact tier: ~11px at weight ~500.
items.whenToUse: Secondary chrome: property names in a grid, status-bar items, tree rows in a compact density.
items.insteadOf: `text-label-xs`, a page-register tier tuned for different weights and leading.

items.name: text-ui-body
items.intent: The reading tier inside chrome: `text-ui-md`'s size at regular weight.
items.whenToUse: Descriptions, help text and empty-state copy inside a panel or inspector.
items.insteadOf: `text-ui-md`, whose medium weight makes a sentence read as a label; or `text-body-sm`, which is page-register.
items.example: Select a layer to edit its properties.

items.name: text-ui-section
items.intent: Panel section headers in tool chrome: `text-ui-sm`'s size, a little heavier and tracked — not uppercase.
items.whenToUse: A `PanelSection` header or any group title inside a dense panel.
items.insteadOf: `text-overline`, whose all-caps reads louder than the content it labels at this density.

items.name: text-ui-micro
items.intent: The smallest chrome tier: ~10px at weight ~450. Use sparingly.
items.whenToUse: Chrome annotations — a unit suffix, a shortcut hint, a ruler tick label.
items.insteadOf: `text-[10px]`, which bypasses the theme and density hooks.

items.name: text-ui-num
items.intent: Numeric values in chrome: mono, tabular figures, at the `text-ui-sm` size.
items.whenToUse: Values in a property grid, a scrub field's readout, coordinates — any number that changes while you watch.
items.insteadOf: `text-ui-sm` (proportional digits make a column jitter while a slider drags) or `text-mono-sm`, which is page-register.

items.name: stream-tail
items.intent: The soft trailing edge of a live text stream: a slight blur plus a fading mask, so the newest token reads as 'more is coming' rather than a sentence that has ended. Static.
items.whenToUse: On the last run of text while a model or source is still streaming; remove it when the stream finishes. `StreamingText` applies it for you.
items.insteadOf: An animated fade or a hand-written `mask-image` gradient. Use `StreamingText` first; this is for a stream rendered without it.

items.name: motion-interactive
items.intent: The transition for interactive chrome: colour, background, border, shadow, opacity, fill, stroke, scale and translate at the fast duration and standard easing. Also removes the mobile tap delay and the platform's grey tap flash.
items.whenToUse: On anything clickable that changes on hover, focus, press or selection: a custom row, a tile, a link, an app-owned button. It is the `response` slot, and the only transition declarer such an element needs.
items.insteadOf: Tailwind's colour-only or all-property transition utilities with a hand-picked duration. Those ignore --motion-scale, skip the transform properties `motion-press` needs, and leave the 300ms tap delay on touch screens. sable-lint's `static-interactive` fires on a hover style with no recipe.

items.name: motion-press
items.intent: A small tactile settle (scale 0.97) while the element is pressed. Skips disabled elements. Declares only the pressed state, not a transition.
items.whenToUse: A pressable surface that is not a Sable Button (Button already has it): a tile, a card that acts as a button, an icon control.
items.insteadOf: An `active:` scale utility with its own transition, which fights `motion-interactive` for the transition property and keeps animating with motion off.
items.example: <button type="button" className="motion-interactive motion-press sable-surface sable-frame sable-frame-r-lg sable-frame-p-4">Open</button>

items.name: motion-fade
items.intent: Opacity-only enter and exit, keyed to Base UI's `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style`: fades in at the enter duration, out at the exit duration.
items.whenToUse: Scrims, backdrops and overlays that should appear without moving. The element rests visible; the data attributes supply the from and to.
items.insteadOf: A keyframe fade or a conditional opacity class, which cannot animate the exit of an element Base UI is unmounting.

items.name: motion-pop
items.intent: Enter with a slight scale from the anchor edge (spring easing) and exit faster without overshoot, keyed to `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style`. Scales from Base UI's `--transform-origin`.
items.whenToUse: Anchored or centred floating surfaces: popovers, menus, selects, tooltips, dialogs, command menus. Sable's own overlays already carry it.
items.insteadOf: A custom zoom keyframe, or a spring on exit, which draws the eye to what the user just dismissed.
items.example: …

items.name: motion-slide-up
items.intent: Fade plus a 0.5rem rise on enter, reversed faster on exit, keyed to `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style`. The suffix is the travel direction on enter.
items.whenToUse: A surface arriving from below: a toast at the bottom of the screen, a bottom bar, a banner under its trigger.
items.insteadOf: A translate keyframe with a literal duration, which keeps moving under reduced motion.

items.name: motion-slide-down
items.intent: Fade plus a 0.5rem drop on enter, reversed faster on exit, keyed to `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style`.
items.whenToUse: A surface arriving from above: a top toast, a dropdown panel that reads better sliding than scaling.
items.insteadOf: A translate keyframe with a literal duration.

items.name: motion-slide-left
items.intent: Fade plus a 0.5rem travel leftward on enter (it starts offset to the right), reversed faster on exit.
items.whenToUse: A surface arriving from the right edge: a side panel, a right-anchored toast.
items.insteadOf: A translate keyframe with a literal duration.

items.name: motion-slide-right
items.intent: Fade plus a 0.5rem travel rightward on enter (it starts offset to the left), reversed faster on exit.
items.whenToUse: A surface arriving from the left edge: a navigation drawer, a left-anchored toast.
items.insteadOf: A translate keyframe with a literal duration.

items.name: motion-disclosure
items.intent: Height plus fade for a panel that opens and closes: carries the overflow, the transition and the content fade. The component sets the target height and zeroes it on the starting/ending style.
items.whenToUse: A hand-built expanding region. Accordion and Collapsible already use it; reach for them first.
items.insteadOf: Animating max-height to a guessed number, or a show/hide with no transition. Height is the one sanctioned non-compositor property.

items.name: motion-icon-swap
items.intent: Cross-fades two glyphs stacked in one cell when a control's icon changes with its state: the outgoing one shrinks and blurs out, the incoming one resolves in. The inactive glyph is the one marked `aria-hidden="true"` (or `data-active="false"`).
items.whenToUse: Play/pause, mute/unmute, outline/fill, copy/check, menu/close: one control whose icon changes. Keep both icons mounted; the correct accessibility markup is also the animation hook.
items.insteadOf: Rendering one icon or the other (it snaps between two frames), or absolutely positioning the second icon, which collapses the wrapper. Under reduced motion the swap is instant and the glyph still changes.

items.name: motion-glide
items.intent: Timing for ONE element that travels to the selected option — position and size ease on the emphasized curve at the slow step. Expressive: `data-motion="subtle"` makes it snap.
items.whenToUse: A selection indicator you position yourself: a custom nav's current-page bar, a segmented control's thumb, an active dot. Tabs, ToggleGroup `segmented`, ThemeSwitcher and Carousel already glide.
items.insteadOf: A fill or border on each option that switches on and off (two things blink instead of one thing moving), or a hand-written transition with a literal duration.
items.example: <span aria-hidden className="motion-glide absolute bottom-0 h-0.5 bg-foreground" style={{ left: x, width: w }} />

items.name: motion-shake
items.intent: A short decaying horizontal shake that plays while `data-shake` is set. `useShake()` sets and clears the attribute and restarts it on a repeat refusal. Expressive: under `subtle` only the error colour remains.
items.whenToUse: An answer the system refused: a wrong one-time code, a submit with invalid fields, a rejected password. Always alongside the error colour and message, never instead of them. OtpField's `invalid` already shakes.
items.insteadOf: A keyframe shake with a literal duration, which keeps moving under reduced motion, or a shake with no error text.
items.example:
const { shake, shakeProps } = useShake()
<form className="motion-shake" {...shakeProps} onSubmit={(e) => { if (!valid) { e.preventDefault(); shake() } }}>…</form>

items.name: motion-tick
items.intent: A selection mark that draws itself in from its leading edge (a clip-path wipe, so it works on any icon set) with an essential fade, keyed to Base UI's starting/ending style. Exits only fade. The wipe is expressive.
items.whenToUse: A check or success glyph that mounts with its state: a custom selection card's tick, a completed step. Checkbox and CheckboxCard already use it.
items.insteadOf: A scale-from-zero pop on a check mark, which reads as a stamp rather than a tick, or a path-length draw that needs to own the SVG.

items.name: motion-appear
items.intent: Fades and scales a small control in on first render through `@starting-style` — no data attribute, no JS. The fade is essential, the scale is expressive. Removal is instant.
items.whenToUse: A control that mounts in place as state changes: a search field's clear button, a send button replacing a mic, a count badge that appears. Put it on a wrapper around a Sable Button or anything carrying `motion-interactive`, so the two do not fight over `transition-property`.
items.insteadOf: Conditionally rendering a control so it pops in on one frame, or wrapping a single icon button in Presence.
items.example: {value && }

items.name: motion-arrive
items.intent: Items a user action brings into a list settle into place one after another: a short fade down from 0.25rem. Stagger with `--motion-arrive-delay` (raw ms; the recipe scales it). Expressive.
items.whenToUse: Only on items that are NEW because of something the user did: a folder's children on expand, a row just added, results that load in. Tree's expand already uses it.
items.insteadOf: A staggered entrance on every render of a list, which turns a list into a loading delay, or an inline keyframe animation with literal durations.

items.name: motion-bloom
items.intent: A small glyph landing in its "on" state grows from nothing past its size (1.2) and settles. The amplitude a 16px glyph needs to read as an event; surfaces never bloom. A keyframe that plays on mount, so remount the glyph (a changing `key`) to replay it. `--motion-bloom-delay` holds it at nothing first (raw ms; the recipe scales it). Expressive.
items.whenToUse: A glyph that a person's choice turns on: a liked heart, a starred item, a status icon arriving in a toast. LikeButton and Toast already use it. Pair with <Burst> for the follow-through on a celebratory toggle.
items.insteadOf: A bigger motion-press or motion-pop on the whole control (a button or card that overshoots 20% lurches), or a hand-written scale keyframe with literal durations. Never on the resting state: a page that loads with a post already liked must not bloom every heart.

items.name: motion-size
items.intent: Eases an element between sizes: between a keyword and a length (0 ↔ auto) through `interpolate-size: allow-keywords`, and between measured pixel sizes when paired with `useAutoSize()`, so a button whose label changes stretches to the new width instead of jumping. A superset of motion-interactive's transition list, so it can sit on a Button. The size is expressive.
items.whenToUse: A control whose content changes length in place: a two-step confirm button, a Copy → Copied label, a chip that gains a count. ConfirmButton already uses it.
items.insteadOf: A hand-written width transition, or a fixed width that clips the longer label. A content-sized box computes `width: auto` before and after its label changes, so on its own the recipe has nothing to ease — that is what `useAutoSize()` is for.
items.example: const size = useAutoSize()

items.name: motion-spin
items.intent: A continuous rotation for a spinner glyph, scaled by --motion-scale so reduced motion freezes it.
items.whenToUse: A loading glyph that is not the Spinner component (use Spinner first), such as an icon inside a busy button.
items.insteadOf: Tailwind's built-in spin animation, which ignores --motion-scale. sable-lint's `builtin-animate` flags it.

items.name: motion-orbit
items.intent: A slow continuous rotation (24s by default) for ambient line art. `--motion-orbit-duration` sets the speed and `--motion-orbit-direction` the direction; it rotates about the centre of any viewBox.
items.whenToUse: The idle loop of an illustration or schematic after it draws on, usually with `motion-draw` on the same figure.
items.insteadOf: `motion-spin`, which is a loader's speed, or a hand-written keyframe that keeps turning under reduced motion.

items.name: motion-pulse
items.intent: A soft looping opacity pulse, scaled by --motion-scale.
items.whenToUse: A live or pending indicator: a recording dot, an unsaved marker, a pending status.
items.insteadOf: Tailwind's built-in pulse animation, which ignores --motion-scale. For a loading placeholder use Skeleton or `motion-shimmer`.

items.name: motion-shimmer
items.intent: The skeleton sweep: one band of light that passes across every skeleton on screen in sequence, because the gradient is fixed to the viewport. Rests off-screen, so with motion off a skeleton is a calm block.
items.whenToUse: A hand-built loading placeholder. The Skeleton component already uses it.
items.insteadOf: A pulse on each block, or a per-box gradient, where a short line and a tall card sweep at different speeds.

items.name: motion-text-shimmer
items.intent: The sweep run through the glyphs instead of behind them, for a live status line. The gradient goes muted to foreground and back, so the text stays readable on every frame.
items.whenToUse: Status text while work is happening: "Thinking…", "Searching", "Generating response".
items.insteadOf: `motion-shimmer` on text, which paints a band behind real words and reads as a skeleton. Named `motion-*`, not `text-*`, so tailwind-merge does not drop the colour class beside it.

items.name: motion-dot-bounce
items.intent: A looping vertical bounce for one dot of a typing or waiting indicator. Offset each dot with an animation delay.
items.whenToUse: A three-dot typing indicator in a chat or assistant surface.
items.insteadOf: Tailwind's built-in bounce animation, which ignores --motion-scale.

items.name: motion-ping
items.intent: A looping ring that expands and fades from a point, scaled by --motion-scale.
items.whenToUse: Drawing attention to a live point: a new-activity dot, a location marker, a beacon behind a status dot.
items.insteadOf: Tailwind's built-in ping animation, which ignores --motion-scale.

items.name: animate-fade-in
items.intent: A one-shot fade in on mount at the base duration, decelerating, with `both` fill so there is no flash before it starts.
items.whenToUse: Content that appears once when a route or panel mounts.
items.insteadOf: A keyframe with a literal duration. For content entering on scroll use Reveal (`motion-reveal`).

items.name: animate-fade-up
items.intent: A one-shot fade plus rise on mount at the slow duration, decelerating, with `both` fill.
items.whenToUse: A page section or list arriving from below on mount.
items.insteadOf: A translate keyframe with a literal duration. For scroll-triggered entrances use Reveal.

items.name: animate-fade-down
items.intent: A one-shot fade plus drop on mount at the slow duration, decelerating, with `both` fill.
items.whenToUse: Content arriving from above on mount, such as a notice under a header.
items.insteadOf: A translate keyframe with a literal duration.

items.name: motion-stream-in
items.intent: Each token of a live stream resolves in from a slight blur once, on mount. Knows nothing of the final length, so there is no stagger.
items.whenToUse: Wrapping each arriving chunk of a streamed response. StreamingText already does it.
items.insteadOf: The reveal recipes, which stage text that is already there, or a typewriter effect.

items.name: motion-caret
items.intent: A caret that blinks only when idle and holds steady while `data-streaming="true"`, so the blink returning signals the stream has finished.
items.whenToUse: The cursor at the end of streamed or typed text.
items.insteadOf: A caret that blinks while text is arriving, which sets two competing rhythms.

items.name: motion-reveal
items.intent: Fade plus a 0.75rem rise when `data-reveal` flips from "out" to "in". Out of view it rests hidden and nudged down; with motion off the content stays visible.
items.whenToUse: Through the Reveal and TextReveal components, which set `data-reveal` when the element scrolls into view. Use the class directly only on an element whose `data-reveal` you set yourself.
items.insteadOf: An IntersectionObserver plus hand-written opacity classes.

items.name: motion-draw
items.intent: Draws an SVG path on when an ancestor's `data-reveal` flips to "in". The path needs `pathLength="1"`. `--motion-draw-duration` and `--motion-draw-delay` (both scaled by --motion-scale) set its pace and stagger.
items.whenToUse: Line art and schematics inside a Reveal. Stagger sibling paths with `--motion-draw-delay`.
items.insteadOf: A hand-written dash-offset animation with literal timing, which keeps animating, or keeps its delay, under reduced motion.

items.name: hit-target
items.intent: Grows an element's tap target to 44px with a transparent `::after`, without moving its layout by a pixel. `--hit-target-size` overrides the size.
items.whenToUse: A deliberately small mark — a tag's remove ×, a tiny disclosure, a toast close — that must still meet the WCAG touch floor. Shrink it (`[--hit-target-size:32px]`) where targets sit side by side, or the later one steals the taps.
items.insteadOf: Padding the glyph up (moves it off the row's grid and pushes siblings) or a bigger icon. Never on an `<input>` or other replaced element — pseudo-elements silently do nothing there; wrap it in a label.

items.name: reveal-on-hover
items.intent: Hides a row or tile action until its item is hovered or holds focus — on hover-capable devices only. Touch and no-hover devices always show it, and it fades with opacity, so it never leaves the tab order or the accessibility tree. The item is the nearest ancestor with `group` (or `data-reveal-scope`); an open popup keeps its trigger visible. `--reveal-offset` adds a short rise.
items.whenToUse: Secondary per-item actions in a dense list or grid — a tile's play button, a row's overflow menu or visibility toggle — where showing every action at rest would turn the list into a wall of controls. Put `group` on the item (the row, the tile), not on the list, and the class on the action or its wrapper.
items.insteadOf: `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` (hidden forever on a phone), `hidden group-hover:flex` (drops it from the tab order and the accessibility tree), or a hand-written `[@media(hover:hover)]:opacity-0` pair (snaps, and misses focus and open menus). Not for a primary action — that stays visible.
items.example: • Track

items.name: stretched-link
items.intent: Makes one link cover its whole item with a transparent `::after`, so a tile or card is clickable everywhere while its other links and buttons stay separate controls. Focus draws the ring on the overlay, rounded by `--stretched-link-radius`.
items.whenToUse: A card, tile or row that IS a link but also holds a second control — a subtitle link to the artist, a play button, a menu. Put it on the primary link (usually the title), `relative` on the item, and `relative z-10` on every other control.
items.insteadOf: Wrapping the item in an `<a>` or `Card render={<a />}` — invalid as soon as it nests another link or button, which browsers re-parent and screen readers read as one long link. Not with `hit-target` on the same element (both own `::after`).
items.example: Low tideJuno Avery

items.name: link-underline
items.intent: An underline drawn from the font's own metrics (position and thickness `from-font`) with ink skipping descenders, so it retunes when a theme swaps typeface. Also carries the link's focus-visible outline in `--ring`, so a plain `<a>` meets the focus floor without app CSS.
items.whenToUse: Every plain text link — inline in running text or standalone ("Forgot password?"). Pair with `motion-interactive` for a colour change on hover.
items.insteadOf: `underline underline-offset-4 decoration-2` — tuned to one face and wrong for the next theme's. Animating thickness or offset is not supported; a growing underline is a separate pseudo-element.

items.name: checkerboard
items.intent: The transparency checkerboard, painted from `--panel` and a derived darker step so it reads in both modes. `--checkerboard-size` (default 16px) and `--checkerboard-alt` tune it.
items.whenToUse: Behind anything that can be translucent: a colour swatch with alpha, an image or artboard preview, an alpha slider track.
items.insteadOf: A hand-rolled `repeating-conic-gradient` with two hardcoded greys. Deliberately not named `bg-checkerboard`, so `cn()` never merges it away against a real `bg-*` colour — you can layer a colour over it.

items.name: texture-dither
items.intent: A faint pixel / halftone dither field that dissolves: a small pseudo-random tile of squares painted in `--border-strong` and faded out by a gradient mask. Static, pure CSS, follows every theme and mode. Hooks: `--dither-fade` (direction, any linear-gradient side or angle, default `to bottom`), `--dither-size` (tile, default 48px = 2px squares) and `--dither-color` (default `var(--border-strong)`).
items.whenToUse: Decoration at the top of a content area, a panel or a card, or behind an empty-state heading. Put it on its own `aria-hidden` element, `absolute -z-10` as the first child of a `relative isolate` parent, so the content after it paints on top with no z-index of its own. It sets `pointer-events: none` and no position, so it never takes layout or catches clicks.
items.insteadOf: A hand-written `radial-gradient` dot grid (reads as graph paper, not dither), a PNG noise texture, a canvas, or hardcoded greys. Deliberately not named `bg-dither`, so `cn()` never merges it away against a real `bg-*` colour class.

propSurface.about: Every prop each exported component accepts, read from its TypeScript type — including what it forwards to its Base UI root, which the component's own props table does not restate. React's DOM attributes are omitted. `sable grade` judges props against this. Generated from src/index.ts — do not hand-edit.

providers.about: App-level context providers: what each one does, whether an app needs it, where it goes, its props and a copyable example. App-wide providers are documented in src/providers/providers.meta.ts; a provider owned by one component (`partOf`) is documented in that component's meta and summarised here. Generated — do not hand-edit.

items.name: CodeHighlightProvider
items.summary: Supplies one highlighter to every CodeBlock beneath it, so an app wires highlighting once. Map the highlighter's token colors to Sable tone tokens so code follows the theme.

examples.label: With a highlighter for the whole app
examples.code: <CodeHighlightProvider highlight={(code) => <span dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: highlightToHtml(code) }} />}><CodeBlock code={"const a = 1"} /></CodeHighlightProvider>

items.name: DensityProvider
items.summary: The bare React context behind density. It feeds only the React side, which is the half that reaches portaled popups; it renders no element and sets no `data-density`, so the CSS control ladder in its subtree does not change.
items.required: Optional, and rarely the right choice. To make a region compact use the Density component (or Workspace), which sets both the context and `data-density`.
items.placement: Around an element you already own that carries `data-density` itself.

props.name: value
props.description: The density popups opened from this subtree should use.

examples.label: An element that sets data-density itself
examples.imports:
import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { DensityProvider } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: IconProvider
items.summary: Supplies the icon set every <Icon> renders with, including the icons inside Sable's own components. Components name icons semantically (`chevron-down`, `check`); the set maps each name to artwork.
items.required: Required for icons. `<Icon>` has no built-in fallback: without a provider, icons render nothing and a development build warns once.
items.placement: Once, at the app root, above every Sable component.

props.name: set
props.description: The icon set: `reiconIconSet` from `@sableui/react/icons/reicon`, another complete set, or `composeIconSets(appExtras, reiconIconSet)` to add app icons over Reicon.

props.name: defaultVariant
props.description: Variant used when an <Icon> does not set one.

notes: The first set in composeIconSets that returns a node for a name wins, so app icons can also override Reicon's.
List the names an app adds in .sable/icons.json ({ "names": [...] }) so `sable grade` does not report them as off-contract.

examples.label: Reicon, Sable's bundled set
examples.imports:
import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { reiconIconSet } from "@sableui/react/icons/reicon"
import { IconProvider } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: App icons added over Reicon
examples.imports:
import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { reiconIconSet } from "@sableui/react/icons/reicon"
import { appIcons } from "./icons"
import { composeIconSets, IconProvider } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: MotionProvider
items.summary: Holds the app's motion policy and writes it as `data-motion` on <html>, which drives the `--motion-scale` and `--motion-expressive` switches every Sable motion recipe reads. Lets an app offer its own motion setting: full, subtle (feedback without flourishes) or off.
items.required: Optional. Without it, motion follows the visitor's OS `prefers-reduced-motion` setting, and useMotion() still works (its setPolicy does nothing).
items.placement: Once, at the app root, when the app has an in-app motion setting.

props.name: defaultPolicy
props.description: Initial policy when uncontrolled. "system" defers to the OS preference. "subtle" keeps essential motion (feedback, overlays, disclosure, loaders) and drops expressive motion (glides, rolling numbers, drawn ticks, shakes, staggers, overshoot).

props.name: policy
props.description: Controlled policy. Pair with onPolicyChange.

props.name: onPolicyChange
props.description: Called whenever the policy changes.

props.name: target
props.description: Where to write `data-motion`. The default covers portaled overlays too; a getter scopes motion to a subtree.

notes: JavaScript motion must read useMotion().enabled and do nothing when it is false; JavaScript flourishes read useMotion().expressive, which is also false under "subtle". CSS recipes follow on their own.
Mapping the app's "full" choice back to "system" keeps honouring the OS reduce-motion preference; "full" itself forces motion on.

examples.label: At the app root
examples.imports:
import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { MotionProvider } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: A reduce-motion setting
A three-way motion setting

items.name: MotionScope
items.summary: Turns motion down for one region — a dense data view, an embedded widget, a screen a test captures — by writing `data-motion` on a box-less wrapper and passing the same level to useMotion() below it.
items.required: Optional. Reach for it when a whole region should be calmer than the app; for one component, use that component's `motion` prop.
items.placement: Around the region. It renders a `display: contents` element, so it adds no box to the layout.

props.name: level
props.description: "subtle" keeps feedback, overlays, disclosure and loaders and drops glides, rolling numbers, drawn ticks, shakes and staggers. "off" stills everything. A scope can only turn motion down.

notes: Overlays portal out of the DOM subtree, so their CSS follows the app-level policy; set it on MotionProvider to cover them too.

examples.label: A calm data view
examples.imports:
import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { MotionScope } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: PresentationProvider
items.summary: Declares what its subtree is presented in, a page or a sheet. Action rows (CardFooter actions, SheetFooter) read it: on a page they are a short row; in a sheet they stack full width and pin to the bottom.
items.required: Optional. A bottom Sheet and IosSheet already provide "sheet", and Dialog, Popover and side Sheets provide "page". Mount it only for a container of your own that presents content like a sheet.
items.placement: Around the content of a custom sheet-like surface.

props.name: value
props.description: What the subtree is presented in.

examples.label: A custom bottom drawer
examples.imports:
import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { PresentationProvider } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: SableThemeProvider
items.summary: Applies and persists Sable's two theme axes on <html>: the colour preference (light, dark or system, written as the `.dark` class) and the design theme (written as `data-sable-theme`). Read and change both anywhere below it with useSableTheme().
items.required: Optional. Without it the app renders the default Sable theme in whatever mode the `dark` class on <html> says. Mount it when users can switch colour mode or theme, or to register an app-owned preset theme.
items.placement: Once, at the app root, above everything that renders Sable components or calls useSableTheme(). It writes to <html> by default so portaled overlays (dialogs, menus, toasts) share the same tokens.

props.name: defaultPreference
props.description: Colour preference on a first visit, before anything is stored. Pass "dark" (or a preset's `defaultMode`) to open in dark.

props.name: preference
props.description: Controlled colour preference. Pair with onPreferenceChange.

props.name: onPreferenceChange
props.description: Called whenever the colour preference is set.

props.name: defaultThemeId
props.description: Design theme on a first visit, before anything is stored.

props.name: themeId
props.description: Controlled design theme id. Pair with onThemeIdChange.

props.name: onThemeIdChange
props.description: Called whenever the design theme is set.

props.name: colorStorageKey
props.description: localStorage key for the colour preference. null disables persistence.

props.name: themeStorageKey
props.description: localStorage key for the design theme. null disables persistence. The default key is shared by every Sable app on an origin (several apps on localhost:5173 in development), and a stored id another app set wins over `defaultThemeId` when this app knows it too. An app with one fixed preset passes `themeId` (or `themeStorageKey={null}`); an app that lets users switch themes passes its own key.

props.name: target
props.description: Where to write `.dark` and `data-sable-theme`. A getter scopes theming to a subtree.

props.name: customThemes
props.description: Extra theme manifests, for example `presetManifest(preset)` for an app-owned preset. Their ids become valid themeId values. Sable does not load their CSS: import it yourself.

notes: Only the alternate design themes need theme CSS: import `@sableui/react/themes.css`, one `@sableui/react/theme/<id>.css`, or the scoped CSS from `sable preset --css`. Light/dark of the default theme needs nothing extra.
A colour-mode toggle is the ThemeSwitcher component; it reads this provider.

examples.label: At the app root, following the visitor's OS
examples.imports:
import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { SableThemeProvider } from "@sableui/react"

examples.label: Dark by default, with an app-owned preset theme
examples.imports:
import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { parsePreset, presetManifest } from "@sableui/react/presets"
import presetJson from "../.sable/presets/my-preset.json"
import { defaultThemeId, SableThemeProvider } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: ToastProvider
items.summary: Wraps Base UI Toast.Provider and renders the themed Viewport + toast list. Mount once near the app root, above any caller of useToast().
items.signature: { children, timeout?, limit?, closeIcon?, position?, stacked?, viewportClassName? }

examples.label: Stacked
examples.code: <ToastProvider stacked position="bottom-right">{children}</ToastProvider>

examples.label: Provider with app chrome
examples.code: <ToastProvider position="bottom-right" limit={3}><AppShell><Region max="feed"><Button onClick={() => toast.success("Saved")}>Save</Button></Region></AppShell></ToastProvider>
examples.imports: import { AppShell, Button, Region, toast, ToastProvider } from "@sableui/react"

items.name: TooltipProvider
items.summary: Wraps an app or group of Tooltips to share open/close delays. Once one tooltip is open, adjacent tooltips open instantly.
items.signature: Base UI Tooltip.Provider props (delay, closeDelay, timeout)

examples.label: Basic
examples.code: <TooltipProvider><Tooltip><TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Info"><Icon name="info" /></Button>} /><TooltipContent>Saved to your workspace.</TooltipContent></Tooltip></TooltipProvider>
examples.imports: import { Button, Icon, Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider, TooltipTrigger } from "@sableui/react"
